Inclusion not met: I4 (although a healthy control group exists, results for the healthy group are not reported separately as a group-level whole-brain map) and I5 (no whole-brain healthy-group task effect is presented; reported whole-brain maps are for all subjects combined and between-group contrasts). Exclusion criteria met: E4 (the reported results rely on combined-subject maps and between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group activation map). Full text was sufficiently represented in the provided NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study investigates social-related processing (empathy for pain; manipulation of social context and perceived agency), uses fMRI, and reports results from healthy adult participants (n=26; mean age 24.4). Importantly, the paper includes multiple group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., Pain>no pain; pain x social context interaction) with whole-brain inference and voxelwise FDR thresholding, and reports peak coordinates/tables. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply.

The study uses task-based fMRI of social cognition (false-belief/Theory-of-Mind cartoons) in healthy adult participants (n=13, ages 22–38), satisfying I3 and I4. However, all reported group-level analyses are described as region-of-interest (model fit over: region of interest; inference restricted to: region of interest) and a MARSBAR ROI analysis is noted; no unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise group-level task activation map is reported. Therefore the paper does not meet I5 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion E2 (ROI-only results). Reported coordinate peaks appear to come from ROI analyses. Full text is available in the record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study reports task-based fMRI in a social-cognition/legal decision-making paradigm (reading crime vignettes with responsibility/punishment ratings), with healthy adult participants (n=20, ages 18–45). Multiple group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts are reported (e.g., strong disgust > weak disgust; trait > biological), with inference performed over the whole brain and results reported as peak coordinates in tables. Reporting and thresholding (FDR) are appropriate and clearly describe healthy-group task effects. Therefore all inclusion criteria for task relevance, sample, and whole-brain reporting are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The paper reports an fMRI perceptual judgment of self vs non-self body-odour peptides in healthy adults (meets I3 and I4). However, NeuroStore indicates inference was restricted to a region-of-interest despite the model being fit over the whole brain. No unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map is reported; results are ROI-restricted. Therefore the study fails I5 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). No other exclusion criteria appear to apply.

The study used task-based fMRI of observation and motor imagery of face and limb movements, which pertains to social-related processing (gesture/face movements relevant to social communication). Participants are healthy adults (mean age 25.18, sd 4.25), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports multiple group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (model fit over whole brain; inference over whole brain; voxelwise FWE-corrected results) such as within-group contrasts (e.g., limb > face, observation vs imagery), with coordinates/peaks reported. Thus all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply.

The paper reports fMRI during a social-related False Belief Task (I3) and includes a healthy adult control group (I4). However, NeuroStore extracts show only between-group interaction contrasts (e.g., healthy > ASD, ASD > healthy) and ROI-restricted within-patient analyses; there is no unmasked, whole-brain, group-level healthy-control task activation map reported in the extracted analyses. Therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts reported without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect).

The study reports task-evoked fMRI (BOLD) during a social task (minimal group membership and emotional face processing), satisfying I3. Participants are healthy adults (n=20, mean age 23.4), satisfying I4. The NeuroStore record indicates model fit and inference were conducted over the whole brain with cluster-level FWE correction and reported peak coordinates/tables, satisfying I5; coordinate/peak reporting also satisfies I6. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not limited to ROIs, are not connectivity- or resting-state-only, do not report only between-group contrasts, and participants are within the 18–65 range. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusions are triggered.

The study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses fMRI during a clearly social task (Social Evaluative Feedback Task) involving self/other trait feedback (I3). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=55, mean ages within 18–65) (I4). The paper reports multiple group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps (e.g., MAIN EFFECT: FEEDBACK ONSET: SELF > OTHER; whole-brain inference, FWE-corrected, reported peaks and tables) satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5). Results are reported with coordinates and tables (Tables t3/t4), meeting I6. No exclusion criteria apply: analyses include whole-brain activation maps (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only), healthy adult group reported, and this is empirical fMRI data. Therefore INCLUDE.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. It used task-based fMRI of social perception (dynamic vs static facial expressions), includes a healthy adult control group (n=13, mean age 24.3) reported separately, and provides a whole-brain, group-level within-group contrast for the healthy controls (Analysis 22889284_analysis_0: whole-brain inference for dynamic>static, cluster-corrected). The article is empirical and not ROI-only or connectivity-only; no exclusion criteria are met.

The study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. I3: Task is social-related (live mutual eye-gaze social cognition task). I4: Sample comprises healthy adults (n=30, mean age 21.8, within 18–65). I5: The paper reports a group-level, whole-brain, task-evoked statistical map (LIVE > REPLAY contrast; random-effects paired t-test; model fit and inference performed over the whole brain; peaks reported in Table t2). I6: Whole-brain results are reported as coordinate peaks/tables. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. fulltext_incomplete set to false.

This fMRI study tests social communication (gesture-speech integration) in healthy adults (meets I3 and I4). However, all reported inferences were restricted to a priori regions of interest using small-volume correction (SVC; voxel-level p<0.01). Although the model was fit over the whole brain, the NeuroStore record shows no unmasked, whole-brain group-level task-activation maps or whole-brain voxelwise inference; only ROI-restricted peaks are reported. Therefore the paper reports only ROI-based inference and does not provide the required whole-brain task-evoked statistical map (I5 not met). This meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only reporting). Consequently the study must be excluded.

Exclusion met: E4 - the NeuroStore record reports only between-group contrasts (ALS > healthy; healthy > ALS) with reported peak coordinates and no unmasked, whole-brain task activation map reported specifically for the healthy/control group. Inclusion met: I3 (task is social-related: FEEST emotional facial expressions) and I4 (sample includes healthy adult participants; mean age ~54 indicates adults within 18–65). Inclusion not met: I5 (no group-level whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked statistical map is reported). The analyses are whole-brain but restricted to between-group contrasts; therefore the paper fails the requirement for an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect and must be excluded.

This study is excluded because it fails to meet the review inclusion criteria. Exclusion IDs met: E2 (analysis is ROI-limited: model fit and inference restricted to DMN_RSN mask), E3 (resting-state ICA connectivity analysis only; no task-evoked fMRI results), E4 (reported contrast is a between-group contrast TD > ASD with no accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect), and E5 (sample is predominantly children/adolescents; reported ages mean 11.0, range 5.9–35.6 with no separate healthy adult (18–65) group reported). Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (no social-related task fMRI — rest task), I4 (no healthy adult group reported separately), I5 (no whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked map from healthy adults). Fulltext is complete for screening. Therefore EXCLUDED.

This randomized, double-blind, within-subject fMRI study (n=40 healthy adult males, mean age 25.8) used an interpersonal touch social task and reports multiple group-level, within-subject whole-brain voxelwise contrasts and correlations (e.g., female>male under placebo; OXT>PLC for female touch; several AQ correlations) with whole-brain inference. Thus it meets I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (reports whole-brain group-level task-evoked contrasts), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, age within range, empirical). Full text is available via the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study reports task-evoked fMRI during a clearly social task (group vs individual problem solving), includes a healthy adult sample (n=23; mean age 25 within 18–65), and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM results with voxelwise inference (FDR p<0.05, cluster extent) and tables of peak coordinates. These meet inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not only connectivity/resting-state; not only between-group contrasts; participants are within age range; empirical fMRI data reported). Full text is available in the provided NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

The study reports task-based fMRI of emotional speech prosody (social communication), meeting the review’s domain. Participants are healthy adults (n=22; mean age 24.8, range within 18–65), so sample criterion is met. The NeuroStore extraction shows a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrast (emotional: angry, surprised > neutral) with model fit and inference over the whole brain and reported peak coordinates (Table 1), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Reporting via cluster-corrected inference and table peaks is acceptable. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This fMRI study examines attentional orienting using gaze (a social cue) and arrow cues, addressing social-related processing (perception/understanding of others). Participants are healthy adults (n=22; mean age 22.95, within 18–65). The NeuroStore record shows model fitting over the whole brain and reports an exploratory whole-brain within-group analysis (Inference over: whole brain; reported peaks in Table tab3), satisfying the requirement for at least one group-level, whole-brain task-evoked map from the healthy group. Results are reported in tables/peaks. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and participants are within the age range). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria and should be included.

All inclusion criteria are met: (I3) the task is social (interpersonal space, social cognition) measured with task-based fMRI; (I4) sample comprises healthy adults age 18–30 reported separately (n=19); (I5) group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results are reported (model fit and inference over whole brain; within-group contrasts such as friend>stranger and treatment×protagonist interaction are presented with reported peaks); (I6) whole-brain results are reported as coordinate tables. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not outside age range, empirical fMRI data present). Therefore include.

This study reports task-evoked whole-brain fMRI results from a sample of patients with opioid use disorder (n=47) performing a baby-schema face-processing task. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses an fMRI social-related task). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no healthy adult group reported; all participants are patients), I5 (although whole-brain results are reported, they are from the clinical/patient group rather than a healthy/control group). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) strictly apply (analyses are whole-brain, not ROI-only or resting-state, and participants are within the 18–65 age range), so exclusion is due to failure to meet required inclusion criteria for healthy-group data. Full text appears complete in the record.

The study uses task-based fMRI probing self-judgments (perception/understanding of self), which is a social-related construct (satisfies I3). The sample is a healthy adult participant group (n=24; sexes reported) with observational cohort assignment (satisfies I4). The paper reports multiple group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts and maps (model fit/inference over whole brain, voxelwise thresholds, and reported peaks/tables in MNI coordinates), meeting the requirement for whole-brain evidence (satisfies I5 and I6). No indication that results are ROI-only, connectivity-only, or restricted to non-healthy or out-of-range ages. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The NeuroStore record reports healthy adult control group analyses (labeled CN) with within-group contrasts for social tasks (e.g., People > Bumper, Social Identity tasks). The model was fit over the whole brain and group-level maps are reported (peaks/tables indicated), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked maps for the healthy/control group. Participants in the control group are adults (ages reported within 18–65). Tasks are clearly social-related (social attribution, social identity, physical identity). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, empirical fMRI data present).

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (n=18, mean age 40.4) performing dyadic joint-action tasks (leading, following, mutual, solo) — a clear social processing paradigm (I3). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (model fit over whole brain; multiple contrasts with whole-brain inference and tables of reported peaks), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement (I5 and I6). The sample meets the healthy adult age criterion (I4). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state, and include within-group whole-brain task contrasts rather than only between-group comparisons, and the paper is empirical. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This fMRI study used an action observation/execution task relevant to social processing (perception/understanding of others). Participants were healthy adults (n=21, mean age 24) within 18–65. The NeuroStore record shows group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task contrasts (untrained > trained) reported for Session 1 and Session 2 (whole-brain inference, p<0.001 uncorrected) and coordinate tables; ROI analyses are also reported but whole-brain results are present. Results are reported as coordinates/tables consistent with inclusion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are satisfied and the study should be included.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of social learning about other people (social vs non-social conditions), using BOLD fMRI during a social-related task (meets I3). Participants are healthy adults (n=26, ages 19–37) satisfying the sample criterion (I4). The paper reports multiple group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts and parametric modulation results with whole-brain inference and reported peak coordinates/tables (e.g., Gifter SPE > Lottery SPE; main effects), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5,I6). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, and empirical data present).

This study uses task-based fMRI during a social interaction (multiround Trust Game probing mentalizing), meeting I3. It includes a healthy adult control group (n=26, mean age 28) reported separately, meeting I4. The NeuroStore record states the model was fit over the whole brain and reports within-group CONTROL contrast (HUMAN > COMPUTER) with reported peak coordinates (Table t2), fulfilling I5 and acceptable reporting per I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and healthy-group whole-brain task maps are reported). Full text is available as a NeuroStore-derived record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study uses task-based fMRI of biological motion perception, a social-perception construct (I3). It reports a healthy adult control group (n=15; age mean 25.7) separately (I4). It includes a whole-brain, group-level within-control contrast (biological motion > scrambled motion) with voxelwise results and reported peak coordinates (I5). The reporting of peaks/tables satisfies acceptable reporting formats (I6). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and a healthy adult whole-brain task map is provided. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

The task is social-related (evaluative judgments tied to self-referential processing/theory of mind) satisfying I3. The study includes a healthy adult control group (n=7, mean age 26.4, within 18–65), satisfying I4. It reports whole-brain, group-level task activation for the healthy/control group (Analysis 19747929_analysis_3: evaluative judgment > semantic memory retrieval; model fit over whole brain; reported peaks in Table tbl3), satisfying I5. Results are reported as peaks in a table, acceptable under I6. No exclusion criteria apply: this is not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, includes within-group healthy whole-brain maps, and participants are within the age range. Full text appears available in this record.

The task is communicative speech production (social communication), fulfilling I3. Participants are 29 healthy adults aged 18–24, fulfilling I4. NeuroStore indicates group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with model fit and inference over the whole brain and reported peak coordinates/tables for within-group task contrasts, fulfilling I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and the study should be included.

Although the study used an fMRI face-processing task (socially relevant stimuli) and included a healthy adult control group (mean age ~31), the NeuroStore record only reports between-group contrasts (WS > DA; WS > CA) with inference restricted to a region-of-interest. There is no clearly reported group-level, whole-brain task activation map for the healthy/control group (no unmasked whole-brain healthy-group effect or within-group contrast provided). Thus it meets exclusion criteria E4 (reports only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect) and E2 (inference restricted to ROI; no whole-brain results reported). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (social-related fMRI task) and I4 (healthy adult sample present). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked map reported).

The study uses fMRI during a social-related task (emotional prosody) and includes a healthy adult control group, but it does not report any whole-brain, group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Whole-brain results present are between-group contrasts (blind > sighted); within-group healthy-group analyses are reported only as ROI-restricted results (amygdala). This violates exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Therefore the study must be excluded.

Meets all inclusion criteria for the review. The study used fMRI BOLD during a social interaction task (interactive rock-paper-scissors) addressing social cognition/mentalizing (I3). The sample is healthy adults (n=18, mean age 21.5) within 18–65 (I4). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise within-subject contrasts are reported (model fit over whole brain; inference over whole brain; FWE-corrected peaks reported in Table t1) satisfying whole-brain evidence (I5); coordinate table reporting is allowed (I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants in age range, empirical fMRI data reported).

The study uses fMRI during a moral judgment task (social-related processing), satisfying I3. The participants are healthy adults (age range 20–41, n=16), satisfying I4. The paper reports a within-group contrast 'Moral dilemmas > neutral dilemmas' with 25 reported peaks (Table 2), which constitutes a group-level, whole-brain task activation reported as coordinates and therefore satisfies I5 and I6. Although one interaction analysis used ROI SVC, the presence of the unmasked within-group Moral>Neutral contrast provides the required whole-brain evidence. No exclusion criteria are met. Minor inconsistencies in the sex counts in the extraction do not affect eligibility.

This study uses task-based fMRI of a social interaction paradigm (VISTTA) inducing social rejection (I3). The sample comprises 43 healthy young women (healthy adult participants reported; participants on oral contraceptives), satisfying the healthy adult sample requirement (I4). NeuroStore indicates voxelwise whole-brain model fitting and whole-brain inference with reported peak coordinates/tables for task contrasts (Rejection > Non-rejection and Non-rejection > Rejection), which constitutes group-level, whole-brain task-evoked results for the healthy group (I5). Reporting of peaks/tables also meets the allowance for coordinate table reporting (I6). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts without healthy-group whole-brain effects, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Note: ages are not numerically stated but participants are described as healthy young women; overall confidence is high but not maximal due to absence of explicit age range in the record.

The study reports fMRI during explicit and implicit emotional face processing, a social cognition task (emotion recognition) meeting I3. Participants are healthy adults (n=29, ages 20–35), satisfying I4. Group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses are reported (model fit over whole brain; inference over whole brain; FWE voxel-level thresholding) for within-group contrasts (EMO, AGE, EMO>AGE) with peak coordinates in tables, satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, age within 18–65, empirical fMRI data). Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED.

The study reports an fMRI experiment using a social interactive task (virtual handshake with acceptance/refusal), satisfying I3. A healthy control group is separately reported (n=16, mean age 27.4), satisfying I4. The analyses indicate model fit over the whole brain and report within-group healthy-control contrast (refusal > acceptance) with reported peak coordinates (Table 2), satisfying I5 and I6. There are no ROI-only, connectivity-only, age-exclusion, or non-empirical issues; no exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is eligible for the review.

The study reports task-based fMRI during an explicitly social task (impression formation) and a non-social sequencing task, satisfying social-related processing. Participants are healthy adults (n=15; ages 18.4–22.9), within the 18–65 range. NeuroStore extraction indicates whole-brain model fitting and whole-brain inference for within-group contrasts (e.g., impression formation > sequencing; diagnostic > nondiagnostic) with reported peak coordinates (tables), meeting the requirement for a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked map. Results are reported as coordinate tables. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, empirical fMRI data). Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study investigates social communication (facial emotion dynamics) in healthy adults (I3 and I4 met). However, all reported analyses were conducted with models fit over a region-of-interest and inference restricted to ROIs (small-volume FWE corrections); no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy group are reported. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only results). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (whole-brain evidence).

The study used task fMRI to probe social communication-related processing (vitality forms of speech and actions), meeting I3. It reports a healthy adult sample (n=18, 9F/9M), satisfying I4 (healthy adult group reported separately). Multiple group-level, whole-brain task contrasts with inference across the whole brain are reported (Analyses 0–3: Listening, Imagination, Observation, Action Imagination; whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference with FWE correction and reported peaks), satisfying I5. Reporting of whole-brain results in the NeuroStore extract is acceptable per I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, empirical fMRI in healthy adults).

The study reports task-based fMRI of voice/speaker recognition, a form of social communication/perception (I3). It includes healthy adult control groups (several analyses report controls: n=30, n=32, etc.) meeting the age range 18–65 (I4). The paper provides group-level, whole-brain task activation results for healthy/control participants (e.g., Vocal>non-vocal in controls, speaker>speech in controls) reported as peak coordinates/tables (I5, I6). The document also contains within-group healthy random-effects contrasts (not ROI-only) and task-evoked maps rather than only connectivity or ROI analyses, and does not violate exclusion criteria. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

The study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. I3: The task is social-cognition (group apology/forgiveness scenarios) collected during fMRI. I4: Sample consists of healthy adult participants (n=25; mean age 21.32). I5: The paper reports multiple group-level, within-subject whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., Costly Apology > Non-costly Apology, Costly Apology > No Apology, Non-costly Apology > No Apology) with model fit and inference performed over the whole brain and coordinates/peak tables reported. I6: Whole-brain results are reported as tables of peaks/coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within 18–65, empirical fMRI data present).

The study examines emotional face perception (a social task) and includes matched healthy control participants, so it meets I3 (social-related fMRI task) and I4 (healthy adult group present). However, the NeuroStore record only reports a between-group interaction/contrast (familial-risk patients > controls) with whole-brain inference; it does not report any unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group (no within-group or healthy-group main-effect whole-brain results are provided). Therefore it fails I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying healthy-group whole-brain task effect).

This study reports task-based fMRI of interpersonal emotion regulation (regulating another person’s emotions), which is a social-processing task (perception/understanding of others/empathy). The sample is healthy adults (n=20; mean age 23; range 18–30), satisfying the age and healthy-sample requirement. Multiple group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise contrasts are reported (flexible factorial group-level model; whole-brain model fit; voxelwise thresholds and tables of peak coordinates are provided for several within-group task contrasts), meeting the whole-brain evidence criterion. Results are presented as coordinate tables and described in the text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and participants are within 18–65). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met.

The study is an empirical fMRI experiment on perception of faces and voices (multisensory social perception), satisfying the social-related task requirement. Participants are healthy adults (n=20, ages 20–30). The NeuroStore record reports multiple group-level, whole-brain, within-group task-evoked contrasts (e.g., A>Fix, V>Fix, AV>Fix, AV>(A+V)) with whole-brain inference and tables of peak coordinates, fulfilling whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting formats. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, reports healthy-group whole-brain activation maps).

(a) Exclusion met: E4 — the NeuroStore record reports only between-group contrasts/interactions (ALS>HC, HC>ALS, interactions) and an ROI-restricted inference; there is no unmasked, whole-brain healthy-control group task activation map reported. (b) Inclusion met: I3 (fMRI during social-related tasks: action observation and action-understanding/Theory-of-Mind tasks) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group; ages reported with mean in 18–65 range). (c) Inclusion not met: I5 (no clearly reported whole-brain, group-level healthy/control task-evoked statistical map). Therefore the study must be excluded under E4.

The NeuroStore record shows this is an fMRI study of social-related processing (task labeled social cognition and games; participants viewed and rated meanings of LEGO models) in healthy adult participants (n=25, mean age 24). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, within-subject task contrasts (Meaning>Physical, Physical>Meaning, Own>Other) with whole-brain inference and reported peak coordinates (FDR thresholding), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps; coordinate tables are provided. An ROI small-volume correction was used only for one interaction, but whole-brain results are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, age outside range, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied.

The study reports an fMRI task involving social-affective communication (virtual agent imitating participants' facial expressions), meeting the social-related task requirement. Participants are healthy adults (n=39, mean age 21.49, within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (model fit and inference over whole brain), with coordinate peaks reported; thus whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked results are available. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be included in the review.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) Task involves social interaction (competitive real-time game vs human/computer opponents; opponent identity manipulation) and uses task-evoked fMRI; (I4) Sample are healthy adults (n=75; ages 18–48); (I5) Reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (model fit over whole brain, whole-brain inference, cluster-thresholding, and reported peak coordinates); (I6) Whole-brain results are reported as peaks/coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, age within range, and is empirical fMRI data). Therefore include for the meta-analysis of social processing in healthy adults.

This fMRI study used social tasks (face processing with social goals) and reports amygdala BOLD responses, so it meets I3 (functional MRI during a social-related task). However, all reported neuroimaging analyses were ROI-based (model fit over: region of interest; regions: amygdala complex) with no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task maps reported, so it fails I5 and meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only results). Participant information lists n=7 (4F,3M) but provides no ages, so I4 (healthy adults aged 18–65) cannot be confirmed from the document. Therefore the paper must be excluded because it does not provide the required whole-brain healthy-group activation evidence (I5) and reports ROI-only analyses (E2).

Exclusion E4: The paper reports whole-brain between-group contrasts and Group×Drug interactions (e.g., CON>IED, Group×Drug) but does not present an unmasked, whole-brain within-group task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group (i.e., no CON: faces>fixation whole-brain map is listed). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related face-processing task) and I4 (healthy adult control group is present). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clearly identified whole-brain, group-level healthy/control task activation map). Full text is sufficiently represented in the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The NeuroStore record documents an fMRI Theory-of-Mind task (Frith-Happé) (I3 met) but the extracted analyses and participant fields refer to patient (AN) within-group results. Although the abstract notes healthy controls were recruited, the study document does not report any group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. All listed voxelwise analyses are labelled for patients and/or report patient-related covariates. Therefore the study fails to meet I4 and I5. This falls under exclusion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts or patient-group maps without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Based on the provided record, I exclude the study.

The study reports task-based fMRI during a social-related task (Cyberball social exclusion) in healthy adult participants (n=21, ages 20–37). It provides whole-brain voxelwise analyses (model fit over: whole brain) including within-group one-sample t-tests for the placebo condition and paired t-tests comparing psilocybin vs placebo, with reported peak coordinates/tables. Thus it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI social processing, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps. No exclusion criteria are met. The NeuroStore record constitutes sufficient reporting of whole-brain task activation maps for the healthy group.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: I3 (uses fMRI during a social-related task: Cyberball social exclusion/empathy), I4 (healthy adult sample, n=16, ages 18–24), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts — Analysis 21122817_analysis_1: observed exclusion > inclusion with whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference; Analysis 21122817_analysis_2: whole-brain regression with trait empathy), and I6 (whole-brain results reported as peak coordinates/tables). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only (whole-brain contrasts are present), not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, ages fall within 18–65, and this is an empirical fMRI study. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the review.

This study reports task-based fMRI of social-related processing (subliminal/supraliminal facial-emotion empathy judgments), in healthy adult participants (n=12, mean age 23.8). NeuroStore extraction indicates group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM results (model fit over: whole brain) with multiple within-group contrasts (e.g., main effect of faces; supraliminal and subliminal effects; supraliminal > subliminal; subliminal > supraliminal) and reported peak tables. Whole-brain results are clearly reported (tables of coordinates). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps), and I6 (results reported in tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and this is empirical fMRI data).

Excluded because the paper does not report an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). (b) Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses fMRI during a social-related Theory-of-Mind task). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clearly identified whole-brain, group-level healthy/control task-evoked map reported); I4 (uncertain: healthy controls are aged 15–25, so the healthy group is not clearly restricted to adults 18–65 and healthy-group results are not reported separately as an adult-only subgroup). Therefore the study must be excluded.

The study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses fMRI during a social-related task (encoding facts about unfamiliar people) (I3); reports a healthy adult sample (n=12, ages 20–32) (I4); provides group-level, whole-brain within-group task contrasts with reported peak coordinates (Analysis 19620621_analysis_1: Person, inference over whole brain) satisfying whole-brain evidence (I5); and results are presented as coordinates/tables (I6). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only (whole-brain analyses reported), not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants fall within the 18–65 range, and the paper reports original empirical fMRI data. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

Meets all inclusion criteria: The study uses task fMRI examining person identity from faces/voices (social-related processing: perception/understanding of others) satisfying I3. Participants are healthy adults (n=11, ages 19–32) satisfying I4. The paper reports a group-level, whole-brain, within-group contrast (human voices > tool sounds) with model fit over the whole brain and reported peak coordinates/tables, satisfying I5 and the acceptable reporting condition I6. No exclusion criteria apply: this is not ROI-only, not resting-state/ connectivity-only, not a between-group-only report, and participants are within the 18–65 range. Therefore INCLUDE.

The study uses task fMRI of audiovisual speech integration (a social-communication relevant task), includes a healthy adult control group (age means within 18–65) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results for the control group (Analysis 19303257_analysis_2 with 15 reported peaks; model fit and inference performed over the whole brain with FDR correction). Thus it satisfies I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult participants with separate control-group results), I5 (whole-brain, group-level healthy-control task effects reported), and I6 (results provided as coordinates/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, age-outside-range-only, or non-empirical issues). Full text appears sufficiently represented in the provided record, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

The study reports an fMRI experiment using a social-perception task (decoding direction of observed head turns), meeting the review’s social-related task requirement. Sample includes healthy adults (n=17, ages 22–38), meeting age/sample criteria. Multiple group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (e.g., searchlight and contrast analyses with inference over whole-brain/group gray matter mask: analyses 4, 5, 6, 9, 11), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Results are reported at the group level and thresholded voxelwise (FWE). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, empirical data).

The study reports task-based fMRI of spontaneous imitation, a social-related process (imitation relates to social communication/perception of others). Participants are healthy adults (n=37, age 18–25), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (Analyses 26168793_analysis_0 and _1: second-level random-effects one-sample t-tests with whole-brain model fit and reported peaks/tables), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Results are reported in MNI coordinates and thresholding is described. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the review.

This study investigates emotional expression processing (facial emotion recognition), meeting I3 (social-related task). It also includes a healthy control group reported in between-group contrasts, satisfying I4 (presence of healthy adult participants). However, all reported statistical maps in the NeuroStore record are between-group contrasts (bvFTD > controls or controls > bvFTD) and no unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group (e.g., within-group or main effect in controls) is provided. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Note: one contrast used a small-volume correction, but that does not provide the required healthy-group whole-brain map. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (whole-brain healthy-group evidence) is not satisfied. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Exclusion criteria applied: E4.

The study investigates collaboration (social interaction) using fMRI hyperscanning with a task requiring collaborative drawing, which qualifies as social-related processing (I3). Participant sample are healthy adults (mean age 27.44, SD 4.98; 16 female, 20 male), meeting the age/sample criterion (I4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise within-group contrasts (Independent > Collaboration and Collaboration > Independent) with whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference (FWE, voxel-level), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement (I5). Results are reported as peak coordinates/tables, acceptable per I6. Although the paper also includes an ROI-based inter-subject synchronization analysis, whole-brain task activation maps are present and clearly reported, so no exclusion criteria are met.

The study reports task-based fMRI of social-relevant processing (self- vs. other-touch; perception/understanding of self and social touch), includes a healthy adult sample (n=27, mean age 23.4), and presents at least one group-level whole-brain, voxelwise contrast (other-touch > self-touch) with random-effects analysis and FWE correction. Although ROI-based PPI connectivity is also reported, the presence of an unmasked whole-brain task activation map satisfies the whole-brain evidence requirement. No exclusion criteria are met based on the provided record.

The study used task-based fMRI in a social cognition (joint attention) paradigm, with healthy adult participants (n=12, ages 20–31). NeuroStore indicates whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses and reports group-level contrasts (Places>Bodies and Bodies>Places) with peak coordinates (Table), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, group-level task-evoked maps. Results are clearly described for the healthy/control group. Therefore inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level results), and I6 (results reported as coordinate tables) are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study investigates perception of social auditory stimuli (single vs. two people walking), engaging social-processing brain areas—thus meeting the social-related task requirement. Participants are healthy adults (n=12, ages 22–37). The report includes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM contrasts (model fit over whole brain) with reported peak coordinates in Tables 1–2 for within-group task contrasts (e.g., STEP2 > STEP1; STEP1 > NOISE1), satisfying whole-brain evidence. Coordinate tables are provided, which is acceptable. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, includes within-group healthy adult effects). Full text is available from the NeuroStore record provided.

This study reports fMRI during a social-related evaluative task (valence judgments of speakers), fulfilling I3. The sample is healthy adults (n=14, mean age ~24.9), fulfilling I4. The paper includes multiple group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps (e.g., whole-brain second-level random-effects localizer contrasts for voice and face areas and whole-brain ANOVA contrasts; Analyses 0–7, 8, 10, 12, 14), satisfying I5. Reporting format meets I6. Although several reported contrasts are between-group interactions (NECT vs. SUDOKU), the presence of unmasked whole-brain group-level task maps (localizers and whole-brain inferences) means E4 does not apply. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

The study uses task-based fMRI to measure responses to images of politicians, addressing social-related processing (perception/understanding of others and social evaluation). Participants are healthy adults (n=18, ages 22–33), satisfying the sample criterion. The NeuroStore record reports group-level, whole-brain GLM analyses with voxelwise inference (model fit over whole brain; inference over whole brain; FWE-corrected thresholds; reported peak coordinates/tables), fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement; results are reported as coordinate peaks/tables as acceptable. No exclusion criteria apply: this is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not outside the age range, and it is an empirical fMRI study. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

The study reports task-based fMRI of social cognition in healthy adults (meets I3 and I4) but the reported fMRI results are region-of-interest (ROI) analyses with inference restricted to ROI (Analyses 0 and 1). No group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked fMRI map for the healthy group is reported; only structural (VBM) whole-brain results are present. Therefore it fails the whole-brain evidence requirement (I5) and meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only fMRI results).

Excluded because the reported analysis is a between-group interaction contrast (post-intervention patients > pre-intervention healthy) with no unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task activation map reported. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E4 (only between-group/interaction contrasts reported without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). (b) Inclusion criteria met: I4 (the paper includes healthy/control participants). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (task is Passive Auditory Stimulation — listening to music — not a social-related task), I5 (no clearly identified whole-brain, group-level healthy/control task-evoked statistical map is reported; the available analysis is an interaction). Therefore the study does not meet the review’s requirement for whole-brain healthy-group social-task activations and must be excluded.

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adults performing an emotion recognition/adaptation task (social processing: perception/understanding of others). The study reports task-based fMRI in a social-communication domain (laughter types), with healthy adult participants (n=18, mean age 26). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, empirical fMRI data present).

The study reports task-based fMRI of social processing (perception of fearful faces/gaze)—meets I3. It includes a separately reported healthy adult group (n=22; mean age 23.7) —meets I4. The paper provides group-level, whole-brain, within-group task contrasts for the healthy/control group (AVERTED>DIRECT) with whole-brain inference and tables of reported peaks —meets I5 and I6. Thresholding and reporting indicate an unmasked voxelwise healthy-group activation map was tested and reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/ connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants are within 18–65). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study reports task-based fMRI of social interaction/retaliation (a social-related task: interaction with provoking vs non-provoking opponents), satisfying I3. NeuroStore metadata states model fit and inference were performed over the whole brain and reports group-level, within-group contrasts and peak coordinates (multiple contrasts and parametric modulations), fulfilling I5 and I6. Results are not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and include unmasked healthy-group whole-brain task effects, so no exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are met.

The task involves observing another person’s effortful actions (action observation of grip-force), which corresponds to perception/understanding of others -> meets I3. Therefore the study does not meet I5 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion E2 (only ROI-based inference reported).

NeuroStore record indicates the reported whole-brain analyses are omnibus between-group contrasts (contrast: omnibus, between-group) and does not provide any group-level, whole-brain task activation maps clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The study meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during a social-related affective picture viewing task) and I4 (healthy adult sample reported), but does not meet I5 (no healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked map reported). The study reports an fMRI task involving spoken sentence comprehension framed as social communication (authors explicitly reference ‘social communication’ and speech comprehension), satisfying I3. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E2), not connectivity/resting-state only (E3), not only between-group contrasts (E4), and participants are within 18–65 (E5). The NeuroStore record provides the necessary group-level whole-brain task activation map information for the healthy group. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The NeuroStore record reports an fMRI social cognition task (I3 met) including patients and healthy participants, but the only reported whole-brain analysis is a Group x Stimulus omnibus between-group interaction. Therefore the study reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task activation map (E4). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (social fMRI task). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no clear separate healthy-group whole-brain results reported as required), I5 (no group-level, whole-brain healthy/control task map presented). The study uses an fMRI social task (Theory of Mind) so I3 is satisfied. No group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) healthy/control task-evoked maps or coordinates are reported in this document. Therefore the paper fails the requirement for a healthy-group whole-brain activation map and for separate healthy-group results. Exclusion criteria E2 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) is met. Inclusion criteria met: I3. Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (healthy adult group results reported separately), I5 (whole-brain evidence from healthy group), I6 (acceptable whole-brain reporting). Full text is available in this record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This fMRI study investigates empathy/perspective-taking (social cognitive processing) using an empathy-for-pain task, meeting the social-related task requirement. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, age within 18–65, and empirical fMRI data present).

The study uses fMRI during a social cognition task and reports a healthy adult group, but it does not present any unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group task activation (I5). Exclusion criteria E2 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) and E4 (only between-group contrasts/interactions without an unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect) apply.

This study reports task-based fMRI during a social Trust Game (social-related processing) in a healthy adult sample (age range 18–25, n reported as 24), satisfying the sample and task requirements. The study uses fMRI during a social cognition task (social reputation processing) satisfying I3. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without healthy-group effects, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. The study uses task-based fMRI of action observation to infer others' effort (social perception/understanding of others). Participants are healthy adults (n=31, age 19–30). The study uses fMRI during a social (False Belief/mentalizing) task (satisfies I3) and includes a healthy adult control group (satisfies I4). Therefore the paper does not meet I5 (whole-brain healthy-group task evidence) and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrast/interaction without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). fulltext_incomplete is false; decision excludes the study for lack of a reported healthy-group whole-brain task activation map.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E4 - the NeuroStore record reports only between-group interaction contrasts (controls > patients) and within-group results only for patients; no unmasked whole-brain, group-level task activation map is reported for the healthy/control group. Therefore the study cannot be included under the review requirement for healthy-group whole-brain task activation data.

Excluded because study reports resting-state connectivity analysis relating emotional intelligence across a mixed sample (patients and healthy) and does not provide a healthy-group, task-evoked whole-brain activation map. The study used task fMRI (naturalistic movie viewing of parent–infant interactions), which is a social/attachment-related paradigm (meets I3). This study reports task-based fMRI in a social perception context (impression formation, attractiveness/liking of faces varying by race/status), with a healthy adult sample (n=60 white males, mean age 23.8). The study reports task-based fMRI during a social interaction task (Prisoner’s Dilemma; Theory-of-Mind-related question), satisfying social-related processing (I3). The NeuroStore record shows fMRI during an interactive social hierarchy task (social cognition/games). The sample is healthy adults (n=24; ages reported within 19–43). The study employed task fMRI during a social-related n-back task using faces varying in trustworthiness (addresses social perception/understanding of others). The study uses fMRI during a social-related task (facial emotion processing), meeting I3. It includes a healthy adult group (NC; n=27, mean age 28.9, within 18–65), meeting I4. This fMRI study investigates facial emotion recognition (a social communication/perception task) in healthy adults, so it meets I3 and I4. Therefore it fails I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Result: EXCLUDED.

The study is excluded because it does not report any whole-brain, within-group task activation maps for the healthy/control group. It examines social processing (facial emotion) and thus meets I3. This fMRI study investigates cooperative and competitive social interactions (social cognition task) in healthy adult participants (n=12; ages 21–28). Excluded because although the study used fMRI during a social-related task (perception of affective gestures) satisfying I3 and included healthy adult participants reported separately satisfying I4, the NeuroStore record only reports between-group contrasts and interaction effects (e.g., Controls>ASD, ASD>Controls, Fearful-by-Dynamic interactions) and does not provide an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. This fMRI study investigates understanding of communicative intentions (a social-communication task), meeting I3. The sample is a healthy adult group (n=23, mean age 24), meeting I4. Results are reported as peak tables and figures (reported peaks, Table references), satisfying I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants in age range, empirical data present).

Exclusion criteria met: E4. Inclusion criteria met: I3. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clear whole-brain, unmasked healthy-group task activation map reported), I4 (although healthy controls are implied by between-group contrasts, the document does not clearly report a separate healthy adult group’s whole-brain task results). This study used fMRI during a social-related task (semantic judgments about people vs objects), included healthy adult participants (n=13, ages 18–27), and reports a group-level, whole-brain within-group contrast (Object > Person) with whole-brain inference and cluster correction. The study reports fMRI during a clearly social/prosocial task (decisions to contribute to family), satisfying I3. The sample comprises healthy adults (n=25, mean age 20.2), satisfying I4. The study employed fMRI to probe perception of emotional expressions in voice and music (a social-communication / perception-of-others task), meeting I3. Meets I3 (fMRI during a social task) and I4 (healthy adult sample, n=16, ages 18–29). The study reports task-based fMRI of dynamic emotion perception (a social-related task), with healthy adult participants (n=28, ages 23–46). The study used fMRI during a social-related task (interpreting animated vignettes as social interactions vs mechanical actions), meeting I3. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply.

The study reports task-based fMRI during an interactive joint attention task (a social cognition paradigm), includes at least one healthy adult group reported separately (neurotypical matched controls and an additional healthy group), and provides multiple whole-brain, group-level within-group contrasts for healthy participants (e.g., RJA>SA, IJA>SA, joint attention>solo attention) with whole-brain inference. Ages fall within 18–65. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only results, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an fMRI study of social versus nonsocial gesture processing in a cohort of healthy participants using a task that probes social communication. Whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level within-group contrasts and cross-subject regressions are reported (model fit and inference over whole brain; cluster-FWE-corrected results; coordinates/tables provided). These satisfy I3 (social-related fMRI task), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise results reported), and I6 (results presented as peak tables/coordinates). I4 is considered met because the reported cohort is healthy adults (mean age 21.41) with participant ages spanning 16.9–25.7; group-level healthy-subject results are reported for the cohort (the slight inclusion of a small number of participants <18 is noted and lowers certainty). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only, out-of-range-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text is complete for screening purposes. Confidence is reduced slightly due to minor age-range ambiguity.

The study reports task-based fMRI during a social decision-making (public goods game) paradigm addressing social tie formation (meets I3). The sample is healthy adults (n=25, mean age 22.6) (meets I4). Multiple group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (model fit over: whole brain for parametric and cross-subject regression analyses) with MNI coordinates and thresholding details (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, and not between-group-only. Full text appears available via NeuroStore extract.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it used task-based fMRI during a social-related task (animacy perception/social cognition) with healthy adult participants (n=15, mean age 26.6, within 18–65). The report includes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (model fit over whole brain; random-effects flexible factorial GLM) and reports peak coordinates/tables for parametric contrasts (increasing/decreasing animacy and movement patterns), satisfying the requirement that whole-brain results are clearly reported (tables of peaks). The analyses are within-group effects for the healthy sample, not ROI-only or connectivity-only, and not limited to between-group contrasts. Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED.

The study used fMRI during a social-related emotion (face matching) task (I3 satisfied). However, all reported statistical inferences are either between-group interaction contrasts or are restricted to a region-of-interest using small-volume correction (SVC). No unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group is reported. Therefore the paper violates exclusion criteria E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect) and E2 (results are reported only with ROI/SVC inference; no whole-brain results are presented). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (results for the healthy adult group are not reported separately as an unmasked whole-brain effect) and I5 (no whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked statistical map is provided). Full text appears complete for screening.

The study reports task-based fMRI during a social Trust Game (reciprocity), with a healthy adult sample (n=19, mean age 24.7). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and inference was conducted over the whole brain (AFNI 3dClustSim cluster-corrected; reported peak coordinates in tables). Multiple within-group contrasts (simple effects and contrasts) are reported for the healthy participant group. These facts satisfy inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adults), I5 (whole-brain group-level task maps), and I6 (results reported as coordinates/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, age within range, empirical fMRI data present). Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

Exclusion criteria met: E3 (study reports only seed-based/resting-state connectivity analyses without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map), E4 (reports only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect), and E5 (participants are adolescents; sample age range/means are below 18 so no healthy adult group 18–65). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (did not use an fMRI social-related task; task is resting fixation), I4 (no healthy adult participants 18–65; sample mean ~14.8, range 11.8–17.7), I5 (no reported whole-brain, task-evoked healthy-group statistical map). Therefore the study does not meet the meta-analysis requirements and should be excluded.

This study should be excluded because it reports only region-of-interest analyses and does not provide whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation maps. Evidence: NeuroStore extraction states 'Model fit over: region of interest' and 'Inference restricted to: region of interest' for all reported analyses, indicating ROI-only results with no whole-brain inference. Exclusion ID met: E2 (ROI-only without whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task — action observation/perception of others) and I4 (healthy adult sample, n=24, mean age 24). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain group-level task-evoked statistical map reported). Therefore the paper fails the whole-brain evidence requirement and must be excluded.

The study uses fMRI during a social task (facial emotion recognition) in a healthy adult sample (ages 19–31), satisfying I3 and I4. However, all reported statistical models were fit and inference was restricted to regions of interest (NeuroStore record: 'Model fit over: region of interest' and 'Inference restricted to: region of interest'), and no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation maps for the healthy group are reported. This fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Connectivity (gPPI) and task-ROI results are reported but are ROI-limited and do not fulfill the whole-brain requirement. Therefore the paper is excluded per E2/I5.

This fMRI study investigates social processing (mentalization during an interpersonal competitive game), satisfying the social-task requirement. The sample comprises healthy adults (n=19, ages within 18–65) reported separately. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (Analyses 20072709_analysis_0 and _1: model fit over and inference over whole brain; random-effects group GLM/2×2 ANOVA; FDR-thresholded results and reported peak tables), meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. ROI analysis is also reported (analysis_2) but does not preclude inclusion because whole-brain results are present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the review.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses task fMRI of social processing (facial emotion recognition) (I3); it reports a healthy adult group (n=17, mean age 23.06) separate from the high-genetic-risk group (I4); it reports group-level, whole-brain, within-group contrasts for the healthy/control group (e.g., Fear>base, Neutral>base, Happy>base fitted over the whole brain with reported peak coordinates and cluster correction) satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5); results are reported as tables of peaks/coordinates (I6). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper includes whole-brain healthy-group task maps (so not E2, E4), is not resting-state/connectivity-only (not E3), participants are within 18–65 (not E5), and it is empirical fMRI data (not E6). Full text appears available in the record. Hence INCLUDE.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses fMRI during a social-related task focused on attachment/affiliation (I3); reports a healthy adult sample (n=51, mean age 28.5) within 18–65 (I4); provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (one-sample t-tests for masked sad > neutral and masked happy > neutral) with inference over the whole brain (I5); and whole-brain results are reported in coordinate tables (I6). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only (E2), not connectivity/resting-state only (E3), not only between-group contrasts (E4), participants are within the age range (E5), and this is empirical fMRI research (not a review; E6).

Exclusion(s) met: E4. Inclusion(s) met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task—partner/stranger handholding during shocks), I4 (healthy adult participants reported). Inclusion(s) not met: I5 (no unmasked, group-level whole-brain task-evoked map from the healthy/control group that is not restricted to a narrow subgroup). Rationale: The NeuroStore record shows multiple ROI-based task contrasts and between-group interactions (OXT vs PLC) and seed-based connectivity analyses. The only whole-brain inference reported is a sex interaction focusing on female participants (a subgroup), which does not satisfy I5. Therefore the study lacks an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task activation map and is excluded under E4.

The study examines romantic caress anticipation, a social/affiliative task (Affiliation/Attachment). Participants are healthy adults (n=24; ages 19–34), satisfying the sample criterion. NeuroStore metadata indicate model fit and inference were performed over the whole brain and report group-level, voxelwise random-effects contrasts with reported peaks/coordinates and cluster-level inference (Monte Carlo/thresholding), meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. Although the paper also reports seed-based connectivity, it additionally reports task-evoked whole-brain maps, so exclusion criteria for ROI-only or connectivity-only studies do not apply. All inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met; no exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text is available via the provided record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Excluded because the document does not report any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map for healthy adults. The only extracted analysis with details (analysis 0) was fit and inference restricted to an a priori fusiform ROI (ROI-only). Analysis 1 has no extracted features in the record despite many reported peaks, so there is no clear whole-brain healthy-group task map in the provided data. The task is social (face perception) and healthy adults are included in the sample, so I3 and I4 are met; however I5 (whole-brain evidence) is not met. Therefore exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) applies. fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study reports seed-based functional connectivity analyses relating left lateral temporal cortex (LTC) connectivity and LTC response during a self-referential task, and resting-state connectivity correlated with delusional thinking. No group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation map for the healthy sample (e.g., SR > baseline or other task activation) is reported in the extracted document. Therefore it fails Inclusion Criterion I5 and meets Exclusion Criterion E3 (only seed-based/connectivity/resting analyses without a whole-brain task activation map). It does meet I3 (fMRI with a social-related self-referential task) and I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately). Full text appears complete for the extracted content (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study reports fMRI during a social-related Emotional Face Matching Task (faces with emotional expressions), includes a healthy adult sample (n=13, mean age 25.7), and presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (model fit over whole brain) with reported peak coordinates (tables) for within-group/placebo vs oxytocin contrasts. These fulfill inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without healthy-group map, age out of range, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study should be included.

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adults (ages 20–33) during prosody production with an interactive social-feedback condition, which is a social communication paradigm. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (model fit over whole brain; whole-brain inference; FWE cluster-level; peaks reported in tables). Therefore it meets the review objective and the inclusion criteria for social-related fMRI in healthy adults. No exclusion criteria are met.

The study uses an fMRI social-related task (Self-Referential Judgment Task) so I3 is met. However, the reported analysis is a cross-subject regression / between-group association (EB regressor) fit and inferred over the whole brain and does not present a clear, unmasked whole-brain task activation map specifically from a healthy/control group. The paper includes both patients (anorexia nervosa) and healthy participants but does not report healthy-group whole-brain results separately. Therefore it fails I4 and I5 and meets exclusion E4 (reports only between-group/cross-subject effects without an accompanying healthy-group whole-brain task effect). Full text appears available from the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study reports task-based fMRI during a social rhythmic interaction (social cognition/games) in healthy adults (n=17, mean age 22) satisfying sample criteria. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported: within-group contrasts (Copy > Random; Random > Copy) and a parametric modulation (subjective PCA) with reported peaks/coordinates and whole-brain inference (cluster-level FWE, threshold p<0.001). Results are presented as group-level whole-brain maps/peaks (Table tbl0005) in MNI space, meeting the requirement for whole-brain evidence. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, empirical fMRI data present). Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This study uses task-based fMRI of social appraisal (preference judgements of faces), includes a separate healthy adult group (n=21, mean age 39.8 within 18–65), and reports group-level, whole-brain, within-group task activation maps for the healthy/control participants (Analysis 20797730_analysis_7; reported peaks in Table). Whole-brain inference and coordinate/table reporting are present. Therefore it meets the review objective and the required whole-brain healthy-group evidence.

The study uses fMRI of a social task (approachability judgments) and includes a healthy adult group (I3 and I4 met). However, the paper does not report any whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group: the healthy within-group activation (approachability > gender) is reported with inference restricted to a region-of-interest (small-volume correction). Most other reported results are seed-based PPI connectivity or patient whole-brain/between-group contrasts. Therefore it fails I5 (no healthy whole-brain task map) and meets exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI results for the healthy group).

Study uses fMRI during a social decision-making task (social cognition/games) with healthy adult participants (mean age ~23.5). The NeuroStore record reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps: Analyses 1 and 3 are whole-brain, permutation-based FWE with TFCE, one-sample t-tests reporting multiple peak coordinates (Tables), clearly from the healthy participant group (n=44). Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply.

Study reports fMRI of a social task (Cyberball social exclusion) with parametric modulation of a Social predicted TD signal (Analysis 18537114_analysis_1) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise inference (inference over whole brain; FDR thresholding; reported peaks). Participants are healthy adults (n=18, mean age 42±12, age within 18–65). Whole-brain within-group task-evoked results are reported (tables of peaks). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, empirical healthy adult sample). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met.

The study uses fMRI during a social task (Cyberball) in healthy adult participants (n=42), but it does NOT report an unmasked, whole-brain task activation map for the healthy group. The only whole-brain task analyses presented are between-group genotype interactions (l/l > s/s) and seed-based PPI connectivity results; task effects are reported either as ROI analyses or as between-group interactions/connectivity. Therefore it violates inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Full text appears complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

All inclusion criteria are satisfied: the study uses task-based fMRI assessing trait empathy (a social-cognitive construct) during music listening (I3); participants are healthy adults aged 18–20 with sample sizes reported for two experiments (I4); analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise regression maps with inference performed over the whole brain and reported peak coordinate tables (I5,I6). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not exclusively connectivity or resting-state, not only between-group contrasts, ages are within 18–65, and this is an empirical fMRI study. NeuroStore extracts show model fit and inference over the whole brain for multiple cross-subject regression contrasts linking empathy measures to task activation, meeting the meta-analysis requirements for inclusion.

This study is excluded because it does not report an unambiguous whole-brain, within-healthy-group task activation map. The NeuroStore extract shows whole-brain analyses, but these are reported as between-group contrasts/interactions (patient vs control, interactions) and several ROI tests; no group-level, unmasked whole-brain task effect for the healthy/control group is identified. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E4. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses an fMRI Theory-of-Mind social task) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clearly identified whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked map). Therefore the paper does not meet all inclusion requirements for the meta-analysis.

The study uses fMRI during a social-related task (Emotional Face Matching) satisfying I3 and includes healthy adult participants reported in the paper satisfying I4. However, the NeuroStore record does not report any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) within-group task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group (I5 not met). The only whole-brain analyses shown are omnibus between-group contrasts (Analyses 1–2), and within-group results are either patient-only or ROI-restricted (Analyses 0,3,4). Therefore exclusion criterion E4 applies (reports only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). fulltext_incomplete=false.

This fMRI study used a social cognition task (participants imagined spheres as people in the social condition and made causality judgments), meeting I3. The sample is healthy adults (n=26, mean age 28.8), meeting I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, task-evoked contrasts (e.g., Analysis 23973351_analysis_3: conjunction (PC vs PD)∩(SC vs SD) with whole-brain model fit and reported peaks; other whole-brain contrasts SC>PC etc.), satisfying I5 (and I6 acceptable). Although connectivity (PPI) analyses are present, they are not the only results, so exclusion criteria E3 is not triggered. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective and should be INCLUDED.
