Excluded because the paper reports only between-group contrasts/interactions and does not present an unmasked, whole-brain task activation map for the healthy/control group. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E4: only between-group contrasts/interactions reported without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I4: sample includes healthy adult participants aged 19–28.6 reported separately. (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I3: task is overt speech repetition and, while related to vocal imitation, is not clearly a social-related task as defined (social-communication context not present); I5: no group-level whole-brain task-evoked map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group is reported (analyses are omnibus between-group interactions). I6 not satisfied because I5 fails. Full text is complete in this record.

The study uses fMRI during a social interaction task with healthy adult physicians (meets I3 and I4). However, the reported analyses are limited to region-of-interest (ROI) model fitting and inference (no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation maps are reported). Therefore it fails the whole-brain evidence requirement (I5) and meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only results).

This fMRI study examines gaze perception and prosocial decision making (a social-related task), meeting I3. Participants are healthy adults (n=27, mean age 24) meeting I4. The NeuroStore record reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts and interaction maps (model fit over whole brain; inference over whole brain for contrasts, FWE-corrected peaks reported), satisfying I5 and I6. The paper therefore provides whole-brain within-group healthy participant activation results. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, age within 18–65, and empirical fMRI data present).

The study reports task-based fMRI in an empathy-for-pain (social) paradigm in healthy adults (n=41, ages 18–37). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses are reported (model fit and inference over the whole brain) with coordinate peaks listed (tables) for contrasts such as AllPain>AllNoPain, PP>PPC, and EP>EPC. These satisfy the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps from the healthy group. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and the paper is empirical).

The study uses fMRI during a social task (Trust Game) in a healthy adult sample, but the reported neuroimaging analyses in the provided document are region-of-interest (subject-specific ToM masks) with inference restricted to those ROIs. No group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy group are reported in the record. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I5) and meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only results).

The study examines self-referential (social) processing using task fMRI and includes a healthy adult control group with separately reported within-group results; however, all reported task analyses were performed and inferred within predefined regions of interest (Model fit over: region of interest) rather than as whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level maps. Inclusion criteria I3 and I4 are met, but I5 (reporting at least one whole-brain, group-level task-evoked map for the healthy group) is not met. This violates exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only results). Therefore the study is excluded.

The study reports task-based fMRI during an empathy-for-pain (social) task (I3). The sample consists of healthy adults (mean age ~21; n=36) meeting the 18–65 requirement (I4). The paper reports a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrast (painful > non-painful) with model fit and inference over the whole brain (FDR-corrected voxelwise results and reported peak coordinates), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5). The reporting of peaks/coordinates also meets acceptable reporting formats (I6). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group whole-brain task effect, participants in age range, empirical fMRI data).

The study uses fMRI during a social perspective-taking task and includes a healthy adult control group (meets I3 and I4). However all reported analyses are region-of-interest (model fit and inference restricted to prefrontal ROIs) and no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps for the healthy/control group are reported. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only results with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain evidence) is not met. Excluding for E2 ensures the study does not contribute to whole-brain meta-analysis despite meeting I3 and I4.

The study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. I3: The task probes social processing (evaluation of personal attributes, self/others perspectives, framing effects), which is a social-related construct (perception/understanding of self and others). I4: Sample comprises healthy adults (n=19, ages 19–41) reported for the group. I5: The record explicitly reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (Model fit over: whole brain; Inference over: whole brain) and lists whole-brain contrasts (e.g., positive frame > negative frame) with reported peaks and cluster-level FWE correction. I6: Whole-brain results are clearly described in the extraction. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and it is empirical fMRI data). Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED.

The study reports event-related fMRI during a social joint Simon task manipulating belief about a human vs computer co-actor, probing social-cognitive processes (action co-representation, mentalizing). Participants are healthy adults (n=36, mean age 22.25). The analyses were fit over the whole brain and multiple within-group task contrasts are reported with peak coordinates in tables, satisfying whole-brain, group-level task-evoked results. Results are clearly from the healthy sample. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. It reports task-based fMRI during a social-related task (changes in political attitudes toward others after viewing campaign advertisements), satisfying I3. Participants are reported as healthy participants (I4). The analyses were fit over the whole brain (Model fit over: whole brain) and group-level random-effects contrasts are reported with peak coordinates in tables for multiple whole-brain contrasts, satisfying I5; reporting in tables of coordinates meets I6. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not limited to ROI-only analyses (E2), are not connectivity- or resting-state-only (E3), and are not only between-group contrasts without a healthy-group whole-brain task effect (E4). The document appears readable and complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Exclusion E4 met: only a between-group contrast (Low-depression > High-depression) is reported at the whole-brain level; no unmasked, whole-brain healthy/control-group task activation map or within-group healthy-group effect is reported. Inclusion I3 met: task is social (faces with emotional expressions, social learning). Inclusion I4 not met: although a low-depression group (BDI mean 1.36, age ~22) appears present, results for a healthy/control group are not reported separately as a within-group whole-brain map. Inclusion I5 not met: no whole-brain group-level healthy/control task map is provided. Therefore the study must be excluded under E4.

This fMRI study examines neural responses to infant cries and faces—socially relevant stimuli (attachment/affiliation, social communication). Participants are healthy adult women (n=17, ages 19–29), meeting the age and healthy-sample requirements. The paper reports multiple group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise within-group task contrasts (e.g., Low Distress Cry > Pink Noise, Happy Face > Neutral Face) with whole-brain inference and coordinate peaks, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Results are clearly from the healthy/control group. Therefore all inclusion criteria met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study uses fMRI during an empathy (social cognition) task and includes a healthy young adult group (I3 and I4 met). However, all reported statistical inferences were restricted to a region-of-interest using small-volume correction (inference restricted to ROI; voxel-level SVC) and the reported results are primarily between-group contrasts and regressions (YA vs OA, age correlations). The paper does not report an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map for the healthy adult group (no whole-brain voxelwise healthy-group task effect). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criteria E2 (ROI-only/no whole-brain results) and E4 (only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect).

This fMRI study used a social interaction task (reaction-time competition with opponents involving provocation and punishment choices), meeting the social-related processing requirement. Participants are healthy adults (n=15, mean age 22.9). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., high>low provocation; model fit over whole brain; coordinates reported in Talairach and peak tables), satisfying whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting formats. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

The study uses fMRI during a social cognition task (Reading the Mind in the Eyes Test), includes a healthy adult sample (n=16 females, mean age 20.8 within 18–65), and reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked contrasts (e.g., stimuli>rest, emotion>control, control>emotion) with whole-brain inference. These whole-brain results are clearly identified as within-group healthy-participant effects. Although the paper also reports seed-based PPI connectivity analyses, whole-brain task activation maps are present, so exclusion criteria for ROI-only or connectivity-only studies do not apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

The study reports an fMRI task that assesses mentalization/action identification (a social-cognitive construct), meeting I3. Sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=15; ages within 18–65) meeting I4. The NeuroStore record lists multiple group-level, whole-brain task contrasts with model fit and inference performed over the whole brain (e.g., Analyses 0,2,5,7,8,9,11), satisfying I5. Results are reported with cluster-level thresholding and peak coordinates (Talairach space), which is acceptable per I6. No exclusion criteria are triggered: the paper does not report only ROI analyses (E2), only connectivity/resting-state (E3), only between-group contrasts without an unmasked healthy-group effect (E4), nor does it involve an out-of-range age sample or appear to be non-empirical (E5,E6). Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports task-based fMRI BOLD in a social cognition task (False Belief judgments) in healthy adult participants (n=6, ages 25–39), and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (model fit over whole brain; within-group contrasts reported with MNI/Talairach coordinates and tables). This satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately), I5 (at least one group-level whole-brain task-evoked map), and I6 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within 18–65, empirical fMRI study).

The study reports task-based fMRI of social processing (spontaneous retrieval of affective person knowledge during face perception), satisfying I3. Participants are healthy adults (n=9, ages 18–32), satisfying I4. Analyses were whole-brain (model fit over whole brain) and report group-level, within-group voxelwise contrasts with peak coordinates/tables, satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E2), not connectivity- or resting-state-only (E3), not only between-group contrasts (E4), participants are within 18–65 (E5), and this is an empirical fMRI study (E6). Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This study reports task-based functional MRI in healthy adult samples (Studies include American and Korean participants, ages ~20), examining persuasion — a social-cognitive/mentalizing process (meets I3 and I4). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., persuasive > unpersuasive) with MNI coordinates and reported peak tables across multiple whole-brain analyses (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not limited to ROIs only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and include within-group whole-brain task effects. Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This fMRI study examines emotional prosody and lexico-semantic emotion (social communication/perception) using BOLD fMRI in healthy adults (n=26; mean age 21.2). The report indicates model fit over the whole brain and presents multiple group-level, within-group whole-brain analyses and random-effects second-level contrasts/parametric modulations with reported peak coordinates/tables (analyses 3–5, gender-specific within-group analyses). Results are reported as coordinate tables, satisfying acceptable reporting. Therefore the study meets I3 (social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps for the healthy group), and I6 (coordinates/tables acceptable). No exclusion criteria apply.

Included because the study meets all required inclusion criteria for this review: (I3) The task involves social-related processing—viewing a competitive sporting event with analyses explicitly linking activity in midline fronto-cingulo-parietal networks implicated in social cognition and self-relevant processing; (I4) Sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=20, mean age ~20.3, males only) within the 18–65 range; (I5) The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps (random-effects GLM one-sample t-tests for task contrasts, model fit over whole brain) with reported MNI coordinates; (I6) Whole-brain results are reported as coordinate tables (Tables t2/t3), which is acceptable. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Therefore include.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. I3: The task is a self-referential encoding task (perception/understanding of self), a social-related construct. I4: An adult healthy group is reported (n=12, ages 22.6–30.4). I5: The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps for the healthy adult group (analyses 6–11: one-sample t tests, whole-brain inference, reported peaks/Tables). I6: Whole-brain results are reported in tables of coordinates (Table t1) and described. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting/connectivity-only, includes adult within-range group, not non-empirical).

This study is excluded because it does not report any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps for the healthy adult group; all extracted analyses are ROI-based (model fit over region of interest: FFA, amygdala, STS, IPS). Exclusion criterion met: E2 (ROI-only results). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task: gaze perception/direct vs averted gaze) and I4 (healthy adult sample reported, n=16, mean age 25). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map reported). Full text appears complete for the purposes of screening (no access issues).

The study uses fMRI of a social (false-belief) task (I3 satisfied) and includes healthy adult participants; however, the NeuroStore record does not report any group-level, whole-brain task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Reported whole-brain maps are either for the combined sample (patients + controls) or for the patient group only, and the reported between-group contrasts (ASD > NT) are interactions/between-group effects. Therefore inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not met, triggering exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group/subgroup effects reported without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect).

This study reports task-based fMRI during a social decision-making task (Prisoner’s Dilemma), meeting the social-processing requirement. Participants are healthy adults (mean age 21.04, within 18–65), so the sample criterion is satisfied. NeuroStore-extracted analyses show whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference with group-level within-group contrasts and tables of reported peak coordinates (FWE cluster-level thresholding), fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement; coordinate tables are presented. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts, and participants are within the target age range. Minor inconsistencies in the reported N across fields do not change that a healthy adult whole-brain group analysis is reported. Thus include.

The study uses task-based fMRI of social cognition (meets I3) and includes healthy control participants, but the NeuroStore record does not report any group-level, whole-brain task activation map for the healthy/control group. The reported whole-brain maps are within-group maps for the ASD patients and between-group interaction/contrast maps (ASD vs TD). Thus the paper fails to provide an unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect (does not meet I4 and I5). This violates exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Therefore the study must be excluded.

This study reports fMRI during a social-related task (Cyberball social exclusion and Cybershape rule violation) in a healthy adult sample (n=23, mean age 24.15). Multiple group-level, whole-brain, within-group contrasts are reported (e.g., Social exclusion > Fair play) with whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference and reported peak coordinates and cluster-thresholding. Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, age outside range, or non-empirical) are met. The NeuroStore record functions as the fulltext surrogate per instructions and does not indicate incomplete access.

The study reports a False Belief (Theory-of-Mind) task—clearly social cognition—using fMRI in a large healthy adult sample (n=462; ages include 18+). It provides a group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise within-group contrast (Belief > Photo) with FWE voxel-level inference and reported peaks, clearly identified from the healthy/control group. These facts satisfy inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria apply.

The study used fMRI during a social trust task (trust games), satisfying I3. The sample comprises 45 healthy participants with ages ranging 13–49, thus including adults within the 18–65 range (I4). NeuroStore extraction shows whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference with reported coordinate peaks for group-level task contrasts (Cooperative, Unfair, Interaction), satisfying I5 and I6. Results are voxelwise whole-brain task activations reported for the healthy sample; no exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts, and participants include adults).

The study uses task fMRI with social stimuli (faces) and reports results for a healthy adult control group (I3 and I4 satisfied). However, all reported fMRI analyses are region-of-interest (amygdala) analyses with inference restricted and multiple-comparison correction applied within that ROI; no whole-brain, voxelwise healthy-group task activation map is reported. This fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only study with no whole-brain results). Therefore the study is excluded.

The paper reports fMRI of social stimuli in healthy adult participants (meets I3 and I4). However, all whole-brain inferences reported are between-group interaction contrasts (parents vs nonparents) or ROI-restricted small-volume corrected results. The record does not report any unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for a healthy/control group (e.g., a main effect or within-group contrast). Therefore this study reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect, meeting exclusion criterion E4. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain healthy-group task map reported).

The study reports task-based fMRI during a social decision-making task (Ultimatum Game) addressing fairness/intentionality, satisfying I3. The sample is healthy adults (n=23; ages 18–25), satisfying I4. The NeuroStore record shows group-level, within-group whole-brain voxelwise contrasts with coordinates reported (Analyses 4 and 5: model fit over whole brain, reported peaks/tables), satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This fMRI study examines moral comparison (a social-cognitive task) in healthy adult participants (n=18; ages 19–25), meeting the social processing domain and sample requirements. The NeuroStore record indicates group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task analyses (model fit and inference over whole brain) with FWE-corrected thresholds and tables of reported peak coordinates, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked results. Results are reported as within-group contrasts and conjunctions. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and it is empirical). Inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied.

The study examines social face/gaze processing (meets I3) and includes a healthy adult control group reported separately (meets I4). However, although the GLM was estimated over the whole brain, all reported inferences for the control within-group contrast were restricted to a region-of-interest and thresholded using small-volume correction. The paper therefore does not report an unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task activation map (I5 not met). This matches exclusion E2 (only ROI-based inference/no whole-brain results). Consequently the study must be excluded.

The study uses task-based fMRI to test persuasion by celebrity ‘expert power’, a social processing paradigm (social influence/understanding of others), satisfying I3. Participants are healthy adults (mean age 21.8), within 18–65, satisfying I4. The NeuroStore record indicates whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with inference over the whole brain and cluster-level FWE correction, and tables of reported peak coordinates for multiple within-group contrasts and main effects (e.g., experts > non-experts, hits > misses), satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and reports healthy-group whole-brain task effects).

The study investigates face processing (a social-related task) and includes a healthy neurotypical group, but it does not report an unmasked, whole-brain, within-group task activation map for the healthy/control group. NeuroStore entries show: (a) whole-group (n=28) faces>houses results and several between-group contrasts (NT>AS) for faces>houses, and (b) within-group contrasts reported for the AS group (and some analyses inference restricted to ROIs). There is no clearly identified whole-brain healthy-group task effect (unmasked within-group NT faces>houses) in the extracted analyses. Therefore exclusion criterion E4 applies (only between-group contrasts reported without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria I3 and I4 are met (social fMRI task; healthy adult group present). Inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain healthy-group map) is not met. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This fMRI study examines disgust perception in racial prejudice using a passive face-viewing task (social perception of others), with healthy adult participants (n=26, mean age 21.2). The NeuroStore record reports a group-level task contrast (Table I: brain activation of the racial prejudice in disgust perception) with reported peak coordinates, which constitutes whole-brain task-evoked results for the healthy group. Although the connectivity analyses (gPPI) are also reported, the presence of Table I satisfies the requirement for a voxelwise whole-brain task activation map (reported as coordinate table). Therefore the study meets the review’s social-task (I3), healthy adult sample (I4), whole-brain group-level task reporting (I5), and the allowance for coordinate-table reporting (I6). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample) are met.

This fMRI study used the Wason social-contract Selection Task to investigate reasoning about social rules, which qualifies as social-related processing (I3). The sample is 14 healthy adults (mean age 23.6, range 21–26), meeting the adult healthy-sample criterion (I4). Multiple analyses report group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (Analyses 1,2,3,4: model fit over whole brain, inference over whole brain, cluster-level correction) with reported peak coordinates/tables, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I5) and acceptable reporting of coordinates/tables (I6). Although one analysis used ROIs, the presence of whole-brain, corrected group contrasts fulfills inclusion. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met.

This fMRI study investigated perception of dynamic and static body expressions of anger (a social-communication/perception-of-others task), satisfying I3. The sample comprises 16 healthy adult participants aged 18–26, satisfying I4. The NeuroStore record indicates whole-brain model fitting and voxelwise inference (voxel-level p<0.001, cluster extent reported) with multiple within-group contrasts and tables of peak coordinates, meeting I5 and I6. The report is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes unmasked, healthy-group whole-brain task effects; no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text is represented in the provided document, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study meets the review objective and all inclusion criteria. It uses fMRI during a social decision-making task (Ultimatum Game), satisfying I3. The sample is 35 adult community participants (healthy adults), meeting I4. NeuroStore reports multiple whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (model fit over whole brain) including within-group cross-subject regressions for low- and high-psychopathy scorers and mixed ANOVA contrasts, with voxel-level thresholding and reported peaks, satisfying I5. Results are reported as whole-brain peaks/coordinates (MNI), which is acceptable per I6. No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not ROI-only (E2), not connectivity/resting-state-only (E3), not limited to between-group contrasts without within-group maps (E4), age is within range (E5), and the paper is empirical (E6). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study uses task-based fMRI of a clearly social-related task (facial emotion recognition) in a healthy adult sample (n=21, mean age 32). Importantly, the NeuroStore record reports group-level whole-brain analyses (Analyses 19530218_analysis_2 and _3: model fitted over whole brain and inference over whole brain with reported peaks), which satisfies the requirement for at least one whole-brain task-evoked statistical map for the healthy group. Although the paper also reports ROI analyses (amygdala, ventral striatum), these do not preclude inclusion because whole-brain results are present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria and should be included.

The task in this study is an aesthetic rating of music excerpts (beauty ratings), which is not a clearly social-related task as defined by the review (e.g., affiliation, social communication, perception/understanding of others). Although the authors report activation in ToM-related regions and interpret this as cognitive empathy, the experimental paradigm does not explicitly engage social processing or require judgments about other people. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (healthy adult sample, n=18, ages 18–24), I5 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task results reported), I6 (coordinates/tables provided). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (study does not use fMRI during a clearly social-related task). No exclusion criteria were triggered.

The study reports task-based fMRI during a social interaction/mentalizing task (Prisoner’s Dilemma) directly addressing social processing and attachment (I3). The sample is a healthy adult cohort (n=164, ages 19–35) meeting the 18–65 requirement (I4). NeuroStore extraction shows whole-brain model fitting and whole-brain inference with reported group-level peaks/coordinate tables and cluster-level thresholding (voxelwise maps reported), fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements (I5). Coordinate tables and reported peaks satisfy acceptability of whole-brain results in tables/figures (I6). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/rest-only, only between-group without healthy-group effect, out-of-range age, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

All inclusion criteria are satisfied: I3 - the study used fMRI during social-related tasks (Theory-of-Mind, Moral Judgment, Biological Motion with social interactions); I4 - sample is healthy adults (n=25, mean age 26.0, SD 4.43, ages within 18–65); I5 - the paper reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) within-group contrasts (model fit over whole brain; inference over whole brain) for healthy participants; I6 - whole-brain results are represented (reported peaks/coordinates) and thresholding details are provided. No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, age within range, empirical fMRI data present). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study investigates perception/understanding of others’ actions (observation of a hand grasping objects, including olfactory cues), which maps onto social-related processing. Participants are healthy adults (n=15; ages 22–33). The NeuroStore record indicates whole-brain, group-level task contrasts with inference over the whole brain (e.g., Grasping Visual > Static Visual; reported peaks and tables), satisfying the requirement for a voxelwise task-evoked map for the healthy group. Results are reported in tables of coordinates (acceptable per I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, and empirical fMRI data present). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be INCLUDED.

The paper uses fMRI during social tasks (empathy-eliciting videos; Prisoner’s Dilemma), and includes a separate healthy control group — so I3 and I4 are satisfied. However, all reported whole-brain statistical results are between-group contrasts or interactions (e.g., CDPre > RDPre; RDPost>Pre > CDPost>Pre) rather than an unmasked, whole-brain task activation map from the healthy/control group alone. No healthy-group main effect or within-group whole-brain activation map is reported. Therefore the study meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect) and fails to meet I5 (and I6). Full text appears complete for screening.

Exclusion criterion met: E4. The paper reports social-task fMRI (I3) with a healthy adult group (I4) but does not report any unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group alone. All whole-brain results extracted are between-group contrasts or interactions (e.g., HCs > SZs, main effect HCs>SZs, group×condition interactions) or ROI-restricted amygdala analyses. Therefore I5 (whole-brain healthy-group task map) is not satisfied. Full text appears complete (no access issues).

The study uses fMRI during a social-related empathy-for-pain task (I3) and includes healthy adult participants (I4). However, the NeuroStore record only reports between-group contrasts and interactions (e.g., control vs autism; high vs low alexithymia) fit over the whole brain; there is no clearly identified, unmasked whole-brain group-level task activation map reported for the healthy/control group alone. Analysis entries are described as group comparisons or interactions, and one analysis has no features extracted. Therefore the paper does not provide an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect (I5 not met) and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without a healthy-group whole-brain map). Decision: EXCLUDED.

The study uses task-based fMRI of a social decision-making task (Prisoner’s Dilemma) in a healthy sample (n=35), satisfying I3 and I4. However, all reported whole-brain analyses are between-group contrasts/interactions (prosocials vs proselfs, trust × SVO) and no unmasked, whole‑brain group-level task activation map for the overall healthy group (or an unselected healthy control group) is reported. This meets exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts/interactions reported without an accompanying whole‑brain healthy-group task effect). Therefore the study is excluded for failing to meet I5.

The study reports an fMRI task involving perception of human footsteps and refers to processing in a ‘social cognition’ area (posterior STS), which qualifies as social-related processing. Participants are healthy adults (n=10, ages 20–29). The NeuroStore record indicates group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) model fitting and reports within-group task contrasts (footstep > rest and rest > footstep) with reported peak coordinates (Table 1) and voxel-level thresholding, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Coordinate tables are acceptable per I6. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state only, not only between-group contrasts, and participants are within the eligible age range. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study investigates humor processing (a form of social cognition) in healthy participants and reports whole-brain coordinate tables, but the NeuroStore record lists only between-group contrasts (gender comparisons) and a parametric between-group modulation. There is no clearly identified unmasked, whole-brain task effect reported for the healthy/control group (e.g., cartoons > neutral within the healthy sample). Therefore it fails exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts reported without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task map). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (social-related fMRI task — humor processing), I6 (whole-brain results reported as coordinate tables is acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clearly identified whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked map in the record), I4 (age range 18–65 not explicitly reported in the document). Given E4 is met, the study is excluded.

The paper reports an fMRI social task in healthy participants (I3) and includes a healthy adult subgroup (young adults age ~21; I4). Whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures (I6) and some group-level whole-brain analyses are present for the pooled sample. However, the manuscript does not report an unmasked, whole-brain task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy adult group alone (age 18–65). Instead, reported adult-related results are primarily between-group contrasts/interactions (young adults vs adolescents) without an accompanying within-group whole-brain adult map. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I6. Inclusion criteria not met: I5.

Meets all inclusion criteria: Task is social (Reading the Mind in the Eyes Test) addressing perception/understanding of others (I3). Sample includes a healthy adult group (n=22, ages 21–52) satisfying the 18–65 requirement (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, within-group task contrasts with whole-brain inference (e.g., Analysis 23593185_analysis_0: emotion > gender recognition — model fit and inference over whole brain; Analysis 23593185_analysis_3: condition-by-stimulus interaction with whole-brain inference), and peaks/coordinates are reported (I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts, ages within range, empirical fMRI data present).

This study should be excluded because it reports only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses and does not provide any whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation maps for the healthy adult group. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E2 (ROI-only reporting). (b) Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task: perception and production of facial expressions) and I4 (healthy adult sample, n=178, ages 19–39). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked group map reported; NeuroStore shows model fit over and inference restricted to ROI). No indication the full text was unreadable, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study reports fMRI responses during a social task (influencers evaluating ideas to recommend), satisfying I3. Participants are healthy adults (n=19, mean age 20.55), satisfying I4. NeuroStore extraction indicates whole-brain model fitting and whole-brain inference with reported group-level random-effects analyses and peak coordinates (analyses include group-level random-effects and whole-brain inference), satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not between-group-only, age range appropriate, empirical study).

The study meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) uses fMRI during a social cognitive task (Reading the Mind in the Eyes / Nencki Children Eyes Test assessing perception/understanding of others); (I4) reports a healthy adult sample (n=38, mean age 24.6, within 18–65); (I5) reports at least one group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrast (Analysis 32737383_analysis_0: AM and CM > AS and CS, model fit over whole brain) clearly from the healthy participant group; (I6) whole-brain results are presented as reported peaks/tables. None of the exclusion criteria apply (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, only between-group contrasts without a healthy-group whole-brain effect, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical). Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED in the review. No evidence the full text was unavailable in the provided document.

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (n=21; ages 23–33, mean 26.86), using a social perceptual judgment task involving dyadic nonverbal interactions (meets I3 and I4). Analyses were whole-brain (model fit over: whole brain) with group-level within-group contrasts (e.g., contingent > mirrored; rigid > smooth) and reported peak coordinates/tables, with FWE cluster-level correction—satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and include healthy-group whole-brain task activations. Note: NeuroStore extraction shows a minor participant-sex labeling inconsistency (0 female, 28 male) that does not affect inclusion.

The study reports task-based fMRI of social-related processing (self vs. friend vs. unfamiliar faces/names — self/other perception; satisfies I3). The sample is 29 healthy adults aged 18–24 with results reported for the healthy group (satisfies I4). All reported analyses were fit and inferred over the whole brain (voxelwise), with group-level contrasts and tables of peak coordinates provided (satisfies I5 and I6). Thresholding and cluster correction are described, and multiple within-group whole-brain contrasts are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, age in range, and empirical fMRI data are present). Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

The study reports task-based fMRI of social cognition (mental-state terms, scenario judgments), with healthy adult participants (n=20; ages 18–27). Analyses used whole-brain searchlight MVPA with inference over the whole brain and cluster-level thresholding; peak coordinates are reported in tables. Thus the paper provides group-level, whole-brain task-evoked results for a healthy adult sample. All inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results), and I6 (results reported in tables) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply.

The study uses task-based fMRI of a social cognitive (Theory of Mind/False Belief) task (meets I3). It includes a clearly reported healthy adult group (Neurotypical NT MATCHED; n=27; age range 18–50) with results reported separately (meets I4). It provides a group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise within-group contrast for the healthy/control group (NT MATCHED: Belief>Photo; model fit over whole brain; peaks reported), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (meets I5). Results are reported in tables/peaks and described (meets I6). No exclusion criteria are triggered: not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy adults, and is empirical. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study reports an fMRI task probing social cognitive processes (causal attribution to self/other/situation), uses a healthy adult sample (n=20, ages 18–41), and provides group-level, whole-brain task activation contrasts (self>truth, other>truth, situation>truth, and a conjunction) with reported peak coordinates and whole-brain FWE correction for non-ROI regions. Thus it satisfies I3 (social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps), and I6 (results reported as coordinates/tables). No exclusion criteria are met (whole-brain results are present despite some small-volume corrections for a priori ROIs).

This study is excluded because it does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked group results. NeuroStore extraction states model fit and inference were restricted to a region-of-interest mask (composite of 16 bilateral ROIs) for all reported analyses, i.e., only ROI analyses are presented. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social task—Ultimatum Game) and I4 (healthy adult sample, n=28, ages within 18–65). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no whole-brain evidence reported). Exclusion criterion met: E2 (studies reporting only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Because I5 is not satisfied and E2 applies, the paper must be excluded from the review.

The study meets the review objective and all inclusion criteria. It uses fMRI during a social-related task (perceptual judgment of emotional faces focused on eyes/mouth; I3). The sample includes healthy adult participants (healthy men screened with SCID; analyses report n=23 and n=46 for groups; I4). The paper reports at least one group-level, whole-brain, within-group task-evoked contrast identified as coming from the healthy/control group (Analysis 25047745_analysis_0: angry eyes > neutral eyes, placebo; model fit over whole brain, voxelwise, reported peaks; I5). Results are reported as whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (tables/peaks), acceptable per I6. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants are within adult range, empirical fMRI data present).

The study uses fMRI during a social task (Cyberball) and includes a healthy adult control group (I3 and I4 satisfied). However, the NeuroStore record indicates the reported whole-brain analyses are between-group/omnibus contrasts (e.g., Analysis 24273076_analysis_0: omnibus, between-group; model fit over whole brain) and does not provide an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map explicitly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Thus the paper appears to report only between-group contrasts without a separate healthy-group whole-brain task effect, meeting exclusion criterion E4. Because I5 (healthy-group whole-brain result) is not met, the study must be excluded.

The study reports task-based fMRI during a social interaction (Prisoner’s Dilemma), meeting the social-related task requirement. Participants are adults (n=22, mean age 21.2) within the 18–65 range and appear to be a healthy sample (no clinical group reported), so sample criterion is met. Analyses were fit over the whole brain (model fit over: whole brain) using a group-level GLM with covariates and report peak coordinates in Table tbl8 for multiple within-group contrasts (e.g., CC vs others, CD vs others), providing whole-brain, voxelwise group results. Reporting of peaks in a table satisfies the allowance for coordinate tables. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, age in range, empirical fMRI data present). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied.

This study reports task-based fMRI of social processing (Social Task viewing stick-light communicative gestures) in healthy adults (n=26, mean age 25.1, within 18–65). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise within-subject analyses are reported (whole-brain voxel-wise t-tests; model fit over whole brain; parametric modulation by communicativeness) with peak coordinates and cluster results, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The paper therefore meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample reported), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise results), and I6 (whole-brain results reported via tables/peaks). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants are within age range, and it is empirical fMRI data). Full text appears sufficiently represented in the provided document.

Excluded because the paper reports only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses for the healthy group and does not present any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) healthy-group task activation maps. Exclusion criterion met: E2. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related face-processing task), I4 (healthy adult group reported separately: n=85, mean age 45). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain evidence for the healthy group). Full text appears complete in the provided record (no access issues).

The study reports task-based fMRI (Dictator Game) probing prosocial/selfish behavior (social-related processing) in healthy young adults (N=23–27; mean age 21.25), satisfying the healthy adult sample requirement. Multiple group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM contrasts are reported (e.g., Friend Prosocial > Disliked Peer Prosocial; Disliked Peer Selfish > Friend Selfish) with whole-brain inference and peaks listed in tables; thresholding is FWE cluster-corrected (p<0.005 cluster-level). These constitute unmasked, whole-brain task activation maps for the healthy group. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text is available in the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

The study uses fMRI of a social task (moral reasoning) and includes a healthy adult control group (I3 and I4 met). However, the NeuroStore record reports whole-brain within-group contrasts only for the patient (ASD) group and reports between-group interaction contrasts (ASD vs HC) for healthy controls; it does not report an unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task activation map (no clear within-group HC whole-brain results). Therefore this study reports only between-group/interactions without a separate healthy-group whole-brain task map, meeting exclusion criterion E4. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. Exclusion criterion met: E4.

This study reports task-based fMRI during a social interaction task (Ultimatum Game) with prior personal trait information, fulfilling the social-related task requirement. The sample is healthy adults (n=24, mean age 21.08), within the 18–65 range. The analyses were fit over the whole brain with inference over the whole brain (permutation-based cluster-wise FWE correction using SnPM13) and reported group-level peaks/contrasts, providing whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results for the healthy group. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample) are met. Note: minor reporting inconsistency in sex counts does not affect eligibility.

This paper reports task-based fMRI of gaze perception, a clearly social cognition task (analysis of others’ eye gaze), in a healthy adult sample (n=10, mean age 24). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (model fit over: whole brain) with multiple within-group task contrasts reported as peak coordinates and tables. Thus it provides healthy-group whole-brain task activation maps relevant to social processing. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met.

The study uses task fMRI probing social-related processing (biological motion/intentions) satisfying I3, and reports a healthy adult sample (n=16, mean age 22.75) satisfying I4. However, all reported analyses indicate model fit and inference were restricted to regions of interest (Model fit over: region of interest; Inference restricted to: region of interest), so no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps are reported. Therefore the study does not meet I5 and is excluded under E2 (ROI-only analyses). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (whole-brain evidence). Exclusion criteria applied: E2.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it used task-based fMRI of social processing (competitive interactions with friend, confederate, and computer) (I3); participants are healthy adults (n=18, mean age 20.4) (I4); the paper reports group-level, within-subject whole-brain task contrasts/inference (main effect of competitor and positive>negative outcome contrasts with whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference reported) (I5); results include reported peaks/coordinates which satisfy acceptable reporting formats (I6). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper does not report only ROI or only connectivity analyses, includes whole-brain task activation maps, and participants are within the 18–65 range. Therefore the study should be included in the review.

This study used fMRI during social decision-making tasks (coordination games requiring strategic thinking), meeting I3. Participants are adults (n=18, mean age 26), with no patient or special-group indication, meeting I4. Several reported analyses explicitly state whole-brain model fitting and whole-brain inference (e.g., contrasts with 'Model fit over: whole brain' and 'Inference over: whole brain' with voxelwise thresholding), providing group-level task-evoked whole-brain maps, meeting I5. Reporting of coordinates/peaks and whole-brain inference satisfies I6. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group healthy maps, ages in range, empirical fMRI data present).

The NeuroStore record reports only a seed-based psychophysiological interaction (PPI) connectivity analysis (VMPFC seed) and does not report any group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation map for the healthy sample. Inference for the connectivity result was restricted to an ROI. Thus the paper provides social-task fMRI in healthy adults (I3 and I4 met) but does not provide the required whole-brain task activation evidence (I5 not met) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (only seed-based/effective connectivity reported without a healthy-group whole-brain task effect). No indication the full text was unreadable.

The study meets all inclusion requirements: it used fMRI during a social-related task (viewing actors’ joyful/angry grasping videos) addressing perception/understanding of others (I3); included a healthy adult sample (n=20, ages 23–33) (I4); and it reports group-level, whole-brain within-group task contrasts (e.g., Angry > Joyful; Grasping > Faces) with FWE cluster-level inference and tables of peak coordinates (I5). Reporting of peaks/tables satisfies acceptable reporting formats (I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effects, participants within age range, and is empirical).

Exclusion IDs met: E3 and E4. The study reports only seed-based psychophysiological interaction (PPI) connectivity analyses (LC and SC seeds) and between-group interactions/correlations (PTSD vs controls, symptom severity correlations). Inclusion IDs met: I3 (task is social-related: direct vs averted gaze/eye contact) and I4 (a healthy adult control group is included). Inclusion IDs not met: I5 is not satisfied — the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group; instead results are connectivity (PPI) maps and between-group contrasts. Therefore the study must be excluded under E3 (only seed-based/effective connectivity reported) and E4 (only between-group/interaction effects without an unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect).

The study uses task fMRI of a social-related Theory-of-Mind/humor processing task (I3). A healthy control group (n=13, age mean 29.6) is reported separately (I4). Whole-brain model fitting is stated and the paper reports group-level, voxelwise within-group contrast results for the control group (ToM > Physical cartoons) with reported peaks (Table tbl3), satisfying whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting formats (I5, I6). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and a healthy-group unmasked whole-brain task effect is present. Full text appears available in the provided NeuroStore record (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study reports task-based fMRI of social cognition tasks in a healthy adult sample (n=45, ages 19–23). It provides group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise within-group contrasts (e.g., social>mechanical and mechanical>social) with inference performed over the whole brain and multiple-comparison correction; results are reported as peak coordinates/tables. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion E4 met: the paper does not report an unmasked, whole-brain task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The NeuroStore record shows (a) between-group and combined-group main effects (n=24) and a within-group analysis only for patients (n=12), and (b) a Controls>aMCI between-group contrast, but no within-group whole-brain healthy-control task map or coordinates explicitly labelled as the healthy group alone. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task is social-related: personal familiar vs unfamiliar faces/rooms) and I4 (sample includes healthy adult participants). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain, voxelwise task effect reported for the healthy/control group alone). I6 (acceptable reporting formats) is not sufficient to overcome the lack of a healthy-group whole-brain result. Therefore the study is excluded under E4.

The study uses fMRI during a social Trust Game (satisfies I3) and includes a healthy adult subgroup (young adults 18–27) (satisfies I4). However, the NeuroStore extraction does not report any unambiguous, unmasked whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy adult group alone; reported whole-brain results are either across the mixed-age sample or are between-group/interaction contrasts comparing age groups. Therefore the paper does not provide a clear whole-brain healthy-adult task effect, failing I5. This meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect).

The study meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) it uses fMRI during a social-related task (Cyberball social exclusion), (I4) participants are healthy adults (n=20, mean age 24.99, within 18–65), (I5) it reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., social exclusion > fair play) with model fit and inference performed over the whole brain, and (I6) results are reported as tables of peak coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, age range appropriate, and empirical fMRI data are presented). Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) it used task-based fMRI during a social cognition task (statements about motivations, mind-states, behaviors); (I4) reported a healthy adult sample (n=25, mean age 23.2, female participants only) within 18–65; (I5) reported group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (model fit and inference over whole brain, GRF cluster-thresholding) including within-group contrasts and parametric modulation; (I6) whole-brain results are reported as peak coordinates/tables. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants are within age range, and this is empirical fMRI data). Therefore the paper should be included.

The study uses task fMRI of social cognition (ToM) and reports whole-brain healthy-group task activation maps (ToM > non-ToM) in the healthy participants, and reports coordinates/tables — so it meets I3, I5, and I6. However, all participants (patients and controls) are adolescents (age range 12–18, mean ~15.7–15.8) and no healthy adult subgroup (18–65) is reported. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (only participants outside the 18–65 range). Because I4 is not met, the study must be excluded for this review objective.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) It uses task-based fMRI of a clearly social/prosocial paradigm (prosocial learning and empathy). (I4) Reports a healthy adult sample (n=31; ages 19–32). (I5) Reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task effects (multiple analyses list ‘Model fit over: whole brain’ and ‘Inference over: whole brain’, with peak coordinates and tables). (I6) Whole-brain results are reported in tables of coordinates (Table table-1/2/3/4) and described in the text. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not limited to ROIs only (whole-brain maps present), not solely connectivity or between-group contrasts, and participants are within the 18–65 range. The NeuroStore record is sufficiently detailed to confirm presence of unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task activation maps. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the review.

This study is excluded because it does not report a whole-brain, group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group (I5 not met), and instead reports mainly between-group contrasts (e.g., HC > RTLE, HC > LTLE) without an accompanying unmasked healthy-group within-group map. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (social-related fMRI task: face processing) and I4 (healthy adult participants included and reported). Exclusion criteria met: E4 (only between-group contrasts reported without a whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Fulltext is complete for screening.

This fMRI study examined observation of nonpainful touch (a social/perception-of-others task) in healthy adult participants (n=19, ages 23–39). It reports a within-group contrast (Touch observation > control) with the model fit and inference performed over the whole brain (voxelwise FWE thresholding) and reports peak(s) in left primary somatosensory cortex in MNI space. Thus it meets the review objective and satisfies inclusion criteria for a social-related fMRI task (I3), healthy adult sample (I4), and reporting of at least one group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrast (I5). The results are reported in standard coordinate space and peaks (I6). No exclusion criteria apply.

The study investigates affective (social) touch and explicitly frames activations in ‘‘social brain’’ regions; the task (experiencing and imagining gentle caress-like touch) maps onto social-related constructs (affiliation/affective social perception). The sample is healthy adults (n=17, ages 19–25). Importantly, the NeuroStore record reports group-level, whole-brain, within-group task contrasts with whole-brain model fitting and whole-brain inference (Analyses 24700583_analysis_0 through _3 report whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Results are reported in tables of peaks/coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, age within range, empirical fMRI data). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI of a social-related task (modified Cyberball social exclusion/performance game) (I3); reports a healthy adult sample (n=40, mean age 27.8, 20F/20M) within 18–65 (I4); and provides whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise task activation results (within-group contrasts such as FG EX > FG IN, PG EX > FG IN, etc.) with voxelwise FWE inference and reported peak coordinates in tables (I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, age appropriate, empirical fMRI data). Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED.

This fMRI study investigates maternal attachment (a social/affiliation task) using task-based BOLD responses to own vs unfamiliar infant videos, consistent with the review’s social processing domain. Participants are healthy adult mothers (n=23) screened for depression/anxiety; two were excluded for elevated BDI, leaving a healthy adult sample. The paper reports a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrast (own infant > stranger infant) with reported peak coordinates (Table 1) and Talairach space, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Reporting in coordinate tables meets the acceptable reporting formats. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked map), and I6 (acceptable reporting of whole-brain results). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met.

The NeuroStore record reports task-based fMRI of social-related processing (action observation of others’ hand actions), satisfying I3. The paper reports separate healthy adult groups (n=31, 25, 23; ages 19–40/32/33), satisfying I4. For each experiment it reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (ActionOBS > CtrlOBS) with whole-brain inference and FWE-corrected peaks/coordinate tables, satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not limited to ROIs (E2), not connectivity/resting-state only (E3), not only between-group contrasts (E4), participants are within 18–65 (E5), and this is empirical fMRI data (E6). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This fMRI study examines affective theory-of-mind processing (social perception/understanding of others) using a False Belief/ToM cartoon task with and without emotional facial expressions (EFE), meeting the review’s social-related task requirement. The sample is a healthy adult group (n=21, mean age 23.73), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task activation results: Analysis 26803059_analysis_0 explicitly reports whole-brain inference with FWE-corrected results and multiple reported peak coordinates (tables), and other whole-brain contrasts/associations are reported in tables/peaks. Thus I3, I4, and I5 are met; coordinate/table reporting satisfies I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, no between-group-only contrasts, age within range, empirical data).

The study uses fMRI during a social task (threat-of-shock with friend/stranger handholding) in healthy adult participants (mean age 23.6), so I3 and I4 are met. However, NeuroStore indicates all reported analyses were fit and thresholded over regions of interest (model fit over: region of interest; thresholding: region-level) with no whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation maps reported. Therefore it does not meet I5 and meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only results).

This fMRI study examines integration of speaker characteristics (a social-communication / perception-of-others task) using whole-brain BOLD contrasts. It reports separate results for a healthy adult control group (n=24; ages 18–39). NeuroStore extraction shows group-level, whole-brain, within-group contrasts for the control group (speaker-incongruent > speaker-congruent and the reverse) with reported peak coordinates in tables, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps for healthy participants. The study is empirical, not ROI-only or connectivity-only, and controls are within the 18–65 age range. No exclusion criteria from the review are met.

Excluded because the sample falls outside the eligible adult age range. Specifically, participants are described as healthy older women (mean age 71.69, SD 7.17), so no healthy adult group aged 18–65 is reported. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (only participants outside 18–65). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task: judging others’ affect from videos), I5 (whole-brain group-level analyses reported: model fit and inference over whole brain with reported peaks), I6 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (sample age range 18–65). Full text is complete for screening.

This NeuroStore record reports an fMRI study of social contexts in healthy adults (meets I3 and I4). However, the only reported whole-brain statistical map in the document is a between-group contrast (Gain > Loss between PPI low vs PPI high). The record does not present an unmasked, whole-brain task activation map for the healthy group (e.g., main effect or within-group contrast for the healthy/control sample). According to the eligibility rules, studies that report only between-group contrasts or interactions without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect must be excluded (E4). Therefore exclude under E4. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no healthy-group whole-brain task map reported).

The study uses an fMRI social task (facial emotion/age judgments) so it meets I3. Although healthy control participants are included, the NeuroStore record does not report any unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation maps clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Reported whole-brain results are primarily between-group interactions (CTL vs REL vs SCZ) or within-group contrasts from patients only. Therefore the study fails to provide the required healthy-group whole-brain task effect (I5) and thus meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task map). Inclusion criteria met: I3. Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (results for healthy group not reported separately as an unmasked whole-brain map) and I5 (no healthy-group whole-brain task effect reported).

This study used fMRI during a social task (Cyberball) in a healthy adult sample (n=22, ages 18–29). The NeuroStore record reports group-level, within-subject whole-brain contrasts (e.g., Control ‘sports’ cues Exclusion > Inclusion and smell × condition interaction) with whole-brain inference and cluster correction (Analyses 8 and 9). Thus it provides at least one voxelwise, group-level task-evoked activation map from the healthy sample. Methods and results meet the review’s requirements for social-related fMRI in healthy adults.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. I3: It uses task-based fMRI to investigate affective/affiliative touch and the sight of touch—socially relevant constructs (affiliative/caress-like touch, perception of others’ touch). I4: The sample is healthy adults (n=12, ages 18–30). I5: The NeuroStore record indicates model fits over the whole brain and reports at least one group-level whole-brain task effect without ROI restriction (analyses 19015100_analysis_17 and _18 show whole-brain thresholding reported as p<0.005 with no ROI restriction), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked maps. I6: Results are reported as peaks/coordinates (Table 2), which is an acceptable reporting format. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state/ connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, empirical fMRI data present).

This study uses an fMRI social-cognition task (brief animations) and includes a healthy control group, so I3 (social task) and I4 (healthy participants reported) are satisfied. However, all reported results are seed-based PPI connectivity analyses and primarily between-group contrasts (FH>HC, MDD>HC, FH>MDD). Although some PPI models were fit over the whole brain, the contrasts reported are between-group connectivity effects rather than an unmasked, whole-brain task-evoked activation map clearly identified for the healthy/control group. Therefore the paper does not provide the required healthy-group whole-brain task activation map (I5 not met) and meets exclusion criteria E3 (connectivity-only results without a healthy-group whole-brain task map) and E4 (only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Exclusion criteria met: E2 and E4. The reported analysis is a group x cue-type (between-group) interaction with inference explicitly restricted to a region-of-interest; although the model was fitted over the whole brain, statistical inference was performed within an ROI, and no unmasked whole-brain, group-level healthy-task activation map is reported. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task — Social Incentive Delay Task with social face stimuli) and I4 (healthy adult sample, ages within 18–65). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clear whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task-evoked map from the healthy/control group is reported) — I6 is therefore not applicable. Because the paper reports only ROI-restricted inference and a between-group interaction without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect, it must be excluded.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E2 and E4. The reported analysis is a between-group interaction (Elderly vs Young) and inference was restricted to a region-of-interest with small-volume correction; no unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task activation map is reported. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task — personal familiarity/familiar faces likely involves social processing) and I4 (healthy adult groups are included; both elderly and young healthy participants are reported). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (the paper does not report an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map from the healthy/control group; results are ROI-restricted and reported for between-group contrast). Full text is complete for review.

This study uses fMRI during a social task (facial emotion/cognitive empathy) and includes a healthy adult control group (I3 and I4 satisfied). However, NeuroStore extraction shows only between-group whole-brain contrasts (Control > Schizophrenia; Schizophrenia > Control) reported (no unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map identified as coming from the healthy/control group). Therefore the study reports only between-group contrasts without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect, meeting exclusion criterion E4. Inclusion criterion I5 (healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked map) is not met. Full text appears available in the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study uses task fMRI of social-related processing (self/other perspective-taking) and includes a healthy adult control group (I3 and I4 satisfied). However, the NeuroStore record shows only between-group contrasts (TD > ASD interactions) and seed-based connectivity analyses; it does not report an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map or within-group healthy-control activation contrast. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). fulltext_incomplete is false.

Meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) fMRI was used during a social-related task (viewing dynamic and static facial expressions; social perception of others); (I4) sample includes healthy adults (n=40, mean age 30.54); (I5) reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps from the healthy group (model fit over whole brain; group average one-sample t-tests for dynamic>static BOLD contrasts with reported peaks/tables); (I6) whole-brain results are reported in tables of coordinates. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, age in range, empirical fMRI data present). Full text appears accessible via the NeuroStore extraction, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Meets all inclusion criteria: the study uses task-based fMRI during a social-related Moral Judgment Task (I3); reports a healthy adult sample (n=23, ages 21–35) (I4); includes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise within-group contrasts and parametric whole-brain analyses (Analysis 28952137_analysis_0 and Analyses 2–5) with thresholding and reported peak coordinates (I5); results are reported as coordinate tables/peaks (I6). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants are within 18–65, and this is empirical fMRI data. Therefore INCLUDE.

This study reports task-based fMRI in a social/empathy paradigm (campaign videos vs neutral), matching social-related processing. Participants are healthy adults (n=20; ages 20–28), meeting the sample criterion. The paper reports a group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise within-group contrast (CV > NV) analyzed with a random-effects one-sample t-test, model fit and inference performed over the whole brain with FWE correction and reported peak coordinates. Results are clearly from the healthy group. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

The study meets all inclusion criteria: it used task-based fMRI during a social-related perceptual judgment of affective vocalisations (I3); participants are healthy adults (n=18, mean age 25.9) (I4); a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrast was reported (Model fit over: whole brain; voxel-level thresholding; reported peaks/table) fulfilling whole-brain evidence (I5); results are reported as peaks/tables (satisfying I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, includes a healthy adult group, empirical task fMRI).

The study investigates emotional prosody comprehension, a social-communication task (meets I3). The sample includes a healthy adult group (n=19; ages 18.0–51.0) within the 18–65 range (meets I4). NeuroStore extraction indicates voxelwise whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference for within-group task contrasts (emotional tones > neutral; complex > simple emotions) with reported peak coordinates/tables, satisfying the requirement for at least one group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map (meets I5). Results are reported as coordinate tables (meets I6). No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts, and participants are within the eligible age range. Full text is sufficiently represented by the provided NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study reports task-based fMRI during social cognition (Theory of Mind/social exchange) using the Wason selection task, clearly a social-related task. Participants are healthy adults (n=12, mean age 24.6), meeting the age/sample criterion. Analyses were fit over the whole brain and report group-level, within-group task contrasts (e.g., Social Contracts > Precautions, Social Contracts > Descriptives) with reported peak coordinates/tables, satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

The study investigates irony comprehension (a social-cognition task) using fMRI and includes a healthy adult control group, but the NeuroStore extraction shows only between-group contrasts and patient within-group regressions. No unmasked, whole-brain group-level activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group is reported. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts without an accompanying healthy-group whole-brain task effect).

The study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It used task-based fMRI during a social-related emotion-regulation task (compassion toward people in distress), satisfying I3. The sample are healthy adult participants aged 45–62 (within 18–65), satisfying I4. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (model fit and inference over whole brain) with tables of peak coordinates for multiple within-group contrasts (Compassion>Watch-Negative, Compassion>Reappraisal, Reappraisal>Compassion), satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and participants are within age range. Therefore the paper should be included.

The study reports an fMRI investigation of social exclusion using the Cyberball task (a social-related task), fulfilling I3. Participants are 64 healthy adults (mean age 47.1, SD 16.3), within the 18–65 range, fulfilling I4.
