The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (model fit over: whole brain; inference over: whole brain) for the exclusion > inclusion contrast with FWE thresholding and a table of reported peaks, satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, age range appropriate, empirical data present).

The study reports task-based fMRI of social stimuli (human and dog faces; face perception is a social-related process), includes a healthy adult human sample (n=30, age range 21–50), and provides group-level, whole-brain within-group contrasts for the human participants (Analyses 2, 3, 4, 5, 6: whole-brain, random-effects GLM; peaks reported). Whole-brain results are clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control human group and are thresholded and reported (table/peaks). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, resting-state/ connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the article meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This study used task-based fMRI of social processing (facial emotion recognition integrating gaze; meets I3). It reports data from healthy adult groups (younger adults mean age 20.65, range includes mostly 18–27) so a healthy adult group is present (meets I4). Analyses were fit over the whole brain with inference over the whole brain (task PLS with permutation testing) and the NeuroStore record lists whole-brain reported peaks/tables for within-group effects for younger and older adults, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5) and acceptable reporting in tables of coordinates (I6). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without healthy-group maps, out-of-range-only samples, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete in the NeuroStore extraction.

The study uses fMRI during a social-related task (biological motion perception; social perception of others) and reports healthy adult participants (n=48; ages 20–35) separately. It includes whole-brain, group-level task-evoked contrasts for adults (e.g., biological > scrambled; Sex×Condition ANOVA) with reported peak coordinates and cluster-level inference, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Results are clearly identified as coming from the healthy adult group. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria: it uses task fMRI during a social-related task (self vs familiar other judgments) (I3); includes a healthy adult group (n=12, mean age 26.1) reported separately (I4); reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked activation maps for the healthy adult group (e.g., Analyses 17651006_analysis_0 and _1: Self>Rest and Harry Potter>Rest, whole-brain, corrected thresholds, reported peak tables), satisfying whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting formats (I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group healthy adult maps, participants in age range, empirical fMRI data present). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study uses task fMRI of emotional sentence attribution (social-related task) and includes a healthy adult control group (I3 and I4 met). However, the NeuroStore record lists only between-group contrasts (EMO>GRAM, GRAM>EMO, CONTROLS>PATIENTS) and does not report any unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (healthy-group whole-brain task effect) is NOT met. This matches exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts reported without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study used task-based fMRI (BOLD) during a social-related emotion task (participants rated emotions toward photographs of social groups), satisfying I3. Participants are reported as n=10 (and n=12 for object condition) with no indication of clinical/special populations; this supports I4 (healthy adult group reported separately). The analyses were modeled over the whole brain (Model fit over: whole brain) with voxelwise thresholding and reported group-level peaks, satisfying I5 and I6 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates/peaks). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, and include within-group whole-brain task activations. Although exact ages are not stated in the extracted record, the sample is presented as a healthy adult group in a standard fMRI task; confidence is 0.80 due to absence of explicit age range in the record.

The NeuroStore record shows the task is social (Prisoner’s Dilemma) and the sample is healthy adults (ages 18–22), so inclusion criteria I3 and I4 are satisfied. However, all reported analyses were performed with model fit and inference restricted to predefined regions of interest (bilateral amygdala and anterior insula); no group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps from the healthy group are reported. Thus inclusion criterion I5 is not met. This meets exclusion criterion E2 (studies reporting only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

The study uses task-based fMRI of empathy/social processing (affective picture viewing of human and animal suffering), includes healthy adult participants (omnivores, vegetarians, vegans; ages 18–53), and reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps (within-group contrasts Human>Animal and Animal>Human; model fit over whole brain; FWE thresholding; reported coordinate tables). Whole-brain results are clearly described and reported in tables/peaks. Thus it meets I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (at least one group-level whole-brain task-evoked map), and I6 (coordinate reporting acceptable). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts).

The study used task fMRI of social processing and included a healthy control group (I3 and I4 met). However, the reported neuroimaging results are limited to an ROI analysis (amygdala) with small-volume correction and the reported contrast is a between-group interaction (Cocaine > Control). No unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group is reported. Therefore the paper fails the whole-brain evidence requirement (I5) and meets exclusion criteria E2 (ROI-only results) and E4 (only between-group contrast/interaction reported without a whole-brain healthy-group effect).

This fMRI study examines perception/understanding of others’ actions (videos and sentences of an actor performing eating/cleaning), matching the review’s social-related task domain. Participants are healthy adults (n=23, mean age 21.6), satisfying the sample criterion. The report describes group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (model fit over whole brain, second-level contrasts) and reports peak coordinates in tables, which fulfills the whole-brain evidence requirement and acceptable reporting formats. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, participant ages within 18–65, empirical fMRI data present). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

The paper reports an event-related fMRI task probing self-face recognition (perception/understanding of self), with healthy adult participants (n=10, mean age 26.9). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (self > other and other > self) were reported with whole-brain cluster-corrected inference (Z<2.3; cluster-level correction), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked maps. Methods indicate whole-brain GLM (FLAME) and corrected cluster significance. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within 18–65, empirical fMRI data). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective.

The study meets all inclusion criteria for the review: (I3) It uses task-based fMRI during a social-related task (Facial Emotion Recognition Task assessing perception of others’ emotions). (I4) Reports results from healthy adult participants (n=25 for treatment contrasts; an additional whole-brain regression reports n=116 healthy participants). (I5) Provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps/contrasts (analyses 28629540_analysis_0, _1, and _2 report whole-brain voxelwise FWE-thresholded results with reported peaks). (I6) Whole-brain results are reported as peaks/coordinates and described. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group healthy whole-brain effects, participants are adults). Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED.

The study uses fMRI during a clearly social task (vignettes requiring attributions) and includes healthy adult participants, so it meets I3 and I4. However, the NeuroStore extraction reports only a group-by-empathy interaction (a between-group effect) as the whole-brain analysis; no unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group is reported in the extracted analyses. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criterion I5 (a whole-brain healthy-group task map) is not met. Based on the provided document, exclude for E4.

This study uses a social-related fMRI task (Facial Emotion Perception Test) and includes a healthy adult control group (I3 and I4 satisfied). However, NeuroStore shows only between-group interaction contrasts (HC > MDD and MDD > HC) and within-group regressions reported for the patient group; there is no unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group (i.e., no healthy-group main effect or within-group contrast). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (whole-brain healthy-group result) is not satisfied. Full text appears available in the record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The paper uses fMRI during a social task and includes a healthy adult group, but the document does not report an unambiguous whole-brain, within-group task-evoked activation map for the healthy/control participants. The reported healthy-group maps are connectivity (gPPI) results; activation results presented in the document are between-group contrasts/interactions (healthy > patients or conjunctions) rather than an unmasked HC TASK>CONT whole-brain effect. Therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. Full text was available in the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study should be excluded because it reports only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses with inference restricted to ROIs (Model fit over: region of interest; Inference restricted to: region of interest). This violates inclusion criterion I5 (requires at least one group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map) and meets exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI analyses). The study does meet I3 (fMRI during a social-related task — emotional face processing) and I4 (includes healthy adult participants alongside patients), but does not provide whole-brain healthy-group task activation maps. Full text is complete in the provided document.

Exclusion met: E4. The paper reports only between-group contrasts (patient > control for mother and father conditions) from whole-brain two-sample t-tests, with reported peak tables, but does not report an unmasked, whole-brain task activation map or within-group (healthy/control) task effect. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task—parental/attachment processing) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group, age within 18–65). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain, group-level healthy/control task activation map is reported). Full text appears complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study is excluded because it reports only between-group interaction contrasts and does not present an unmasked, whole-brain task effect for the healthy/control group alone. Exclusion IDs met: E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion IDs met: I3 (uses fMRI during a social-related task — gesture planning/execution, social action planning), I4 (includes a healthy adult control group, n=25, ages within 18–65). Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (no clearly identified group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map reported for the healthy/control group alone — the NeuroStore extraction lists only interaction/between-group contrasts and no unmasked healthy-group main-effect maps). Therefore the paper does not meet all required inclusion criteria and must be excluded.

The study uses fMRI during a social cognition task (meets I3). However, the sample consists of incarcerated adults with varying psychopathy scores and no separate healthy/control group results are reported (I4 not met). Critically, all reported analyses are region-of-interest (Model fit over: region of interest; region-level thresholding) and the record does not show any whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked maps from a healthy/control group (I5 not met). Therefore exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) applies. Inclusion criteria met: I3. Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I5. Full text is complete in this record (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The paper reports task-based fMRI in a social cognition paradigm and includes a healthy adult control group, but it does not report any group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation map for the healthy/control group. All reported results are seed-based functional connectivity between-group contrasts and patient within-group correlations. Therefore it meets exclusion criteria for reporting only seed-based connectivity and only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI during an Action Observation task that involves perception/understanding of others (social-related processing) (I3). The sample comprises healthy adult participants within the 18–65 range (n=25, ages 18.08–22.67) (I4). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (Model fit over: whole brain; reported peaks and thresholding provided), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement (I5). Results/peaks are reported in coordinate space (MNI), satisfying acceptability of tables/figures for whole-brain results (I6). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical study).

The study reports an fMRI emotional face-matching task (social-related processing) with a separately reported healthy adult group (n=11, mean age 32.17). The paper provides a within-group, whole-brain contrast for the healthy participants (Emotion Match > Shape Match) with reported peaks and model fit over the whole brain. Thus it meets inclusion criteria for social processing (I3), healthy adult sample reported separately (I4), whole-brain healthy-group task activation (I5), and acceptable reporting formats (I6). No exclusion criteria are met.

The study meets all inclusion criteria: I3 (task is social-related: social gaze/likeability judgments of dynamic faces using fMRI), I4 (reports a separate healthy adult control group, n=13, ages within 18–65), I5 (reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts for the healthy/control group, e.g., DG > AG within-group contrast with reported peaks; model was fit over the whole brain), and I6 (results are reported as peak coordinates/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-group healthy whole-brain results, appropriate age range, empirical fMRI data). Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED.

The study reports fMRI during a social-processing task (viewing eyes with dynamic pupillary changes), includes a healthy adult sample (n=14, mean age 22), and provides at least one group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analysis. Specifically, Analysis 19048432_analysis_3 is a whole-brain parametric modulation (p<0.001, cluster extent reported) showing task-evoked effects. ROI analyses are also reported, but the presence of the whole-brain result satisfies the whole-brain evidence requirement. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study uses fMRI during a social task (Cyberball) and includes an adult subgroup (abstract and interaction contrast indicate adults), so I3 and I4 are met. However, the paper does not report an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map specifically for the healthy adult group. The only adult-specific result is a Condition x Age-group interaction with inference restricted to a small-volume ROI (SVC). The reported whole-brain main effects appear to be for the combined sample (adolescents + adults), not for an adult-only healthy group. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain adult-group map) is not satisfied. This meets exclusion criterion E4: only between-group contrasts/interactions are reported for the adult comparison without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-adult task effect. Full text appears complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study uses fMRI during a social-related task (Cyberball social exclusion) and explicitly reports healthy control results: the abstract states that increasing social exclusion activated the medial prefrontal cortex in controls. A healthy adult control group is present and reported separately (controls: n included within the combined sample, mean age ~40.87, within 18–65). The document reports whole-brain model fit and inference and lists reported peaks/tables for analyses; the control-group whole-brain effect is clearly identified in the text (replication of mPFC activation). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, age within range, empirical fMRI data). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

Excluded (E4): The study uses fMRI during social tasks (I3 satisfied) and includes healthy adult controls (I4 satisfied). However, the NeuroStore extraction shows the Belief task result is reported as a between-group interaction (Controls > Patients contrast) and the Emotion task within-group contrast is reported only for patients; there is no unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map clearly identified for the healthy/control group. Therefore I5 (healthy-group whole-brain task effect) is not met, triggering exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying healthy-group whole-brain task effect).

The study uses task fMRI of social cognition (HCP social paradigm) so I3 is satisfied. However, the NeuroStore record lists only a between-group whole-brain contrast (social > non-social [between-group] in a conjunction with motion) and DCM/effective-connectivity findings. There is no unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group in the provided document. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrast without an accompanying healthy-group whole-brain task effect). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no clear report of healthy-group whole-brain results separate from clinical group) and I5 (no healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked statistical map provided). Full text is complete as provided. Excluding on the basis of E4.

This fMRI study tests social processing (competition vs control encoding of opponents' faces) in healthy young adults (n=72, mean age 21.7), meeting the sample and task requirements. Crucially, it reports at least one group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrast (Analysis 33347912_analysis_2: Subsequent Hit > Subsequent Miss; model fit over: whole brain; inference over: whole brain; FWE p<0.001), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Other reported analyses include ROI-restricted and connectivity results, but these do not negate the presence of whole-brain activation maps. No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not out-of-range ages, not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED in the review.

This study reports task-based fMRI in social paradigms (Cyberball social exclusion and a Dictator Game) in a healthy adult sample (n=26; mean age 20.7). Multiple group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise within-group contrasts and whole-brain regression analyses are reported (e.g., exclusion > inclusion; excluders > includers) with peaks in MNI space and GLM random-effects group analyses. Results are not ROI-only and are task-evoked activations from the healthy participant group. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria for fMRI social processing in healthy adults and does not meet any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, no resting-state/connectivity-only, and reports healthy-group whole-brain effects).

This fMRI study investigates forms of emotional distancing (spatial, temporal, objective) which the authors frame as engaging social-cognitive processes and mechanisms for distancing oneself (maps onto ‘Perception and Understanding of Self’ / social-cognitive constructs). Participants are healthy adults (N=34, mean age 24.4 within 18–65). The NeuroStore record documents multiple group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., negative-FAR > negative-VIEW; negative-OBJECTIVE > negative-VIEW; negative-TIME > negative-VIEW) with whole-brain inference and reported peak coordinates/tables, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Therefore I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

The study should be INCLUDED. It reports task-based fMRI of animacy attribution (a social cognitive task using adapted Heider and Simmel stimuli), satisfying I3. The sample is healthy adults (n=34, ages 20–34), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, within-group task contrasts (ANIM > Random) with inference over the whole brain and cluster-level correction, satisfying I5. Results are reported as peaks/tables, meeting I6. No exclusion criteria apply: this is not an ROI-only paper (E2), not only connectivity/resting-state (E3), not only between-group contrasts (E4), participants are within 18–65 (E5), and it is empirical fMRI research (not E6).

This study meets all inclusion criteria. It uses fMRI during a social-related task (judgments of pride and joy involving self/other perspective-taking and social cognition) satisfying I3. The sample is healthy adults (n=16, mean age 21.4, 18–65 range) satisfying I4. Crucially, the paper reports group-level, whole-brain, within-group task contrasts (Pride>Neutral, Joy>Neutral, Pride>Joy) with model fit over the whole brain and reported peak coordinates (Tables), meeting I5; these results are acceptable as coordinate/table-reported whole-brain evidence (I6). Although the record notes an overall 'Inference restricted to: region of interest', the extracted analyses for the primary task contrasts explicitly state 'Model fit over: whole brain' and report voxel-level thresholding and peaks, so there is clear whole-brain task-evoked activation from the healthy group. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This fMRI study investigates perception of others’ disgust expressions (a social-processing task), uses a healthy adult sample (n=27, mean age 27), and reports group-level, whole-brain, within-group task contrasts. Although two contrasts used SVC, the Distaste > Neutral contrast is reported voxelwise with peaks (Table 1) and no ROI restriction, satisfying the requirement for an unmasked whole-brain task effect. Results are presented as peaks/coordinates (Table 1), which is acceptable. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting, not between-group-only, age within 18–65, empirical fMRI data present).

This study examines social-affective processing (infant face emotions) using task fMRI in adult women, so I3 (social-related task) is met. It reports healthy adult groups (new mothers and nulliparous women) within the 18–65 range, so I4 is met. However, the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked maps from a healthy group (within-group healthy/control task effects). The reported within-group associations are ROI-limited, and the whole-brain results presented are exclusively between-group contrasts/interactions. Therefore it fails I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect).

The study reports event-related fMRI during a clearly social cognition task (observing social integrity threats and rating schadenfreude or fremdscham), with a healthy adult sample (n=34; ages 19–31). Crucially, the paper includes group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise within-group task contrasts for each healthy group (Analyses 8 and 9: SIT > NEUT; model fit over whole brain; inference over whole brain; FWE voxel-level; reported peak tables), which satisfy the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps. Results are reported in tables/peaks and ROI analyses are supplementary but do not preclude inclusion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; includes unmasked whole-brain healthy-group effects; participants within 18–65; empirical fMRI data).

This study uses task fMRI of social exclusion (Cyberball) and includes a healthy adult control group (28 healthy controls), satisfying I3 (social-related fMRI task) and I4 (healthy adult sample reported). However, the NeuroStore record and reported analyses show only group-by-condition interactions and between-group contrasts fit and inferred over the whole brain (e.g., omnibus between-group contrast), and the abstract/analyses report differences between suicide attempters, depressed non-attempters, and healthy controls. There is no evidence in the document of an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task-evoked map or within-group contrast reported explicitly for the healthy/control group (I5 not met). Because the paper appears to report only between-group contrasts/interactions without a clearly identified whole-brain healthy-group task effect, exclusion criterion E4 applies. Therefore the study is excluded.

The study reports task-based fMRI during emotional face processing (a social perception task), with a within-group contrast for fear in healthy adults (n=10, mean age 25). NeuroStore indicates the model was fit and inference performed over the whole brain with voxelwise FDR-thresholded results and coordinates reported (peaks in tables). Thus it meets I3 (social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task effect clearly from healthy group), and I6 (results reported as tables of coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; ICA was applied to task data but whole-brain task effects are reported).

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adults performing social-comparison judgments (self vs known others on height and intelligence), satisfying the review’s focus on social-related processing. Participants are adults (mean age 29.7, within 18–65) and results are reported as group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects contrasts (height > intelligence; intelligence > height) with corrected inference and reported peak coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). The NeuroStore record appears to contain the necessary whole-brain task activation results for the healthy group. Full text is available in the record (no access notice).

This study uses task-based fMRI during a social decision-making task (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma with cooperation/competition framing), with healthy adult participants (n=14, mean age 30.5). The paper reports a within-group, whole-brain, voxelwise contrast (cooperate > defect) with whole-brain inference (cluster-level FWE) and reported peak coordinates, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study investigates self-referential (social) processing in healthy adults (I3 met) and includes healthy adult groups reported separately (I4 met). However, it does not report any whole-brain, task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group. The task-related analysis reported is a PPI (effective connectivity) that was restricted to ROIs (vMPFC–precuneus) and the other reported whole-brain results are resting-state seed-based connectivity analyses, not task-evoked activation maps. Therefore Inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain task-evoked healthy-group map) is not met. This meets exclusion criterion E3 (studies reporting only seed-based/effective connectivity or resting-state analyses without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map).

The study is excluded because it does not provide a whole-brain, voxelwise healthy-group task activation map. It reports only between-group contrasts (HC > BD) and inference is restricted to a region-of-interest. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (only between-group contrasts reported without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect) and E2 (ROI-restricted inference with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related self/other-reflection task). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no clear reporting of healthy-group whole-brain results reported separately) and I5 (no whole-brain, voxelwise healthy-group task map reported). Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

The study meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) It uses task-based fMRI during a social-related Self-Referential Judgment Task (self, friend, celebrity judgments). (I4) The sample is healthy adults (n=37, mean age 22.9, within 18–65). (I5) It reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., Self > Celebrity; Friend > Celebrity) with whole-brain inference. (I6) Results are reported as peaks/coordinates (tables) and clearly described. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity-only analyses, and are within the adult age range. Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED.

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adults performing a social cognition task (judging appropriateness of facial affect; ToM-related), meeting the review objective. Participants are healthy adults (n=14, ages 19–27), satisfying the sample criterion. The analyses were whole-brain random-effects voxelwise GLM results (model fit over whole brain) with reported contrasts and peak coordinates (Talairach) in tables, meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement; reporting in tables is acceptable. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, ages are within 18–65, and this is empirical fMRI data. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it used fMRI during an explicitly social task (Ultimatum Game) assessing memory for social partners (I3). The sample is healthy adults (n=16, mean age 19.9) within the 18–65 range (I4). The report contains group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (POS>NEG and NEG>POS) with model fit and inference performed over the whole brain and peak coordinates reported (I5). Reporting of coordinates/peaks in the table satisfies acceptable reporting formats (I6). No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only), and participants are within the eligible age range. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study uses fMRI during a social-related emotion-regulation task (I3) and includes a healthy adult group (I4). However, NeuroStore’s extraction lists only between-group contrasts/interactions and SPM interaction maps (healthy > patients, patients > healthy, and double-difference interaction maps). There is no clearly identified unmasked, whole-brain task activation map reported for the healthy/control group alone (no within-group healthy whole-brain contrast provided). Therefore this paper meets exclusion E4 (only between-group contrasts/interactions reported without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain healthy-group task map reported). Full text appears complete in the provided record.

a) Exclusion ID met: E4 (study reports only between-group contrasts/interactions or group-specific effects masked by the interaction without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task map). The NeuroStore record shows control-group results are reported only as effects masked by the group×(contrast) interaction (e.g., CON: own>unknown masked by group×(own>unknown); group-specific effects masked by group×facial emotion). b) Inclusion IDs met: I3 (uses task-based fMRI of social-related processing: emotional face recognition of own vs unknown child) and I4 (includes at least one group of healthy adult participants—the non-maltreated mothers are reported as a control group with no current mental disorder). c) Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (no clear, unmasked, whole-brain group-level task-evoked map identified as coming from the healthy/control group; reported whole-brain results for groups are masked by interaction or reported as between-group contrasts). Therefore the study must be excluded per E4.

Although this fMRI study used a social task (multi-round Trust Game) so I3 (social-related task) is satisfied and it included a healthy control group, the paper as represented here reports only between-group contrasts (control > patients) from whole-brain voxelwise analyses and does not report any unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation maps explicitly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Therefore it fails the requirement for healthy-group whole-brain evidence (I5) and does not meet the requirement that clinical studies report healthy-group results separately (I4). This matches exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts reported without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears available for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study uses fMRI during a social-related Theory-of-Mind task (satisfies I3) and reports a healthy participant group (satisfies I4). However, the NeuroStore record only reports region-of-interest analyses (model fit over: region of interest) for a between-group interaction (PP > HC for HI > LI) and does not report any unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group. Therefore it fails I5 (no whole-brain healthy-group task effect reported) and meets exclusion criteria E2 (ROI-only results with no whole-brain results) and E4 (reports only between-group/interaction contrast without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group effect). Based on these violations the study is excluded.

This study examines social processing (cross-modal person recognition) in healthy adults (n=16, ages 20–31), so I3 and I4 are satisfied. However, although several analyses were estimated over the whole brain, all reported task-evoked activation results are explicitly inference-restricted to predefined regions-of-interest (right OFA, right FFA, right aTL, and voice-sensitive STS), and many reported results are seed-based PPI connectivity analyses. The record does not report any unmasked, group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map (i.e., whole-brain inference results) for the healthy group. Therefore the study reports only ROI (and seed-based connectivity) results without a whole-brain task-evoked map and fails to meet I5, triggering exclusion under E2.

The study involved healthy adult participants (n=21) and used fMRI during tasks that relate to social processing (participants encoded and later retrieved life events involving a social interaction) — so inclusion criteria I3 and I4 are met. However, the reported imaging results indicate the model was fit over the whole brain but statistical inference was restricted to a region-of-interest (posterior hippocampus) using small-volume correction, with only ROI peak(s) reported. The paper does not report an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy group. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only reporting). Excluded for not reporting whole-brain task-evoked results (I5 not met; E2 met).

The study reports task-based fMRI during a socially-relevant joint action (leader/follower partnered dance interaction), satisfying the social-task requirement. Participants are described as healthy skilled leaders and followers (recruited dancers), and group-level analyses are reported for these healthy participant groups (within-group contrasts for leaders and followers, and cross-subject regressions), satisfying the sample requirement and healthy-group reporting. All reported analyses were whole-brain (model fit and inference over whole brain) with tables of reported peak coordinates and cluster-level correction, satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement; results are reported in coordinate tables (acceptable per I6). Although exact ages are not listed in the extracted record, the participants are described as adult dancers (recruited leaders/followers), so I4 is considered met based on the provided document. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, age-outside-range, or non-empirical) are triggered by the provided information.

This fMRI study uses a social-related humor/contingency task (participants elicit/listen to laughter; self vs other conditions) in a healthy adult sample (n=38; mean age 21.2, within 18–65). The paper reports multiple group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task activation contrasts and inferences (e.g., Analysis 28477977_analysis_2, 3, 4, 5, 6 report whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference with FWE cluster-level thresholding and reported peak coordinates/tables). Thus it meets I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply because the study is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group whole-brain activations, and is empirical with healthy adults. Full text is available in the provided record.

This study meets all inclusion criteria. It used fMRI during a social-related task (Facial Emotion Recognition) assessing perception of others and emotion (I3). The sample consists of healthy adult participants aged 21–33 (n=21 males), meeting the age and healthy-group requirement (I4). The NeuroStore record indicates whole-brain model fit and reports group-level, voxelwise results (reported peaks, MNI coordinates, voxel-level threshold p<0.001) for within-group contrasts and cross-subject regressions, providing whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps from the healthy group (I5). Coordinates/peaks are reported in the record, which is acceptable (I6). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, out-of-range age, or only between-group contrasts) are met. Full text is available in the record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study reports task-based fMRI during a social interaction (Gaze Perception / Joint Attention task) with a within-group contrast (task A > task B), meeting the review’s social-related task requirement. Participants: n=19 (12 F, 7 M) with observational cohort assignment and no clinical group reported, satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion (I4) as presented in the document. The model was fit over the whole brain and group-level paired t-test GLM results (voxelwise) are reported with peak coordinates in a table; thus the paper provides whole-brain, group-level task-evoked activation maps (I5/I6). No ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range age, or non-empirical exclusions apply. Confidence is slightly reduced because exact ages (18–65) are not explicitly listed in the extracted record, but the cohort is described as healthy adults and the sample size and sex distribution are reported. Therefore include.

This study used task-based fMRI during a clearly social-evaluative emotion task (videos of posers delivering positive/negative/neutral social statements), included a healthy adult sample (n=37, mean age 24.8 within 18–65), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (negative>neutral, positive>neutral, conjunction) with whole-brain inference and FWE correction and tables of reported peaks. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, and empirical fMRI data present).

The study reports task-based fMRI of social-related processing (self-referential and social stimulus judgments), with healthy adult participants (n=28; age range 30–50). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (model fit and inference over whole brain; FDR-corrected threshold; tables of peak coordinates for within-group contrasts: self-referential > social, social > self-referential, conjunction), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within 18–65, empirical fMRI data). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This fMRI study investigates social vs non-social semantic judgments (stereotypes vs object knowledge), using tasks that probe understanding of others (social cognition). Participants are healthy adults (n=19; ages 19–28), satisfying the sample age criterion. NeuroStore indicates group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM analyses with inference over the whole brain for multiple within-group contrasts (social>non-social, non-social>social, person>object, object>person) and reports peak coordinates/tables, meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. Results are reported as cluster-thresholded whole-brain maps and coordinate tables. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or between-group-only, participants within age range, empirical fMRI data present). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is eligible for inclusion.

The study meets all inclusion criteria: it used task fMRI during an empathy task (social-related processing) with BOLD measures and contrasts assessing empathic responses (I3). The sample comprises 32 healthy adult participants (mean age 19.9, within 18–65) (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (multiple analyses explicitly state ‘Inference over: whole brain’, with coordinates reported in tables and MNI space), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5,I6). Several within-group contrasts (empathize/watch/memorize vs neutral and their conjunctions) are reported as whole-brain GLM random-effects results. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, empirical fMRI data present). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study used fMRI during a social-related task (passive viewing of face images vs scenes) in a healthy adult sample (n=44, ages 18–32). The NeuroStore record indicates group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (Faces > Scenes and Scenes > Faces) with reported peak coordinates (Tables), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Although the paper also reports ICA-based network synchrony analyses, the presence of unmasked, within-group whole-brain activation contrasts for the healthy participants meets the inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria are met.

The study reports only seed-based functional connectivity and resting-state connectivity analyses and between-group contrasts (patients vs controls) without presenting any unmasked, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map from the healthy/control group. Therefore it does not provide the required healthy-group whole-brain task activation results. Exclusion criteria E3 (only seed-based/resting-state/connectivity analyses without healthy-group whole-brain task map) and E4 (only between-group contrasts/interactions without accompanying unmasked healthy-group task effect) are met. Inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task—ToM/humor processing) and I4 (healthy adult participants reported) are met; I5 (healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked map) is not met. Full text appears complete for screening.

The study reports task-based fMRI of action observation (mirror system) relevant to ‘Perception and Understanding of Others’ (social-related processing). Participants: healthy adult group (n=10) reported; no indication of clinical or out-of-range ages. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, within-group task contrasts (model fit and inference over whole brain, voxelwise corrected; reported peak tables). Thus it provides whole-brain healthy-group task activation maps meeting the meta-analysis requirements. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Full text is available as a NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study reports task-based fMRI of self-face recognition, which falls under social-related processing (Perception/Understanding of Self). Participants are healthy adults (n=16, ages 19–24). NeuroStore extraction indicates group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (Model fit over: whole brain; Inference over: whole brain) with FWE cluster-level correction and reported peaks, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked maps. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, empirical fMRI data present). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED.

The study is excluded because it does not report an unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task activation map (I5 not met). While the task is social (empathy-related face processing) and a healthy adult control group is included (I3 and I4 met), all reported whole-brain voxelwise results are for a between-group interaction (Analysis 25572160_analysis_0) rather than a within-group/main-effect map for the healthy controls, and the other critical results are ROI-restricted (Analyses 1–3). This meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Therefore the paper must be excluded from the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (whole-brain healthy-group evidence).

The study used task-based fMRI of social evaluation in healthy adults (meets I3 and I4). However, all reported analyses were region-of-interest (vACC ROI) with inference restricted to that ROI using small-volume correction; no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps are reported. Therefore it fails I5 and meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only results).

Exclusion: E2 applies — all reported analyses were region-of-interest (model fit and inference restricted to ROI with small-volume FWE correction) and no whole-brain (voxelwise) healthy-group task activation map is reported. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task is an fMRI social-related Empathy for Pain task using face/social stimuli) and I4 (healthy adult sample, n≈73–74, mean age ~23). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map from the healthy/control group was reported). Therefore the study must be excluded because it lacks whole-brain results required by the review.

Meets all inclusion criteria: The study uses task-based fMRI of social-cognitive/mentalizing processes (watching others play bowling; false-belief task), includes a healthy adult sample (n=22; ages 18–28), and reports group-level, whole-brain within-group task contrasts (Unexpected > Expected and False Belief > False Photograph) with whole-brain inference. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within 18–65, empirical fMRI data present).

The study reports task-based fMRI (BOLD) during a social cognition task (False Belief mentalising stories) in healthy adult participants (n=17, mean age 22), satisfying the sample criterion. NeuroStore indicates whole-brain model fitting and whole-brain inference with reported group-level contrasts (mentalising > factual and parametric modulations) and tables of peak coordinates, meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. Results are clearly from the healthy/control group and not limited to ROIs or connectivity-only analyses. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study investigates social-emotional action control using fMRI in a healthy adult sample (meets I3 and I4). However, although the model was fit over the whole brain, inference was explicitly restricted to a region-of-interest with FWE small-volume correction and reported only ROI-thresholded peaks. The paper therefore reports ROI-constrained results without an unmasked/whole-brain, voxelwise healthy-group task activation map (no whole-brain results reported). This meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only results). Inclusion criteria I5 (reported whole-brain group-level task-evoked statistical map) and I6 (acceptable reporting of whole-brain results in tables/figures/supplement) are not satisfied.

Excluded because the reported analyses are restricted to predefined anatomical ROIs (model fit and inference restricted to ROI), and no whole-brain (voxelwise) healthy-group task activation map is reported. Exclusion criteria met: E2 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related face/emotional processing task) and I4 (healthy adult control group reported separately). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain group-level healthy/control voxelwise map reported). NeuroStore extraction explicitly lists 'Model fit over: region of interest' and 'Inference restricted to: region of interest' for all analyses, indicating absence of unmasked whole-brain healthy-group results. Full text is complete for screening purposes.

The study reports whole-brain, between-group contrasts (control > ASC) but does not present an unmasked, whole-brain task activation map for the healthy/control group alone. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task — emotion-word/affective language processing) and I4 (healthy adult participants included). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no clearly identified whole-brain group-level task map for the healthy/control group). Exclusion criterion met: E4 (reports only between-group contrast without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). fulltext_incomplete=false

This study investigates gesture-speech integration (a social communication task) using fMRI and includes healthy adult controls; however, the NeuroStore record does not report a standalone, unmasked whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group. Reported whole-brain analyses consist of a conjunction (overlap of control and patient groups for the integration contrast) and an omnibus between-group effect. Therefore the paper lacks a clearly identified healthy-group whole-brain task effect required by the review. Exclusion based on E4 (only between-group contrasts/conjunction without an accompanying unmasked healthy-group whole-brain task map). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult group present). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no separate whole-brain healthy-group task map reported).

Exclusion based on inclusion criterion I4: the study does not report a separate group of healthy adult participants (18–65). The sample is mixed-age (n=38, ages 10–22) with no adult subgroup analysis, so it does not satisfy the requirement for a distinct adult group. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts with whole-brain inference and coordinate tables) and I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables/coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no separately analyzed healthy adult group), and I3 is not clearly satisfied from the document (the task is emotion regulation of IAPS images and is not explicitly described as a social-related task). Exclusion criteria met: none ([]) . Full text is complete for purposes of this review (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. I3: The task is social (Reading the Mind in the Eyes; gaze/intention processing), so it assesses social-related processing. I4: A neurologically normal/healthy participant group is reported separately (n=9, mean age 23.4), satisfying the requirement for a healthy adult group; although the reported age range includes a minimum of 15.5 years, the healthy group is reported separately and centered in adulthood, so I judged it to meet the criterion. I5: The paper reports a whole-brain, voxelwise within-group contrast (incongruent > congruent) for the healthy group (model fit over whole brain; reported peaks in Table 1). I6: Whole-brain results are provided as coordinate peaks. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult-only sample) are met. Minor uncertainty about one participant <18 is noted but not sufficient to exclude given separate healthy-group whole-brain reporting.

The study used fMRI in a social task with healthy adult participants (I3 and I4 met). However, all reported statistical inferences were restricted to a region-of-interest using small-volume correction (inference restricted to ROI; voxel-level SVC). Although the model was fit over the whole brain, no unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation maps or whole-brain voxelwise inferences for the healthy group are reported. This meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only results) and fails inclusion criterion I5 (no whole-brain evidence). Therefore the paper is excluded.

The study uses task fMRI of social stimuli (fearful/calm faces), satisfying I3. It includes a separately reported healthy adult group (n=10, ages 26–55), satisfying I4. A group-level, whole-brain, within-group task contrast for the healthy/control participants is reported (Calm > scrambled control; Analysis 17166860_analysis_1) with peaks listed in Table 3, satisfying I5. The NeuroStore record indicates whole-brain model fit and reports peaks in tables, which meets I6 (table/coordinate reporting acceptable). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not only connectivity/resting-state, and a healthy-group whole-brain map is present. Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

The study reports an fMRI Self-Referential Encoding Task (social-related: perception/understanding of self and others). A healthy adult group is reported separately (n=28; mean age 21.6). Whole-brain voxelwise models were fit and a within-group (one-sample t-test) contrast for the healthy group (Self>Other) is reported with peak coordinates (Table 2) and cluster-corrected thresholds. Thus it meets all required inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

Study includes healthy adult participants (I4) and uses an fMRI task involving social influence from an expert (social-related processing) satisfying I3. However, the reported whole-brain results are focused on between-group (developmental/age) contrasts and correlations (age effects; EA > AD contrast) rather than an unmasked, whole-brain task activation map reported specifically for the healthy adult group. Thus it fails I5. This meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group/interaction effects without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Therefore exclude. Key points: inclusion met: I3, I4; inclusion not met: I5; exclusion met: E4.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: I3—uses task-based fMRI during a Social Evaluative Feedback Task involving social feedback; I4—reports a healthy adult sample (n=21 males, age 21–39); I5—reports at least one group-level, whole-brain voxelwise within-group contrast for the healthy group (placebo: negative social feedback > positive social feedback) with inference over the whole brain (FWE cluster-level) and reported peaks; I6—results are reported in tables of coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes a within-group whole-brain effect, participants are within 18–65, and this is empirical fMRI data). Full text appears available in the extracted record.

The paper reports an fMRI social attribution task (meets I3) and includes a healthy adult control group (meets I4). However, all reported statistical maps in the NeuroStore record are between-group interaction contrasts (controls vs patients) rather than unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effects. No clear group-level, whole-brain task activation map explicitly identified as coming from the healthy/control group (e.g., a within-group control > baseline map) is reported. Therefore exclusion criterion E4 is met (only between-group contrasts/interactions reported without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion I5 is not satisfied. Conclusion: EXCLUDE under E4.

Excluded because the paper reports only region-of-interest analyses and does not present any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map from the healthy group. Exclusion criterion met: E2 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task — Ultimatum Game/negotiation), I4 (healthy adult sample reported; mean age 19.86). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain evidence reported; model fit was over an ROI and results are ROI-averaged correlations). fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study examines processing of facial expressions (a social-perception task) and includes a separately reported healthy adult control group, so it meets I3 (social-related fMRI task) and I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately). However, all reported analyses were fit and inferred within a region-of-interest (insula/amygdala) rather than as whole-brain, voxelwise group-level maps for the healthy/control group. Therefore it does NOT meet I5 (whole-brain evidence). Because the paper reports only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results, exclusion criterion E2 applies. Conclusion: EXCLUDED because E2 is met; inclusion criteria met: I3 and I4; inclusion criterion not met: I5.

The study used an fMRI facial-emotion task in healthy adults (meets I3 and I4) but all reported analyses were region-of-interest (model fit over and inference restricted to ROI as stated). No group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for the healthy group is reported; thus it fails inclusion criterion I5. Therefore exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) applies. Sample: healthy adults (n≈30, mean age 23.9).

The study reports an event-related fMRI task that is clearly social (associating faces with praise/criticism about others vs objects), meeting the review’s social-processing requirement. The sample is 30 healthy adults (age 20–25, 15F/15M), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. Crucially, group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts are reported: main effects of valence and target have inference over the whole brain with FWE peak-level thresholding, and whole-brain model fitting is stated for multiple contrasts; coordinates/peaks are reported. Connectivity ROI analyses are also present but are supplemented by whole-brain activation results. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state/only connectivity, includes within-group whole-brain maps, participants are within 18–65, and it is empirical). Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

The study reports fMRI during a social task (vicarious embarrassment; perspective-taking), includes a healthy adult sample (n=43, mean age ~24), and provides multiple group-level whole-brain task activation analyses (e.g., Analyses 3,4,5,6 report model fit and inference over the whole brain, with reported peaks and Table 3). Whole-brain results are clearly from the healthy group. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply.

The NeuroStore record reports only between-group interaction contrasts (Analyses 1 and 2: 'interaction, between-group') with whole-brain model fitting, but does not report any group-level, unmasked whole-brain task-evoked maps (e.g., main effect or within-group contrasts) clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The localizer/ROI selection is mentioned but no whole-brain healthy-group activation map is provided. Therefore the study meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria I3 (social-related task: dynamic facial expression processing) and I4 (healthy adult sample reported) are satisfied; I5 (whole-brain healthy-group task map) is not met. Full text appears available in the record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study uses fMRI during a social-related (attachment) task and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task results. However, the participant sample is not clearly a healthy adult group: NeuroStore labels participants as 'patients', half the sample had a history of perinatal major depressive episode, and some mothers were taking SSRIs. No separate results for a healthy/control subgroup are reported. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (social-related fMRI task), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise results), I6 (acceptable reporting of whole-brain results). No exclusion criteria from the list are explicitly met. Conclusion: EXCLUDE because I4 not satisfied.

The study uses task-based fMRI during a social learning task (representational similarity analysis of social memory for faces), meeting the social processing requirement. The sample is healthy adults (n=22, ages 18–34) meeting the age/sample criterion. The analysis reports group-level searchlight (whole-brain voxelwise) RSA results with FWE-corrected TFCE and provides peak coordinates (Table t2), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain evidence and allowing coordinate-based reporting. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion.

The study uses fMRI with social stimuli (emotional faces) and reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps for the healthy/control group, but the healthy group includes minors (age range reported 12–23) and no healthy adult (18–65) group is reported separately. Therefore inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I5 (whole-brain healthy-group results), and I6 (results reported as coordinates/tables) are satisfied, but I4 (at least one group of healthy adult participants aged 18–65 reported separately) is NOT satisfied. No exclusion criteria from the protocol are triggered. Because I4 is not met, the study is excluded.

The study reports fMRI of social cognition (ToM/empathy) but the NeuroStore record lists only patient participants (n=44) and the reported functional results are between-group/ROI-masked contrasts (diagnosis effects, controls>patients, ROI-restricted regressions). There is no clearly reported unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for a healthy/control group in the document. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criteria I4 (healthy adult group results reported separately) and I5 (a whole-brain healthy-group task map). It meets I3 (functional MRI during a social-related task). It thus satisfies exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group/interaction or ROI-masked results without an unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect).

The study investigates emotion processing (a social-related task) in healthy adult participants (unaffected siblings and controls) satisfying I3 and I4. However, the NeuroStore record shows only a between-group interaction/contrast (siblings > controls) reported at the whole-brain level; there is no accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task activation map (e.g., a within-group or main-effect map for the healthy/control group). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrast/interaction without a healthy-group whole-brain task effect). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Full text appears complete for the purposes of screening.

The study is excluded because it reports only seed-based task-related functional connectivity and between-group contrasts/regressions without any group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation map for the healthy/control group. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (only seed-based connectivity reported without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map) and E4 (reports primarily between-group contrasts/interactions without an unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses fMRI during a social-related task) and I4 (includes a healthy adult group reported separately). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain, healthy-group task activation map reported).

This study is excluded because it does not report a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map for the healthy adult sample; the NeuroStore record contains only region-of-interest and seed-based connectivity (gPPI) results. Exclusion criteria met: E2 (reports only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) and E3 (reports only seed-based/effective connectivity without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses fMRI during a social-related false-belief / perspective-taking task) and I4 (healthy adult sample, ages 18–34, n=36; subgroup n=25 reported for the connectivity analysis). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map reported). I6 is therefore not satisfied (no whole-brain results to be reported in any format). fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study used fMRI during a social trust task (iterated Trust Game) examining reputation-related neural signals, meeting I3. The sample is healthy adults (n=29, mean age 30), meeting I4. The paper reports a group-level, whole-brain within-subjects omnibus contrast for reputation during decision-making (Analysis 23922638_analysis_5: model fit and inference over whole brain, cluster-corrected), satisfying I5 and the allowance in I6. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical issues). Full text is available in the provided record, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

The NeuroStore record shows the task is social (Reading the Mind in the Eyes) and healthy control participants are included, but all reported whole-brain results are between-group contrasts/interactions (main effects of ALC, schizophrenia, SZ×ALC interaction, omnibus between-group). No unmasked, whole-brain within-healthy-group task activation map (e.g., healthy MSA > gender or main effect within controls) is reported. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3 and I4 but does not meet I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group/interaction results reported).

The study reports fMRI during a Theory-of-Mind (social) task (False Belief Task), satisfying social-related processing. Participants are described as n=188 healthy German volunteers assessed with SCID-I (healthy, non-affected), indicating a healthy adult sample. The paper reports a group-level, whole-brain within-group contrast (ToM > control): Model fit and inference were performed over the whole brain, with voxelwise FWE correction and reported peak coordinates (Table 3). This constitutes a whole-brain task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group. Results are reported as peaks/tables, which is acceptable. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants are healthy adults, and it is empirical). Note: age range (18–65) is not explicitly listed in this document, but use of SCID-I and description as healthy volunteers supports interpretation as an adult sample; confidence reflects this minor uncertainty.

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adults using an auditory semantic-priming task that addresses perception/understanding of others' actions (social-related processing). The sample is healthy adults (n=11, ages 21–29). Analyses were fit over the whole brain and inference was performed over the whole brain; group-level within-subject contrasts and peak coordinates are reported (tables of peaks), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked results. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

The study uses fMRI of a social-related task (empathy for pain) and reports multiple whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task effects. However, the participant sample spans ages 7–40 and the paper does not report a separate adult-only (18–65) group or group-level results restricted to adults. Inclusion criterion I4 requires at least one group of healthy adult participants (age 18–65) analyzed and reported separately. Therefore the study does not meet all inclusion criteria and must be excluded.

The study includes an emotional face-matching task (meets I3) and reports healthy control participants (meets I4). However, the NeuroStore record does not report any whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical map identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The reported task results are between-group contrasts (patient > control or control > patient) and the paper additionally reports seed-based resting-state connectivity analyses. Therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I5 (no healthy-group whole-brain task map) and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect).

This fMRI study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. Task: implicit emotional face processing (socially relevant perception of others) satisfies I3. Participants: healthy adults (n=31; ages 18–35) satisfy I4. The NeuroStore extraction reports whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference with voxelwise contrasts and reported peak coordinates for within-group task contrasts (before > after; after > before), satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, include within-group whole-brain activation maps for the healthy sample, and participants are within the eligible age range. Full text appears complete in the provided record. Therefore include.

This fMRI study uses a social-related task (facial attractiveness judgments) in healthy adults (n=26). The NeuroStore record indicates whole-brain model fitting and reports a group-level whole-brain contrast (attractiveness judgment > age judgment) with Gaussian random field corrected p<0.05 and reported peaks (Table tbl1), satisfying the requirement for a healthy-group, whole-brain task-evoked map. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise results), and I6 (results reported clearly). No exclusion criteria apply.

This study does not meet the review inclusion criteria. It used a Simon (cognitive control) task, not a social-related task (I3 not met). The sample consists of patients with schizophrenia and treatment groups; no healthy adult group results are reported separately (I4 not met). The paper does not report any whole-brain, group-level task-evoked activation map for a healthy/control group (I5 not met). Instead, reported analyses are ROI-based activation and seed-based connectivity/interaction effects in patients (between-group treatment x time interactions). Therefore exclusion criteria E3 (reports only seed-based connectivity/task-based connectivity without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map) and E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect) apply. No inclusion criteria are satisfied.

Although the study used task fMRI during a social task (watching The Office) and included a healthy control group, the NeuroStore record reports only a between-group (NT > ASD) whole-brain contrast. No unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group alone is reported in the extracted analyses. Therefore it fails the requirement for reporting a healthy-group whole-brain task effect. Exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect) applies. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) and I4 (includes a healthy/control group). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no clearly identified whole-brain group-level task-evoked map for the healthy/control group).

This study is excluded because it reports only region-of-interest results in a clinical (currently depressed) patient group and does not provide whole-brain task activation results from a healthy adult group. (a) Exclusion IDs met: E2 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). (b) Inclusion IDs met: I3 (uses fMRI during a social-related task: masked facial expressions). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I4 (no healthy adult group results reported; only depressed patients are described) and I5 (no group-level whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked map reported). Full-text is available in the NeuroStore record and no other exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports task-based fMRI of empathy/emotion attribution (social cognition), with healthy adult participants (n=26, mean age ~24.4). Critically, it reports group-level whole-brain task activation contrasts for the healthy sample (SELF > baseline and OTHER > baseline) with voxelwise FWE-corrected inference and tables of peaks. Results are clearly described for the healthy group. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adults), I5 (whole-brain group-level task maps), and I6 (reported as tables/peaks). No exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because the paper reports only ROI-restricted inference (small-volume correction; "Inference restricted to: region of interest"), indicating no unmasked whole-brain group-level task activation map was reported — meets exclusion E2. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (healthy adult sample, n=23, ages within 18–65). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (the task is an emotional memory/recall task for sporting events and does not clearly operationalize a social-related task such as affiliation/communication or perception/understanding of self/others), and I5 (no whole-brain voxelwise healthy-group task results are reported; inference was restricted to ROIs with SVC). Therefore the study must be excluded.

The study meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) it used fMRI during a social-related Theory-of-Mind task; (I4) the sample consists of 109 healthy adult participants; (I5) it reports a group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise within-group analysis (cross-subject regression of ToM > control with inference over the whole brain, FDR-corrected, with reported peak coordinates); (I6) whole-brain results are presented as peak coordinates/tables. No exclusion criteria apply: this is not an ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-groups-only, outside-age-range, or non-empirical paper. Note: the reported whole-brain map is a cross-subject regression on risk-allele dose rather than a simple task main effect, but it is a group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map from the healthy sample and thus qualifies under I5.

The study used fMRI during an autobiographical task involving participant-generated social situations (embarrassment, shame, humiliation) and negative self-beliefs, satisfying the social-related task requirement. The sample consists of 35 healthy adults aged 22.6–55.4 (within 18–65). Multiple group-level, whole-brain voxelwise within-group contrasts are reported (model fit and inference over whole brain; tables of peak coordinates and cluster thresholds are provided), meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. Results are reported for the healthy/control group and appear as tables of coordinates and cluster-corrected maps. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy adult group, empirical fMRI data). Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and none of the exclusion criteria.

Study reports task-evoked BOLD fMRI during a social perception task (judging biological vs artificial actions; engages mentalizing/motor resonance networks). Participants are healthy adults (n=12, mean age 27.3). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses are reported (model fit over: whole brain; t-tests/factorial RFX; reported peak coordinates), satisfying whole-brain evidence—reported peaks/contrasts correspond to within-group effects. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied.

The study reports task-based fMRI of social cognition (mentalizing about groups and individuals), satisfying I3. The sample is healthy adults (n=14, ages 18–23), satisfying I4. Critically, the paper reports a group-level, whole-brain multivariate searchlight analysis with inference over the whole brain and cluster-level thresholding (Monte Carlo; voxelwise p<0.005; cluster extent reported), which constitutes a voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked map, satisfying I5 (and acceptable per I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not between-group-only, age within range, and empirical fMRI data present). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

This study reports task-based fMRI of social perception (perceiving emotionally expressive targets) in healthy adults.
