Participants are adults (mean age 19.1, SD 1.72) and results are reported for the healthy group (n=16). The NeuroStore record indicates whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference with voxelwise contrasts and reported coordinate peaks/tables (multiple within-group contrasts and parametric modulations). Thresholding and cluster reporting are described, satisfying reporting of whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy adults, empirical fMRI task data). Therefore the paper meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This fMRI study used an Ultimatum Game paradigm manipulating facial trustworthiness (a social decision-making task), satisfying I3. Participants are healthy adults (mean age 23.4 within 18–65), satisfying I4. The NeuroStore record reports group-level voxelwise analyses fit over the whole brain (e.g., Analysis 21942764_analysis_1: model fit over whole brain, voxel-level threshold p<0.001) and other whole-brain fits with reported peaks, satisfying I5. Results/peaks are reported (tables/coordinates/peaks), satisfying I6. No exclusion criteria apply: the paper reports whole-brain task-evoked maps (not only ROI or only connectivity), and participants are within the target age range. Full text appears available in the provided record (no access issue).

The study reports task-based fMRI during an interactive task requiring participants to adapt communicated confidence to social context (social communication/social context processing), satisfying the social-related task requirement. Sample is healthy adults (n=28, mean age 26.36, within 18–65). Multiple group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses are reported (one-sample t-tests against 0; inference over whole brain; cluster-level FWE; reported peak tables), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement; results are reported in tables/figures (inlinetable1–3), meeting reporting acceptance. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not only between-group contrasts, age appropriate, empirical data).

This study meets all inclusion criteria. I3: Task involves social processing (learning about another’s values, choices for self vs familiar/novel other; agent cues; social influence on preferences). I4: Sample comprises healthy adults (n=27, mean age 25.6, SD 5.6). I5: Reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (model fit over whole brain; inference over whole brain) with reported peak coordinates for multiple contrasts. I6: Whole-brain results are reported as peak coordinates/peaks. No exclusion criteria are met (whole-brain results present; not ROI-only; not connectivity/resting-only; healthy adult group analyzed). Full text appears complete for the purposes of screening.

The study uses fMRI during a social task (Social Incentive Delay), and includes healthy adult participants, but it does not report any unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation maps for the healthy/control group alone. All reported whole-brain results are between-group contrasts/interactions (HC > BPD or interactions) and the only within-group/condition x group effects that are reported for the healthy group are limited to an ROI (bilateral amygdala). Therefore it fails the requirement for a healthy-group whole-brain task map. Exclusion criterion E4 applies (only between-group contrasts/interactions reported without an unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion met: I3. Inclusion not met: I4 (healthy-group results not reported separately as required when clinical groups are included), I5 (no whole-brain healthy-group activation map).

The paper reports only between-group interaction contrasts (e.g., Adults > Children) and no unmasked, whole-brain task activation map for the healthy adult group. This violates exclusion criterion E4. Inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult group present) are met, but I5 (at least one whole-brain group-level healthy-group task activation map) is not met. Full text appears complete for screening.

This study uses task-based fMRI of social processes (mentalizing, empathy, prosocial behavior) in a healthy adult sample (n=32; mean age 22.7), satisfying I3 and I4. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (Painful > Non-Painful contrast) with whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference and reported peak coordinates, satisfying I5 (and I6 is acceptable). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants are within the 18–65 range, and the paper is empirical. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This fMRI study directly examines social-related processing using the Choose-a-Movie (CAM) task (social vs object stimuli) in a sample of healthy adults (n=24, ages 19–49). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses are reported (one-sample t-tests) with whole-brain inference and tabulated peak coordinates for multiple within-group contrasts (e.g., Social > Object, Object > Social, parametric effort effects). Reporting of whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts in tables/figures satisfies whole-brain evidence requirements. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task maps), and I6 (results reported via tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met.

The study uses fMRI during a social cognition task (Reading the Mind in the Eyes Test), meeting I3. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=29) screened for psychiatric/medical conditions, meeting I4. NeuroStore extraction reports a group-level, whole-brain model fit and voxelwise inference (model fit over: whole brain; reported peaks in Table 1; thresholding p<0.001), satisfying I5 and I6. Results are reported as coordinates/peaks. Although the contrast label includes ‘between-group’, the extracted model is a one-sample GLM (task condition) and whole-brain group maps/peaks are provided for the healthy sample, so no exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the paper should be included.

The study reports task-based fMRI during a self-referential judgment task (social cognitive: self representation), fulfilling I3. It includes a healthy sighted adult group (n=23, ages 18–28) reported separately from blind participants, fulfilling I4. Multiple group-level, whole-brain, within-group contrasts for the sighted/control group are reported (e.g., Analysis 21051474_analysis_0 and 1: model fit over = whole brain; inference over = whole brain; cluster-corrected), satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity-only, includes healthy adults within 18–65, empirical fMRI data).

This study does not meet the review’s social-task requirement (I3). Although it reports task-based fMRI in healthy adults (I4 satisfied: n=18, age 25.5) and provides whole-brain, voxelwise group results reported in tables/coordinates (I5 and I6 satisfied), the experimental task is sensorimotor synchronization to auditory pacing tones with a concurrent n-back working-memory task. The task involves tapping to tones (not explicit interaction with or perception of other people) and the authors’ speculative link to social-cognitive processes (e.g., resembling music performed by human agents) does not establish that the task was a social-related paradigm as required by I3. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5, I6. Inclusion criteria not met: I3. Full text appears complete for screening.

The study used fMRI during a social cognition (theory of mind/mentalizing) task, satisfying I3. It includes a healthy younger adult group with ages 18–33 reported separately (n=40), meeting I4. The NeuroStore record reports whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference and provides group-level within-group contrasts for the healthy (younger adult) group (e.g., YA false belief > false photo) with peak coordinates/tables, satisfying I5 and the acceptable reporting formats in I6. Thresholding and cluster/voxel-level whole-brain results are explicitly described. No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not ROI-only (E2), not connectivity/resting-state only (E3), not only between-group contrasts without healthy-group whole-brain effects (E4), and a healthy adult subgroup within 18–65 is present (no E5). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

The study reports task-based fMRI during social interactive video-based language learning (participants guessed word meanings from social videos), which constitutes social-related processing (I3). The sample is healthy adults (n=34; ages 19–25), meeting the age and health requirements (I4). NeuroStore indicates model fitting and inference were performed over the whole brain with group-level, voxelwise second-level one-sample t-tests and reported peak coordinates/tables (FWE cluster-level), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement and acceptable reporting formats (I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not limited to between-group contrasts, ages are within 18–65, and the paper is empirical. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

The study investigates perception of dynamic audio-visual emotional cues (a social-related task involving emotion perception/understanding of others), includes a healthy adult sample (n=10, ages 18–33), and reports group-level whole-brain task activation contrasts (multiple analyses specify 'Model fit over: whole brain' with voxelwise thresholds and reported peaks/tables). Coordinates are provided (Talairach). Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met because whole-brain results are reported for the healthy group and the sample age is within 18–65. Full text appears readable in this record, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

The study reports task-based fMRI during a social decision-making task (Public-good-game), with healthy adult participants (n=25, mean age 22.48). Multiple group-level, within-group whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses are reported (GLM1/GLM2/GLM3) with whole-brain inference (FWE cluster-level) and reported peak coordinates, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Reporting of peaks/coordinates fulfils acceptable reporting formats. No exclusion criteria are met (results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, include healthy adults in range, and are empirical). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study uses task-based fMRI of social interactions (Ultimatum Game and Prisoner’s Dilemma) engaging theory-of-mind processes, with BOLD measures and relevant social tasks (I3). It reports a healthy adult sample (n=19; age mean 21.8, SD 7.8), satisfying the sample requirement for healthy adults (I4). The paper includes group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., Analysis 15275925_analysis_2 and 15275925_analysis_3 are whole-brain one-sample GLM contrasts with voxel-level thresholds and reported peak coordinates), fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement (I5). Whole-brain results are reported as coordinate peaks/tables, which is acceptable (I6). No exclusion criteria apply: the study does not rely only on ROI analyses, connectivity/resting-state methods, only between-group contrasts, nor is it non-empirical. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This study uses task fMRI of social processing (Facial Emotion Recognition), and reports whole-brain coordinate results (meets I3 and I6). However, the sample (n=25, mean age 23.4) includes participants with Autism Spectrum Disorder (three HFA/AS participants) and all reported group-level, whole-brain analyses (including cross-subject regressions with EQ and conjunctions) appear to be performed across the full sample (n=25) rather than a healthy-only control group. The document provides no clear healthy/control-group-only whole-brain task maps. Therefore it does not meet I4 (healthy adult group results reported separately) and I5 (whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked map). No exclusion criteria from the list are explicitly triggered.

The study investigates social-related processing (fanaticism/affiliation) with healthy adult participants, but the NeuroStore extract shows only group-level between-group interactions/contrasts (fanatics vs non-fanatics) and seed-based connectivity. There is no evidence of an unmasked, whole-brain task-activation map reported for the healthy/control group alone. Therefore it fails the requirement for a healthy-group whole-brain task effect (I5) and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (social-related fMRI task) and I4 (healthy adult sample). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no healthy-group whole-brain task map); I6 (no qualifying whole-brain healthy-group results reported in any form). Full text appears complete.

This study reports task-based fMRI during social cognition (expectancy violations on warmth and competence) using BOLD in healthy adult participants (n=12, mean age 20.4). The NeuroStore record indicates whole-brain model estimation and whole-brain inference with voxelwise thresholding and tables of coordinate peaks for multiple within-group contrasts (warmth and competence violation and consistency contrasts). These fulfill the requirement for group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation maps reported for a healthy adult sample. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study reports task-based fMRI of social touch (manually administered and imagined massage), constituting a social-related task (I3). The sample is healthy adults (n=46, mean age 21.2, within 18–65) meeting the sample criterion (I4). The NeuroStore record states model fit and inference were performed over the whole brain and reports voxelwise peaks/tables (whole-brain, FDR-thresholded results), fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement (I5,I6). Reported contrasts include within-group/main effects (real > imagined, combined > rest) and oxytocin effects on neural activations, not limited to ROIs or connectivity-only analyses. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Therefore the paper should be included for the review.

Excluded because the study reports only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses restricted to bilateral amygdala with model fit and inference limited to the ROI, and does not provide any whole-brain (voxelwise) healthy-group task activation maps. Exclusion criteria met: E2 (ROI-only, no whole-brain results) and E4 (reports predominantly between-group contrasts/interactions without an unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task involves social processing of facial emotions) and I4 (includes healthy adult participants reported alongside patients). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map clearly identified for the healthy/control group). Full text appears complete in the provided record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This fMRI study investigates memory for neutral faces embedded in goal-relevant vs. goal-irrelevant situations, a social-perception task involving face identity and social/contextual processing (e.g., superior temporal sulcus activation). The sample is healthy adults (n=17, mean age 27.65, within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (analyses 30264337_analysis_0 and _1 report whole-brain inference and peaks; additional analyses include ROI/SVC but whole-brain results are present). Thus it meets the review objective and inclusion criteria for social-related fMRI in healthy adults and provides whole-brain task-evoked maps. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study investigates self- and other-related processing with fMRI in healthy adults (meets I3 and I4). However, the NeuroStore record does not report any group-level, whole-brain task activation map for the overall healthy sample (n=34) unconfined to a narrowly defined subgroup. Reported results are an ROI-restricted gene × interdependence interaction and multiple within-group (l/l carriers, n=17) cross-subject regressions (subgroup analyses). Therefore the paper does not provide the required whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked statistical map and fails inclusion criterion I5. No exclusion criteria from the list are strictly met (e.g., some whole-brain modeling is indicated, and results are not exclusively between-group contrasts), so exclusion is based on failure to satisfy I5.

The study used task-based fMRI of empathy (social processing) in healthy adult participants (n=20, mean age 26). It reports multiple group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (model fit and inference over whole brain; FWE thresholding) with peak coordinates and within-group contrasts (e.g., empathic vs. unempathic, feedback contrasts). Thus it satisfies the review objective and meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65 reported separately), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked voxelwise results), and I6 (results reported as tables of coordinates). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete for screening from the provided NeuroStore record.

This fMRI study investigates social perception (perception/understanding of others’ intentions) using an event-related reach-to-grasp task, satisfying the social-related task requirement. The sample is healthy adults (n=12; ages 19–28), meeting the age and healthy sample criterion. The paper reports multiple group-level, whole-brain voxelwise within-group contrasts (e.g., ‘incorrect’ simple effect with model fit over whole brain, reported peaks and thresholding), meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement; whole-brain results are presented in tables of peaks. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and participants are within 18–65). Therefore the study should be included.

This study acquired resting-state fMRI seed-based functional connectivity (amygdala subfields) with participants instructed to focus on a fixation cross, and the reported analyses are seed-based resting connectivity interactions (long-term stigma change × group; group × condition). It does not report any task-evoked, whole-brain activation map from a social-related task in the healthy group. Therefore it violates exclusion E3 (only seed-based/resting-state connectivity reported without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation) and also meets E4 (reports only between-group/interaction contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria: I4 (healthy adult sample) is met. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (functional MRI during a social-related task) and I5 (whole-brain task-evoked group-level map). Full text appears complete for the extracted data.

The study used fMRI with an emotional face-matching task (social processing) and included healthy adult control participants, so it meets I3. However, the NeuroStore record reports only a group×drug omnibus interaction and between-group contrasts (whole-brain interaction) and parameter estimates extracted from interaction clusters; it does not report an unmasked, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I4/I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group interaction without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete in the record.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) it used fMRI during a social-related Theory of Mind task (self/other mentalizing); (I4) it reports a healthy adult control group (n=33, ages 18–42); (I5) it reports a whole-brain, within-group control contrast (Controls Self > Other) with whole-brain model fit and inference; (I6) whole-brain results are clearly described (thresholding and reported peaks). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes a healthy-group whole-brain task map). Full text is complete in the provided record.

The study meets all inclusion requirements for the review. It uses fMRI during a social-related task (Approach-Avoidance Task with emotional faces), addressing perception/understanding of others (I3). The sample is a healthy adult group (n=40; ages 18–33), satisfying the sample criterion (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts for healthy participants (Analyses 32034069_analysis_0 and _1: model fit and inference over whole brain), meeting whole-brain evidence requirements (I5). Results are reported as peaks/coordinates consistent with acceptable reporting formats (I6). No exclusion criteria are met: whole-brain task activation maps are present (not ROI-only), the paper is empirical with healthy adults, and connectivity analyses do not replace the whole-brain task results. Full text appears complete for the needed fields.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI during a clearly social task (preference judgments about faces) (I3); reports results from a healthy adult sample with ages 23–51 (I4); provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation contrasts (model fit and inference over the whole brain, reported peak tables for Preference and Preference>Gender contrasts) (I5); and whole-brain results are reported in tables of coordinates (I6). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper includes whole-brain activation maps in addition to connectivity analyses, is not ROI-only, not resting-state/only connectivity, reports within-group healthy results, and participants are within 18–65. Therefore include.

Exclusion: E4 applies — the reported analyses are between-group contrasts/interactions (placebo vs oxytocin) and do not present an unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect or within-group/main-effect map. Inclusion met: I3 (uses a social task — Trust Game) and I4 (reports healthy participants). Inclusion not met: I5 (no clearly identified group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group separate from between-group contrasts). Full text appears complete for screening (no access or availability notice).

Study used task-based fMRI manipulating social competition (a social-related construct). Participants are healthy adults (n=20; ages 18–35). Multiple analyses report group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (model fit and inference over whole brain; Monte Carlo cluster correction; reported peak coordinates/tables). Thus it meets all inclusion criteria: I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I6 (results reported in tables/coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, empirical fMRI data).

This is an fMRI study of a social task (Trust Game) examining reciprocity, satisfying social-processing relevance. Participants are healthy adults (n=18; ages 18–22) meeting the sample criterion. The paper reports multiple group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts and regressions with whole-brain inference (e.g., defect>reciprocate, reciprocate>defect, cross-subject regressions) and reported peaks/tables, satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. One analysis used an ROI, but whole-brain results are also reported, so E2 does not apply. No exclusion criteria are met. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5, I6. Full text appears complete for the purposes of the screening record.

This fMRI study uses a social task (Cyberball) and reports BOLD results, so I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) is satisfied. However, the NeuroStore record shows only between-group interaction contrasts (support group vs no-support) with inference restricted to regions-of-interest using small-volume correction; no unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task activation map or within-group/main-effect for the healthy participants is reported. Therefore the study violates E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). The results also appear limited to ROI/SVC inferences rather than whole-brain results, meeting E2. Additionally, participant ages are not reported (cannot confirm they are adults 18–65), so I4 (age-specified healthy adult sample) and I5 (whole-brain healthy-group evidence) are not met. On balance, exclusion is warranted because the paper does not provide the required unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task activation maps.

The abstract reports investigation of self vs. others’ body-part processing and self-recognition, which falls under perception/understanding of self/others (social-related processing). The document reports healthy participant groups (n=11–12 across analyses) with no indication of clinical or out-of-range samples. NeuroStore indicates model fit over the whole brain and reports voxelwise group contrasts (e.g., body > objects) with reported peaks and voxel-level thresholds, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, group-level task-evoked maps. Thus the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), and I5 (whole-brain evidence). No exclusion criteria are met. Note: participant ages are not explicitly listed in the extraction, but the sample is presented as typical healthy adult participants; fulltext_incomplete set to false because the record is treated as the full-text representation.

The paper reports a task-based fMRI study of social judgments (allocentric social hierarchy and social alliance), in healthy adult participants (n=22, mean age 24.2, males only). Group-level, whole-brain (model fit over: whole brain) within-group contrasts are reported (e.g., social alliance > number equal; social hierarchy > fame/age/gender/number), with FWE thresholding and reported peak coordinates/tables. These satisfy inclusion criteria for (I3) social-related fMRI task, (I4) healthy adult sample, (I5) at least one group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map from the healthy group, and (I6) results reported as peaks/tables. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Therefore the study should be included in the review.

The study used task fMRI to investigate social evaluation (forming impressions), satisfying the social-task requirement. It reports analyses fit over the whole brain (Model fit over: whole brain) with reported peak coordinates for Social > Non-Social and Non-Social > Social contrasts and age-group comparisons; the abstract and NeuroStore entries describe within-group engagement for both age groups, indicating whole-brain, group-level task-evoked maps for healthy adult groups. The sample includes healthy young and older adult groups (healthy adults present). Thresholding and reported peaks meet the criterion that whole-brain results are reported (tables of peaks). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group without healthy-group map, or out-of-range ages) are met based on the provided document.

The study uses fMRI during a self-referential (social-related) task and includes a healthy younger adult group (mean ~23.4), satisfying I3 and I4. However, the NeuroStore record reports only between-group (OLD > YOUNG) whole-brain contrasts/interactions (multiple analyses) and does not present an unmasked, whole-brain task activation map or group-level contrast clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group alone. This matches exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts reported without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Therefore the study is excluded. Inclusion met: I3, I4. Inclusion not met: I5 (no whole-brain healthy-group task map reported). Full text is complete in the provided record.

The study uses task-based fMRI probing social semantic processing (semantic judgment of social vs animal-function concepts), includes a healthy adult sample (n=26, mean age 29.4 within 18–65), and reports multiple group-level, within-group whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., social > animal; positive > negative; animal > fixation) with peaks and a table of coordinates. Whole-brain inference is explicitly reported for several contrasts and results are presented in tables/peaks, satisfying the requirement that healthy-group whole-brain activation maps are reported. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study examines social-cognitive perspective-taking in healthy adults (meets I3 and I4), but the reported fMRI result is based on an analysis with inference restricted to a region-of-interest using small-volume correction (dmPFC SVC). Although the model was fit voxelwise over the whole brain, the paper reports only ROI-corrected inference (no unmasked, whole-brain group-level task-evoked statistical map is presented). Therefore it does not provide the required whole-brain healthy-group activation map (fails I5) and meets exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI results reported).

The study used fMRI during a social-related task (delayed match-to-sample with facial expressions requiring disambiguation of social cues). The sample is healthy adults (n=16, mean age 19.2), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts for the healthy group (multiple analyses with model fit and inference over the whole brain, with coordinates and peaks reported in tables). Thresholding and random-effects one-sample t-tests are described. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria are met.

The NeuroStore record shows an fMRI study of social dominance learning (social cognition/games) in healthy adults (n=28, ages 18–27), satisfying sample requirements. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked results: Analyses 28094034_analysis_0 and _2 explicitly state model fit and inference over the whole brain with FWE correction (cluster-level), indicating unmasked, voxelwise healthy-group effects. ROI analysis is present but whole-brain results are also reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state/ connectivity-only, not outside age range, not non-empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria relevant to this review are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and the study should be INCLUDED.

This fMRI study used a social-related task (control-of-trust/distrust with neutral faces) in a healthy adult sample (n=60; mean age 20.25). It reports multiple group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., Trust > Age, Distrust > Age, Trust > Distrust) with whole-brain inference and FWE correction, and activations are reported in tables of coordinates. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and participants are within the 18–65 range. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study investigates social approach/avoidance using face stimuli (social task) and reports analyses from healthy participants (n=36; subgroup n=20). Whole-brain group-level task contrasts are reported and inferred over the whole brain (e.g., Analyses 2, 3, 5–8 list whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference for the healthy sample), satisfying the requirement for at least one unmasked healthy-group whole-brain task activation map. Task content (approach-avoidance, stimulus rating of social faces) meets the social-processing construct. Although participant ages are not explicitly listed in the record, participants are described as healthy adults screened with the DSM-IV SCID, consistent with an adult sample. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports task-based fMRI of social cognition (intention inference) in healthy adult participants (n=18, ages 24–54), meeting the population requirement. Multiple group-level, within-subject whole-brain voxelwise analyses are listed (model fit over: whole brain; GLM parametric modulations and reported peaks/coordinates in MNI), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. The task is explicitly social-related (perception/understanding of others). The paper also reports connectivity analyses but not exclusively, so no exclusion criteria are met. Thus all required inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3, I4, I5, I6).

The study uses fMRI in a social task (monitoring others vs computer), and reports healthy adult participants (n=12, mean age 21) — satisfying inclusion criteria I3 and I4. However, all reported statistical inference was restricted to an ACC region-of-interest using small-volume correction (SVC); although the model was fit over the whole brain, no unmasked whole-brain, voxelwise healthy-group task activation map is reported. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only results with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criterion I5 (reporting at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise task map) is not met. Full text is available in the provided record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This fMRI study investigates recognition of others’ attitudes (vitality forms) from action sounds, a social-perception/social-communication task—meeting I3. Participants are healthy adults (n=15, mean age 23.3), meeting I4. The NeuroStore record shows whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference with group-level within-group contrasts (e.g., gentle>control, rude>control, vitality vs baseline) and reported peak coordinates/tables, satisfying I5 and I6. Results are not limited to ROIs or connectivity-only analyses, and the healthy-group whole-brain task effects are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text is available as the NeuroStore-derived record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study reports task-based fMRI of social-related processing (self/other processing in romantic interactions) in a healthy adult sample (n=37; ages 23–40). Multiple group-level, within-group whole-brain voxelwise contrasts are reported (e.g., positive>neutral, negative>neutral, positive>negative) with FWE thresholding and peak tables, and results are described in tables/coordinates. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task activations), and I6 (results reported via tables/coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply.

The study uses fMRI during a social cognition/game-theory task examining deception (meets I3). Participants are healthy adults (n=29; ages 21–32) satisfying the sample criterion (I4). The analyses report group-level, whole-brain (model fit over: whole brain) voxelwise second-level Bayesian GLM contrasts with reported peak coordinates and tables for within-group contrasts (simple deception > truth; sophisticated deception > truth, etc.), satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting and acceptable coordinate/table reporting (I5,I6). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not only between-group contrasts, and participants are within the 18–65 range. Full text appears complete for screening.

The study reports fMRI of interpersonal (social) touch vs impersonal touch, meeting the social-related task requirement (I3). Sample is healthy adults (n=30, mean age 40.5) within 18–65 (I4). Multiple group-level, whole-brain within-group task contrasts are reported with whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference (Analyses 0–7), fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement (I5); results are presented as reported peaks/tables, acceptable per I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, age within range, empirical data).

The study tests a social (imitation/observation) fMRI task (I3) and includes a healthy adult sample alongside schizophrenia patients (I4). However, the NeuroStore record does not report any whole-brain, group-level task activation maps that are clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group; reported within-group whole-brain maps are for patients only and the healthy-related results are reported only as between-group contrasts (healthy > patients) (Exclusion E4). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 (no unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect reported). Full text appears complete in this record.

This fMRI study examines self- and other-referential personality judgments (social cognition: perception/understanding of self and others) using task-based BOLD imaging in healthy adult participants (mean age 24.2, range 19.4–31). The NeuroStore record shows multiple group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., self>syllables, other>syllables, self>other) reported at voxel-level thresholds and coordinate tables, satisfying requirements for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for social-related fMRI in healthy adults, and no exclusion criteria apply (the presence of an ROI SVC analysis does not preclude inclusion because whole-brain results are reported).

The study reports an fMRI task involving social cognition (deciding which person is saddest using faces and contextual drawings), meeting I3. Participants are described as n=57 healthy participants, satisfying I4 (healthy adult group reported); ages are not explicitly listed but the document identifies a healthy participant group. The analyses report whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference (Model fit over: whole brain; Inference over: whole brain) with voxelwise results and reported peak coordinates/tables, satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not limited to ROIs, resting-state, or exclusively between-group contrasts, and the paper is empirical. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

The NeuroStore record indicates this is an fMRI study of face perception (a social-related task) with healthy adult controls, and reports whole-brain task results (tables of peaks). However, the extracted within-group whole-brain contrasts (EYES UP, MOUTH UP) are not explicitly labelled as coming from the healthy/control group in the document; the only contrasts clearly identified by group are between-group interactions (NT vs ASD). Because the record does not clearly present an unambiguous whole-brain, group-level task activation map identified as from the healthy/control group, the study fails inclusion criterion I5. This meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports between-group contrasts/interactions without a clearly identified healthy-group whole-brain task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related face-processing task), I4 (healthy adult participants reported), I6 (whole-brain results reported as coordinate tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clearly identified healthy-group whole-brain map).

The study uses fMRI during social-related tasks and includes a healthy adult control group (I3 and I4 are met). However, the NeuroStore record shows only between-group contrasts and interaction tests (controls vs. patients) and does not report an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group alone (e.g., a within-controls contrast or main effect). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. Exclusion criterion E4 (reporting only between-group contrasts/interactions without a whole-brain healthy-group task effect) applies, so the study is excluded.

This fMRI study tests social prediction (predicting others’ preferences), satisfying the social-related task requirement. Participants are healthy adults (n=22; mean age 24.68), meeting the sample criterion. The NeuroStore record reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (BLOCK3 > BLOCK1 and an interaction contrast) with whole-brain inference and reported peak coordinates (Analyses 0 and 1), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Connectivity analyses are present but do not preclude inclusion because whole-brain task-evoked maps are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met.

The study investigates social processing (facial emotion discrimination) and includes healthy adult participants, but it does not report an unmasked, within-group whole-brain task activation map for the healthy/control group. Reported whole-brain results are between-group contrasts (HS > patients and patients > HS) and patient within-group effects; no healthy-group main effect or within-group whole-brain map is provided. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (social-related fMRI task) and I4 (healthy adult group reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no whole-brain healthy-group task map reported).

The study uses task-based fMRI of face perception/recognition, which is a social-related construct (perception/understanding of others). The sample is healthy adults (n=17, ages 19–36) with no neurological/psychiatric history. The report includes at least one group-level, whole-brain, within-group task contrast (false alarms / false recognition) analyzed with RFX GLM and whole-brain inference and reported peaks (Talairach coordinates). Whole-brain results are explicitly reported (peaks/thresholding). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6, and no exclusion criteria apply. Confidence reflects small sample but clear reporting of whole-brain, within-group task activation in healthy adults.

This fMRI study examines social perception of in-/out-group members in healthy adults (meets I3 and I4). However, although the group-level model was estimated over the whole brain, all reported statistical inference was restricted to regions-of-interest (masked ROI and TPJ seed PPI), and reported peaks derive from ROI-restricted analyses. The paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain task-evoked group map or whole-brain voxelwise results for the healthy group. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI results reported). Inclusion criterion I5 (reported whole-brain group-level task map) is not met.

Exclusion based on lack of a healthy-group whole-brain task effect. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E4 (the paper reports only between-group/interactions comparing patients vs. controls; no unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task activation map is reported). (b) Inclusion criteria met: I3 (the task is social-related: implicit emotional face processing). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (although healthy participants are included, results for the healthy group are not reported separately), I5 (no group-level whole-brain healthy/control task-evoked map is reported), I6 (not applicable because healthy-group whole-brain results are absent). Therefore the study must be excluded.

The study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI of social perception (affective body perception; I3), reports a healthy adult sample (n=21, mean age 22; I4), and presents multiple group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts with whole-brain inference reported (Model fit over: whole brain; Inference over: whole brain; thresholding and tables of peaks are provided; I5). Results are also reported as tables of coordinates/peaks, consistent with acceptable reporting formats (I6). Although some ROI analyses are present, they do not replace the whole-brain results, so no exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the paper is eligible for inclusion.

The study reports task-based fMRI of social cognition (perception/understanding of others; mentalizing) using pictures of actions—matching the review’s social processing scope. Participants are healthy adults (n=20; ages 18.0–27.0), meeting the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise within-group contrasts (Unusual Intention > Normal; Unusual Means > Normal) with reported peak coordinates and whole-brain inference, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Results are presented as coordinate tables (Table 1), which is acceptable. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not restricted to between-group contrasts, ages are within 18–65, and the paper is empirical. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of social-related processing (self vs close other; role/trait/group judgments) satisfying the review focus. Participants are healthy adults (n=38; ages 18–31), meeting the sample criterion. The paper reports multiple group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and parametric modulations with whole-brain inference and coordinate peak tables (several analyses report model fit and inference over the whole brain and peak tables), fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements. Results are reported as thresholded maps/coordinate tables. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, ages within range).

The study used task-based fMRI during an emotion categorization task of facial expressions (social perception/understanding of others), included healthy adult participants (n=10, mean age 25.3), and reports a group-level, whole-brain multivariate analysis (model fit over whole brain with reported peak coordinates). These satisfy inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears sufficiently represented in the NeuroStore record.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing: participants made social judgments (age estimations and individuating food-preference judgments) while BOLD was measured, satisfying I3. The sample are healthy adults (n=18, mean age 20), satisfying I4. The paper reports multiple group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (Model fit over: whole brain for several contrasts; Talairach coordinates and reported peaks), satisfying I5. Whole-brain results are reported as coordinates/peaks, which is acceptable per I6. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

The study reports an fMRI social-communication task (integration of verbal and nonverbal emotional cues), meeting I3. Sample is 20 healthy adults (mean age 24.7), meeting I4. The NeuroStore record reports at least one group-level, whole-brain, within-group task-evoked statistical map (Analysis 22516367_analysis_0: TASK > REST; inference conducted over the whole brain with cluster-level correction), satisfying I5. Results/peaks are reported in tables, which satisfies I6. No exclusion criteria apply: the paper does not report only ROI analyses (it includes whole-brain results), nor is it connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

The study reports task-based fMRI of social perception (imitation-inhibition observing human vs robot agents), satisfying I3. Participants are healthy adults (n=23, mean age 26.4), satisfying I4. NeuroStore extraction indicates model fit and inference were performed over the whole brain and group-level within-subject contrasts are reported (peak coordinates in Table rstb20150075tb1), satisfying I5 and acceptable reporting per I6. The reported contrasts are within-group whole-brain task-evoked activation maps (robot>human, motion-capture>computer-animation, interaction contrasts), and no exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, ages in range, and empirical fMRI data present). Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria for this review.

This study investigates voice-identity perception (a social-perception task), and reports data from healthy participants, but it does not report a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map. The NeuroStore extract shows the primary analysis was fit and inferred within a region-of-interest (TVA); no clear whole-brain, voxelwise healthy-group task map is reported (Analysis 1 lacks detail). Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (social-related task). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (age range not specified in document), I5 (no whole-brain voxelwise task result reported). Exclusion criteria applied: E2. Full text is available in the record provided (fulltext_incomplete=false). Decision: EXCLUDED.

The study uses task fMRI of social perception (gender discrimination of emotional faces) in healthy adult participants (n=30), so it meets I3 and I4. However, all reported analyses are region-of-interest (ROI) based (model fit over: region of interest; inference restricted to ROIs such as bilateral amygdala and sgACC) and no group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for the healthy group is reported. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only study). Full text appears sufficiently available in the record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study used task-based fMRI addressing a social-related construct (self-face recognition — Perception and Understanding of Self), reporting group-level, whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise contrasts (e.g., self > familiar, familiar > unknown) with coordinate tables and thresholding. Participants are healthy adults (n=12; mean age 19.36, within 18–65). Whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps from the healthy group are clearly reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

The study reports task fMRI during a social interaction paradigm (Prisoner’s Dilemma; social cognition/games) with behavioral relevance to social/moral judgments, meeting I3. The sample is healthy adults (n=11, age mean 25.6, range 21–36), meeting I4. Multiple group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts are reported (one-sample random-effects t-tests across the 11 subjects; model fit over whole brain; voxelwise threshold p<0.001; peaks/tables reported), satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not resting-state or connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and participants are within 18–65. Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED.

This study is excluded because it does not provide a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map for the healthy sample (I5 not met). NeuroStore-extracted analyses indicate the main reported inference was region-of-interest restricted (Analysis 29105572_analysis_1: model fit over and inference restricted to ROI). Analysis 0 lacks feature detail and cannot be confirmed as a whole-brain map. Therefore the paper meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task—affective Theory of Mind False Belief task) and I4 (reports a healthy participant group). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no confirmed whole-brain healthy-group task map). Full text was available in the record; exclusion is based on reported analyses.

The study reports task-evoked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level activation maps from healthy adult participants performing an fMRI task involving perception of other people (erotic pictures and videos). Multiple within-group contrasts are reported (e.g., female > male pictures/videos) with whole-brain inference (FWE-corrected p < 0.05) and peak coordinates, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain evidence. Sample consists of healthy adult women (ages 25–50) with group-level results reported separately for heterosexual, bisexual, and homosexual groups. The task is labeled as an emotion task involving perception of other people, fitting the review’s social-related processing scope (perception/understanding of others). Therefore I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study uses fMRI during a social decision-making task (Trust Game) with a healthy adult sample, so I3 and I4 are satisfied. However, all reported whole-brain statistical results in the NeuroStore extract are between-group contrasts/interactions comparing high-Mach vs low-Mach subgroups (analyses labeled as interactions or between-group contrasts). There is no clear report of an unmasked, within-healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked map (i.e., no main effect or within-group whole-brain contrast for the healthy/control group). Therefore the study meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain healthy-group map) is not met. fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study reports an fMRI task that is clearly social (participants predicted another person’s choices), meeting the review’s social-related processing scope. Participants are described as healthy (n=36). Multiple group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task results are reported (model fit and inference over the whole brain with FWE cluster-level thresholding; coordinates reported in tables), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Results are presented for the healthy group and not restricted to an ROI or connectivity-only analysis. No exclusion criteria are met. Note: the document does not explicitly state participant ages, but the sample is described as healthy participants in an adult cognitive/neuroimaging study; confidence is slightly reduced for the missing explicit age-range reporting.

I3 met: study used fMRI of a social ToM (False Belief) task. I4 met: a healthy adult control group (NT) is reported separately. I5 not met: the paper does not report a whole-brain, within-group task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The whole-brain results in the NeuroStore record are interaction or between-group contrasts (diagnosis x sex; NT males > ASD males), while the within-group ToM effects are either ROI-restricted or reported for the patient/ASD group. Therefore the study reports only between-group/interactions for whole-brain inference without an unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect, which meets exclusion criterion E4. Full text is complete in the record. Exclusion IDs: E4. Inclusion IDs met: I3, I4. Inclusion IDs not met: I5.

The study reports fMRI during a collaborative communicative memory task (social communication/collaboration) with healthy adult participants (n=28, ages 18–33). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise random-effects analyses and within-group contrasts are reported (model fit and inference over whole brain; Monte Carlo cluster-thresholding; coordinate tables of peaks provided). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria for social-related task, healthy adult sample, whole-brain task-evoked group maps, and acceptable reporting format. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, empirical fMRI data present).

The study reports fMRI of social/linguistic stories in healthy adults (n=20, ages 19–31), satisfying inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task) and I4 (healthy adult sample). However, NeuroStore extraction shows model fitting and statistical inference were restricted to an a priori bilateral STS region-of-interest ("Model fit over: region of interest"; "Inference restricted to: region of interest"). No unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps are reported, so inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain evidence) is not met. This fulfills exclusion criterion E2 (studies reporting only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). fulltext_incomplete set to false.

Exclusion applied because the NeuroStore record reports only between-group interaction contrasts (drug-by-sex) as whole-brain results and does not present an unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task activation map. (a) Exclusion met: E4. (b) Inclusion met: I3 (fMRI during a social task — iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma), I4 (large sample of healthy adult men and women reported). (c) Inclusion not met: I5 (no clearly reported whole-brain, group-level task-evoked map from the healthy/control group is present in the extracted analyses). The record shows a whole-brain interaction analysis and MNI peak tables but no within-group or main-effect whole-brain activation map for the healthy group. Therefore the study must be excluded under E4.

The study uses fMRI during a clearly social task (Ultimatum Game) comparing meditators and controls. NeuroStore lists whole-brain, group-level task-evoked contrasts for healthy participants: within-group unfair>fair for meditators (n=26) and controls (n=40) with whole-brain inference and reported peak coordinates, satisfying the requirement for unmasked, voxelwise healthy-group maps. Participant samples are healthy adults (mean ages 40.4 and 36.8), meeting the age/sample criterion. Results are reported as coordinates/tables. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and within-group healthy-group whole-brain effects are reported). Therefore the paper satisfies inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis.

This study meets I3 (task: facial emotion recognition — social perception) and I4 (includes a healthy young adult group aged 20–31). However, it does not report any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps for the healthy group: all reported analyses are ROI-based or have inference restricted to ROIs (amygdala, mPFC, dmPFC, vmPFC), and no clear whole-brain voxelwise results are provided. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only results). Inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain evidence) is not met. Full text appears complete for screening.

The study reports a task-based fMRI experiment using a face-name paired-associates encoding task (social-related processing: perception/understanding of others and social communication). It includes a healthy control group of adults (n=18, mean age 39) within the 18–65 range and reports whole-brain, group-level within-group contrasts for the control group (Novel > Fixation and Fixation > Novel) with whole-brain inference and reported peaks. Thus it meets inclusion criteria for task type, sample, and presence of whole-brain healthy-group task activation maps. No exclusion criteria are met.

Study reports task-based fMRI of social processing (approach-avoidance to facial emotions), with healthy adult participants (n=23; ages 18–29). Multiple reported group-level, whole-brain, within-group contrasts (Main effect of emotion; Main effect of direction; Direction × Emotion) specify model fit and inference over the whole brain (voxelwise) with FDR thresholding and reported peak coordinates/tables. Thus the study meets all required inclusion criteria for whole-brain task-evoked activation in healthy adults.

This fMRI study examines neural correlates of regulating facial expressions of pain, a form of social communication, and explicitly frames facial expression as relevant to social interactions. Participants are healthy adults (n=34; ages 18–30). The NeuroStore record documents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., Pain > Warm within-subject contrasts with whole-brain FWE-corrected inference and reported peak coordinates in tables), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Results are reported as coordinate tables and described in the text/analyses. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study should be excluded because it does not meet the sample age criterion (I4). Although it uses fMRI during a social task (RMET) satisfying I3, and it reports a whole-brain, group-level within-group contrast (mind > age) in healthy participants satisfying I5 (and the reporting format is acceptable, I6), the healthy participant group falls outside the review's required age range. Reported ages: mean 68.4 (SD 8.54), range 51.0–84.0 — the group includes participants >65 and no separate healthy adult subgroup restricted to 18–65 is reported. Therefore I4 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are directly triggered beyond failing I4. Full text is complete for screening.

The study uses fMRI during a social task (trust game) so I3 is satisfied. However, the NeuroStore record shows only ROI-based between-group analyses (model fit and inference restricted to ROI) and reports peaks from ROI results; no unmasked whole-brain, group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group is reported. Therefore the report meets exclusion criteria E2 (ROI-only, no whole-brain results) and E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not met (no clearly reported healthy-group whole-brain results; healthy-group results are not presented separately as whole-brain maps). Full text appears complete in the record. Excluding on this basis.

The study uses task-based fMRI examining recognition of visual feedback as self vs other (social-related construct: perception/understanding of self and others), includes a healthy adult sample (n=15, ages 20–28), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (one-sample t-tests, model fit over whole brain, reported peaks in table). Whole-brain results are presented (coordinate peaks), satisfying the allowance for tables/figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and it is empirical fMRI data). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

Excluded because the paper does not report an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group. Exclusion criterion met: E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task — facial emotion processing) and I4 (includes a healthy adult group reported separately). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (no whole-brain, voxelwise healthy-group task-evoked map identified in the document). The NeuroStore record shows whole-brain analyses only for between-group contrasts and ROI-based within-group correlations, but no unambiguous whole-brain healthy-group activation map; therefore the study must be excluded.

The study reports task-based fMRI during a social gaze perception/joint-attention task (meets I3). The sample is healthy adults (n=18; ages 18–30), meeting I4. The reported analyses include whole-brain voxelwise group-level results: model fit and inference over the whole brain with FDR correction and tables of peak coordinates, satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not between-group-only, and participant ages are within 18–65).

The study is excluded because it does not report an unmasked, whole‑brain group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group; all reported significant results are ROI-restricted (FWE small-volume correction) and are from between-group contrasts/interactions or ROI regressions. Exclusion criteria met: E2 (results effectively ROI-only; no whole‑brain significant results reported) and E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying unmasked whole‑brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses fMRI during a social-related approach–avoidance task). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (age range 18–65 not explicitly reported for the sample in the document) and I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map identified as coming from the healthy group). Full text appears available, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The task is passive viewing of isolated sexual (genital) images to probe sexual preference/reward. Stimuli intentionally lacked faces, gestures, or social-context information and the reported analyses focus on reward/motor responses to preferred vs non-preferred sexual stimuli. This does not assess social-related processing constructs (e.g., affiliation, social communication, perception/understanding of self or others) as defined by the review. The study does include healthy adult participants and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps (tables of coordinates), but it fails Inclusion Criterion I3 (social-related task). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Therefore excluded.

This fMRI study investigates observation of others' actions (social perception), using an action-observation task—meeting I3. The sample is 29 healthy adults (ages 18–28), satisfying I4. The paper reports a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrast (2H DIFF > 2H SAME) with model fit and inference over the whole brain and FWE cluster/peak thresholding, and peak coordinates in a table, satisfying I5 (and I6 by acceptable reporting). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within 18–65, and empirical fMRI data present). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study reports an fMRI facial emotion recognition/social decision-making task (social-related processing) in a healthy adult sample (n=47, ages 18–33). Group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses are reported (multiple contrasts with inference over whole brain and FWE-corrected voxel-level thresholds) with peaks listed in tables, satisfying the requirement that whole-brain results are available. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not limited to ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, nor is the sample outside 18–65, and this is empirical fMRI data. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and the study should be INCLUDED.

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adults (n=22, ages 22–32) examining processing of action vs. abstract verbs and reports whole-brain, group-level contrasts (e.g., Human Action > Silence; Robotic Action > Silence; Action > Abstract) with voxel- and cluster-level FWE thresholds and coordinate tables. The task targets motor resonance/action understanding (mirror neuron system; affordance processing), which falls under social-related constructs (Perception and Understanding of Others / Social Communication). All inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3,I4,I5,I6). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range age, or non-empirical paper).

This study meets the review objectives and all inclusion criteria: (I3) It uses task-based fMRI during a social-relevant gaze perception / joint attention task. (I4) A healthy control group is reported separately (TD group, n=14, mean age 24.2, within the 18–65 adult range overall despite one minimum age of 16.1). (I5) The paper reports a whole-brain, group-level within-group contrast for the healthy/control group (Direct > Averted; model fit over whole brain; reported peaks in Table t2). (I6) Results are reported as peaks/coordinates in a table, which is acceptable. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and includes healthy adults). Therefore include.

The study reports task-based fMRI of social cue (gaze) processing during a decision-making/learning task, with healthy adult participants (n=50; ages 18–48). NeuroStore extraction documents voxel-wise, whole-brain group-level analyses (one-sample t-tests and cross-subject regressions) with reported peak coordinates and whole-brain inference (FWE cluster-level; uncorrected p<0.001), satisfying requirements for whole-brain healthy-group task activation maps. Therefore inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise results), and I6 (coordinate/table reporting acceptable) are met. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages only, or non-empirical) apply.

This study does include healthy adult participants (I4 satisfied) but does not clearly meet the social-related task requirement nor provide an unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task activation map. The task is an affective picture viewing paradigm (IAPS) focused on emotional responsivity; while some stimuli depict people (e.g., erotic images), the paradigm appears targeted at emotion processing rather than explicit social cognition constructs (Affiliation, Social Communication, Perception of Others), so I3 is not clearly satisfied. NeuroStore extractions show mainly between-group contrasts and group x gender interactions (patient vs control, interactions) and control gender comparisons; I do not find a clearly identified whole-brain, within-healthy-group task effect (e.g., NC: erotic > neutral) reported as an unmasked healthy-group map. Thus exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying healthy-group whole-brain task effect) applies. Inclusion criteria met: I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I3, I5. Exclusion criteria met: E4.

The study uses fMRI during a social trust game (social processing), includes healthy adult participants (n=18, mean age 23.06), and reports multiple group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (see Analyses 4,5,6,7,8,9,10,11 with whole-brain model fit and inference and tables of reported peaks). Thus it meets I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level results), and I6 (results reported as coordinate peaks/tables). It is not ROI-only and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears sufficiently represented in the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study used task-based fMRI of face perception (faces vs scrambled), which maps onto social-related processing (Perception and Understanding of Others). Participants are healthy adults (n=20, ages 21–30). The NeuroStore record reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation contrasts (Faces>scrambled and hemifield effects) with FWE-corrected voxelwise inference and reported peak coordinates. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain, group-level task-evoked maps), and I6 (results reported as coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, and empirical data present).

The study reports an fMRI social interactive task in healthy adults (I3, I4 satisfied). However, although the GLM was fit over the whole brain, all reported inferences were restricted to regions of interest using small-volume correction (SVC) and no unmasked whole-brain task-evoked group results are reported. This means it only presents ROI-restricted results (no whole-brain group-level activation map), so it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E2.

Excluded because exclusion criterion E2 is met: the report indicates model estimates were computed over the whole brain but statistical inference was restricted to a region-of-interest using small-volume correction, and reported peaks appear ROI-restricted. Therefore the paper does not provide an unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task activation map (inclusion criterion I5 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social False Belief task addressing understanding of others) and I4 (healthy adult sample, n=15, ages 18–30). Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Full text appears available from the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants performing a social joint-action task (virtual cooperative bar-balancing), meeting the review’s focus on social-related processing. Sample: n=20 healthy adults aged 18–27 (meets age and healthy-group requirement). Whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (model fit over: whole brain) and group-level contrasts (Isomorphic>solo, Non-isomorphic>solo, Non-isomorphic>iso, etc.) are reported with peak coordinates/tables, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Results are clearly for the healthy group and not restricted to an ROI or connectivity-only analysis. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the paper satisfies all inclusion criteria and should be included.

The study uses task-based fMRI of social-related processing (pictures depicting one vs two persons; instructions to take another’s perspective), includes healthy adult participants aged within 18–65 (male participants, ages reported 19–39), and reports multiple group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts from the healthy group (e.g., Social>single and Negative>neutral within-group contrasts with whole-brain inference reported). Whole-brain results are reported in tables of peaks. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6, and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only; not only connectivity; within-group whole-brain maps are present).

The study investigates verbal irony comprehension, a social-communication/Theory-of-Mind task (meets I3). Sample consists of healthy adults (n=20, mean age 22) meeting the 18–65 requirement (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (Ironic > Literal) with whole-brain inference and reported coordinate peaks (Talairach), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5) and acceptable reporting formats (I6). PPI connectivity analyses are present but do not preclude the reported whole-brain activation maps. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: I3 - uses task-based fMRI with social-related stimuli (IAPS erotic and fearful social scenes; emotional face matching task); I4 - sample comprises 55 healthy adult men (mean age 24.9) reported separately; I5 - reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (Analyses 3–6: erotic>neutral, fearful>neutral, erotic>fearful, fearful>erotic) with whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference and reported peaks; I6 - whole-brain results are clearly described in the extracted analyses. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy adults within 18–65, is empirical fMRI data).

This fMRI study investigates self-evaluation (Perception/Understanding of Self) using musically induced mood, which is a social-related construct. Participants: 20 healthy adults (age range 21–42) within the 18–65 inclusion window. NeuroStore metadata indicate whole-brain voxelwise GLM analyses (model fit over whole brain; inference over whole brain) with reported group-level contrasts (e.g., SELF>LEX) and tables of peak coordinates, meeting the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group task activation maps. Results are reported for the healthy cohort and not limited to a subgroup. No exclusion criteria (ROIs-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI of facial emotion perception (a social-perception/communication task), includes a healthy adult sample (n=25, mean age 25.9), and reports multiple group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps/contrasts (several analyses list inference over whole brain and report peaks/tables). Results are reported as whole-brain contrasts with cluster/FDR thresholds and coordinate tables for peaks. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants are within 18–65, and the paper is empirical).

This fMRI study examines communicative (social) vs non-social gestures during observation and imitation, directly addressing social-related processing (I3). Participants are healthy adults (n=20, mean age 24.6), meeting the sample criterion (I4). The paper reports multiple group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts and cluster-corrected inference (model fit and inference over whole brain; reported peak tables), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5,I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, empirical fMRI data present).

The study reports task-based fMRI during a social-cognition task (viewing emotional social clips with identification vs attribution goals), meeting I3. The sample is healthy adults (n=22, ages 19–32), meeting I4. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (one-sample t-tests, whole-brain inference; contrasts How>Why and Why>How; coordinate tables), meeting I5 and I6. Although a PPI connectivity analysis is also reported, whole-brain task activation maps from the healthy group are clearly presented. No exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports task-based fMRI during social cognition (observing animated social encounters), in a healthy adult sample (n=20; ages 18–29). It includes at least one group-level, whole-brain within-group contrast (analysis 29354042_analysis_0: avoidance > approach; model fit over: whole brain) with reported peak coordinates and cluster-level inference, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked results. Thresholding and coordinate space are provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met, and no exclusion criteria apply.

Study used task-based fMRI measuring social-cognitive responses (mental state attribution) to sexualized and clothed targets, satisfying the social-related task requirement. Participants are healthy adults (n=21, mean age 21.05), meeting the sample criterion. NeuroStore reports model fit over whole brain and inference over whole brain for group-level contrasts (e.g., sexualized female > others) with reported coordinate tables and cluster-thresholding, providing whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results from the healthy group. Results are reported as peaks/tables and are clearly group-level. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without healthy-group maps, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6) and no exclusion criteria apply.

Meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) uses task-based fMRI of social processing (perceptual judgment of faces / eye-region threat cues); (I4) reports healthy adult participants (mean age ~23.9, within 18–65); (I5) reports at least one group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task contrast from the healthy/placebo group (Analysis 3: Fearful > Happy, model fit and inference over whole brain, p<0.001 cluster extent 10); (I6) whole-brain results are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria are met (there are whole-brain within-group maps, not ROI-only or connectivity-only, and healthy-group effects are reported). Full text is available via the NeuroStore-derived record. Therefore include.

The study is excluded because it does not provide the required healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked activation map and reports only connectivity-based, between-group contrasts.
