Specifically: Exclusion criteria met: E3 (reports only seed-based/ROI connectivity analyses without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map) and E4 (reports between-group contrasts only, without an unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (the paper targets self-referential processing, which falls under “Perception and Understanding of Self”). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (insufficient information to confirm a healthy adult group within the 18–65 age range — participants are described as older adults with aMCI and controls but ages are not reported in the document), and I5 (no group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group is reported; analyses are between-group connectivity contrasts and ROI/seed-based). Therefore the paper does not meet all required inclusion criteria for the review.

This fMRI study investigates social-related processing (linking person perception and person knowledge) using an event-related task involving bodies, names, and trait vs neutral statements (meets I3). Participants are healthy adults (n=21, mean age 24.6) and results are reported for the healthy group (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked univariate contrasts (main effects of Social Agent and Social Knowledge, and their interaction) with reported peak coordinates/tables (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria are triggered: whole-brain results are present (so E2 and E3 do not apply), results are within a healthy adult group (E4/E5 not met), and this is an empirical fMRI study (E6 not met).

The study uses fMRI during a social-related self/other-reflection task and includes a healthy adult group, but all reported whole-brain results are between-group interaction/contrast maps (patients vs controls). No unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group (e.g., within-group main effect or control>baseline map) is reported. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts reported). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (social-related fMRI task) and I4 (healthy adult participants reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no whole-brain healthy-group task map reported).

The paper reports original fMRI experiments and coordinate-based meta-analyses using healthy adult participants performing social-related face-processing tasks (dynamic facial expressions). Experiments 1–3 provide group-level, whole-brain, within-group task contrasts (model fit and inference over whole brain; cluster-corrected thresholds) for healthy adults (n=24, n=15, n=15; mean ages within 18–65). The ALE meta-analyses also report whole-brain coordinate results. Thus the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3: social-related fMRI task; I4: healthy adult samples reported separately; I5: whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps reported; I6: whole-brain results reported as coordinates/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, ages within range, empirical data present).

This fMRI study examines social cognition (predicting others’ behavior re: rules vs desires) in healthy adults (n=18, ages 18–44). The NeuroStore record reports multiple group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (e.g., PORTRAIT and FEEDBACK general effects; main effects of SCENARIO; contrasts desires>rules and rules>desires) with tables of peaks and cluster-/voxel-level inference, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Reporting includes coordinate tables (Tables tbl2/tbl3). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

The study reports task-based fMRI of social cognition (self vs other recollection), meeting the review’s I3 criterion. The sample is healthy adults (n=18, ages 19–29), meeting I4. Multiple analyses report group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (Analyses 24700584_analysis_1, _2, and _3: model fit over whole brain and inference over whole brain with FWE voxel-level thresholding), satisfying I5; reporting is via tables/peaks which meets I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, empirical fMRI data present). Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED.

(a) Exclusion met: E4. The paper reports only between-group contrasts and group-comparison multivariate decoding (e.g., Blind > Sighted; interactions; group-difference searchlights) and does not present an unmasked, whole-brain task activation map clearly attributed to the healthy/sighted group alone. (b) Inclusion met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task: voice-based identity and emotion recognition—perception of others) and I4 (contains a healthy adult sighted control group). (c) Inclusion not met: I5 (no group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map reported for the healthy/control group). Therefore the study must be excluded under E4. The NeuroStore record appears complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study investigates social emotions using fMRI in healthy adults (I3 and I4 satisfied). However, all reported analyses in the NeuroStore record are Granger causal connectivity (seed-based) maps from the left hippocampus (connectivity measure, GCM model, seed-based), and the paper does not report a group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map (voxelwise task activation) for the healthy group. Thus it meets exclusion E3 (only seed-based/effective connectivity reported without a whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain task-evoked statistical activation map clearly reported) and consequently I6 (format of whole-brain task results) is not applicable/ not met. Decision: EXCLUDED for E3.

The study reports task-based fMRI of a social processing task (facial emotion recognition) with healthy adult participants (n=20, mean age 20.65), and presents whole-brain, group-level analyses (whole-brain PLS with reported peak coordinates and tables) including within-group contrasts. Results are reported as tables of peaks and connectivity tables. Although one participant is 17, the sample is predominantly adult and group-level healthy adult results are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study meets I3 (uses fMRI during a social-related task: production/observation of communicative pointing) and I4 (healthy adult sample, n=16, ages 19–32). However it does NOT meet I5 (no group-level whole-brain/voxelwise task-evoked results reported): NeuroStore extraction shows all analyses were fit over regions of interest with region-level thresholding (ROI-only results). Therefore exclusion criterion E2 (reports only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) applies. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Because I5 is unmet and E2 is triggered, the study must be excluded.

The study reports task-based fMRI during a social Trust Game (meets I3). Sample includes n=38 healthy participants (adults) reported separately (meets I4). The paper provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (Fair>Control and Unfair>Control modeled over the whole brain with reported peak coordinates and tables), satisfying whole-brain evidence (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and include unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effects rather than only between-group contrasts. Therefore the study should be included.

The study uses task fMRI of an empathy-for-pain paradigm (socially relevant processing: perception/understanding of others) in a healthy adult sample (n=15, mean age 25.3). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (Pain>Neutral across targets and separately for People, Animals, Nature) with thresholding and reported peak coordinates. Thus it meets all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and does not meet any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper).

The study uses an appropriate social fMRI task (Cyberball) and includes a healthy adult control group, but the NeuroStore record reports only between-group/interaction contrasts and patient-only contrasts. No group-level, whole-brain task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group (e.g., a within-group healthy > passive or main effect map) is reported in the extracted analyses. Specifically: Analysis 30559687_analysis_1 is a patient-group interaction (BPD patients > MD patients, n=31 patients), and Analysis 30559687_analysis_0 is an omnibus between-group contrast. Therefore the paper lacks an unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect, meeting exclusion criterion E4.

Excluded: The study reports fMRI of social-related processing (maternal response to child affect) and provides whole-brain coordinate tables, but the sample consists solely of clinically depressed mothers (n=19) with no healthy adult/control group reported. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (social-related task), I6 (whole-brain results reported in coordinate tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no healthy adult group 18–65 reported separately), I5 (no whole-brain group-level task map from a healthy/control group). No exclusion criteria from the provided list directly apply. Therefore the article is excluded for failure to meet I4 and I5.

Analysis 27109357_analysis_8 reports task-based fMRI (Prisoner’s Dilemma) measuring BOLD responses with a group-level contrast (ment > cont) in healthy adult participants (n=163). The model was fit over the whole brain and inference was performed over the whole brain, with reported peak coordinates (reported peaks: 4). Thus the study provides a whole-brain, voxelwise, task-evoked statistical map for healthy adults, addressing social processing. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study examines face recognition (a social-related task; I3 met) and includes healthy adult participants alongside autism patients (I4 met). However, all reported analyses are seed-based task functional connectivity and between-group contrasts (FFA seed), with several ROI-restricted inferences; no group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation map for the healthy/control group is reported. Therefore it fails I5 and meets exclusion criteria E3 (only seed-based connectivity reported without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map) and E4 (reporting mainly between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect).

The study reports an fMRI task of face individuation, which fits the social-related construct ‘Perception and Understanding of Others’ (I3). The sample is healthy adults (n=15, mean age 24.8) satisfying the age and healthy-group requirement (I4). The NeuroStore record contains multiple group-level, whole-brain within-group task contrasts (e.g., faces>watches, objects>faces) with voxelwise inference and reported coordinates, fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement (I5); these results are presented with cluster correction and coordinate tables/peaks (I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, and empirical fMRI data present). Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This study examines social processing (facial emotion recognition) and includes a healthy adult control group (I3 and I4 met). However, NeuroStore shows only a seed-based effective connectivity (PPI) analysis and a between-group interaction (controls vs patients) reported; no unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked activation map is reported. Therefore it violates exclusion criteria E3 (only seed/effective connectivity reported without a healthy-group task activation map) and E4 (only between-group contrast/interaction reported without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group effect). Inclusion criterion I5 (healthy-group whole-brain task map) is not met. Full text is adequately represented in the provided document (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study meets I3 (fMRI during a social-related task: fearful face perception) and I4 (reports a separate healthy adult group, n=13, age within 18–65). However, although the model was fit over the whole brain, all statistical inference reported is restricted to predefined ROIs using small-volume correction (ROI-restricted inference); no unmasked, whole-brain group-level voxelwise activation map for the healthy/control group is reported. Therefore it fails I5 (no whole-brain healthy-group task map) and meets exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Accordingly, the study is excluded.

Excluded because the paper reports only between-group contrasts/interactions and does not present an unmasked whole-brain, within-group task activation map for the healthy/control group. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E4. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task: Reading the Mind in the Eyes) and I4 (study includes healthy adult participants reported separately). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain, group-level healthy/control task activation map is reported; reported analyses are between-group contrasts and an interaction). Full text available from NeuroStore record; exclusion based on reported analyses.

The study reports task-based fMRI during an explicit social cognition task (emotional perspective taking) in a healthy adult sample (n=50, mean age 20.14). NeuroStore extraction indicates whole-brain voxelwise model fitting and whole-brain regression analyses (warm-altruistic composite scores modulating the emotion perspective taking > match shapes contrast) with reported peak coordinates. Results are within-group/cross-subject regressions clearly from the healthy sample. Thus it satisfies: I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult participants), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analysis reported), and I6 (results reported as peaks/coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, age within range, empirical fMRI data present). Full text appears sufficiently represented by the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. I3: The fMRI task includes recognition of hand postures, explicitly testing communicative (social) postures (e.g., thumbs up), which falls under Social Communication/Perception of Others. I4: Participants are healthy adults (n=21, mean age 24.0), within 18–65. I5: Group-level whole-brain (searchlight) multivariate analyses were performed and reported with MNI peak coordinates (reported peaks = 2 for each contrast), indicating whole-brain voxelwise results for the healthy group. I6: Results are reported as coordinates/peaks in standard space, which is acceptable. No exclusion criteria are met: this is not ROI-only (E2), not connectivity-only (E3), not only between-group contrasts (E4), includes appropriate ages (E5), and is empirical fMRI data (E6). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study reports task-based fMRI of social cognition (semantic judgments about psychological states vs body parts for people/dogs), satisfying the social-related task requirement. Participants are healthy adults (n=19, ages 19–24), satisfying the sample criterion. Analyses were fit over the whole brain and include within-group, voxelwise contrasts with thresholding and reported peak coordinates (Table), satisfying the whole-brain evidence and reporting requirements.
